path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 156. Information as to buildings not conforming to act; hearing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 156. Information as to buildings not conforming to act; hearing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 156. Information as to buildings not conforming to act; hearing (2023)
content:
If at any time any governing body or other authority of any locality may know of any
   reason why a magazine or building in which explosives are used or kept is not or cannot
   be conducted in accordance with the provisions of this act, and should not be permitted
   to operate, upon notifying the Secretary of Labor and Industry, in writing, or his
   duly authorized representative, a hearing may be conducted by the said Secretary of
   Labor and Industry or his duly authorized representative, to show cause why a license
   should not be issued or should not be revoked.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 151. Explosives; makers and dealers of subject to act; exceptions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 151. Explosives; makers and dealers of subject to act; exceptions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 151. Explosives; makers and dealers of subject to act; exceptions (2023)
content:
No person shall manufacture, process, store, or have in his possession any explosives
   in this Commonwealth, until all requirements of this act have been complied with:
   Provided, That nothing contained in this act shall be construed to apply to the storage
   and actual use of explosives in or in connection with anthracite and bituminous coal
   mines and coal mining operations, or clay or shale mining operations, or in the operation
   of stone or rock quarries, or in agricultural work, or to the military and naval forces
   of the United States, or to the transportation of explosives upon vessels or railroad
   cars when in conformity with the rules of the Interstate Commerce Commission.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 159. Licenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 159. Licenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 159. Licenses (2023)
content:
After January first, one thousand nine hundred and thirty-eight, every person storing
   or in possession of explosives shall be required to have a license for each magazine
   used for the storing or placing of explosives, which license shall be issued on a
   form prepared and furnished by the Department of Labor and Industry.  The application for license shall be accompanied by the proper license fee, which
   shall be prescribed by the department, according to the quantity of explosives which
   are to be stored or placed in the magazine, and shall not be less than three dollars
   and fifty cents ($3.50) nor more than fifty dollars ($50).  Such license shall be kept posted conspicuously in or about the magazine for which
   issued.  Licenses shall expire annually on the thirty-first day of December, and shall be
   renewed annually upon payment of the fee as specified in this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 160. Records of manufacturers, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 160. Records of manufacturers, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 160. Records of manufacturers, etc. (2023)
content:
Every person, company, or corporation manufacturing, storing, selling, transferring,
   dealing in, or in any manner disposing of any explosives, shall keep, in a book for
   that purpose, an accurate record of all transactions with the date thereof relating
   to the receiving and disposing of the same, which record shall show the amount of
   each such explosive received, by whom transported or conveyed, and each and every
   sale or other disposition made of such explosives with the amount thereof, and the
   name of the person to whom delivery of the same was made, who shall be required to
   receipt therefor.  Such record shall at all times be open to the inspection of any duly authorized
   representative of the Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 160.2. Storage of black powder in commercial establishment; penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 160.2. Storage of black powder in commercial establishment; penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 160.2. Storage of black powder in commercial establishment; penalty (2023)
content:
(a) No person shall store more than fifty pounds of black powder in a commercial establishment.  It shall be unlawful to store black powder in a commercial establishment unless
      a license to store explosives is obtained from the United States Department of Treasury,
      Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms.  Black powder shall be stored in accordance with27 C.F.R. § 181.90in a type 4 storage facility which shall be mounted on wheels for easy removal in
      case of fire.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 160.1. Possession and storage of powder
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 160.1. Possession and storage of powder
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 160.1. Possession and storage of powder (2023)
content:
(a) Possession and storage of commercially manufactured black powder (in quantities
      not to exceed ten pounds), percussion caps, safety and pyrotechnic fuses, matches
      and friction primers, intended to be used solely for sporting, recreational, cultural
      purposes in antique firearms or antique devices as defined in§ 921(a)(16) of Title 18 of the United States Codeshall be exempt from regulation by the Department of Environmental Resources.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 157. Regulations as to safety
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 157. Regulations as to safety
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 157. Regulations as to safety (2023)
content:
All explosive plants and all buildings and magazines wherein explosives are manufactured
   or stored shall be located, operated, maintained, equipped, and conducted so as to
   provide for the adequate protection for all persons employed in or about such explosive
   plants or magazines.  The location of explosive plants with respect to other buildings, railroads, and
   highways, and the location of buildings wherein explosives are manufactured or stored
   with respect to other magazines or buildings when explosives are manufactured shall
   be in accordance with the regulations adopted by the Department of Labor and Industry.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 164. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 164. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 164. Definitions (2023)
content: As used in this act--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 163. Fees to be paid into State Treasury
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 163. Fees to be paid into State Treasury
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 163. Fees to be paid into State Treasury (2023)
content:
All fees collected under the provisions of this act shall be paid into the State Treasury,
   through the Department of Revenue.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 161. Rules and regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 161. Rules and regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 161. Rules and regulations (2023)
content:
For the purpose of carrying out the provisions of this act and applying these provisions
   to specific cases, the Department of Labor and Industry shall have the power, and
   its duties shall be, to make, alter, amend, or repeal general rules and regulations
   to provide protection in the manufacture, processing, transportation, storage, use,
   or handling of explosives.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 153. Reports of manufacturers to Department of Labor and Industry
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 153. Reports of manufacturers to Department of Labor and Industry
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 153. Reports of manufacturers to Department of Labor and Industry (2023)
content:
All persons engaged in the manufacture of explosives, or any process involving explosives,
   or where explosives are used as a component part in the manufacture of any article
   or device on the date when this act takes effect, shall, within sixty days thereafter,
   and all persons engaging in the manufacture of explosives, or any process involving
   explosives, or where explosives are used as a component part in the manufacture of
   any article or device after this act takes effect, shall, before so engaging, make
   a report in writing, subscribed to by such person or his agent, to the Department
   of Labor and Industry, the report stating--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 154. Reports concerning stored explosives
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 154. Reports concerning stored explosives
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 154. Reports concerning stored explosives (2023)
content:
All persons storing explosives or having explosives in their possession on the date
   when this act takes effect, shall, within sixty days thereafter, and all persons contemplating
   the storing of explosives or having same in their possession after this act takes
   effect, shall, before obtaining or storing such explosives, make a report in writing,
   subscribed to by such person or his agent, to the Department of Labor and Industry,
   the report stating--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 152. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 152. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 152. Definitions (2023)
content:
The term“explosives,”whenever used in this act, shall mean and include any chemical compound or other
   substance intended for the purpose of producing an explosion, or that contains oxidizing
   and combustible units or other ingredients in such proportions or quantities that
   ignition by fire, by friction, by concussion, by percussion, or by detonator, may
   produce an explosion capable of causing injury to persons, or damage to property.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 158. Plans of plants
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 158. Plans of plants
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 158. Plans of plants (2023)
content:
There shall be kept in the main office on the premises of every explosive plant a
   plan of said plant, showing the location of all buildings and the distance they are
   located from other buildings where persons are employed and from magazines, and these
   plans shall at all times be open to inspection by duly authorized inspectors of the
   Department of Labor and Industry.  The superintendent of each plant shall, upon demand of said inspector, furnish the
   following information:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 165. Examination and licensing of blasters; fees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 165. Examination and licensing of blasters; fees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 165. Examination and licensing of blasters; fees (2023)
content:
No person shall detonate explosives in any blasting operation unless he has passed
   an examination, prescribed by the Department of Labor and Industry, which shall test
   the examinee's skill and knowledge of the principles and practice of blasting operations
   and the storage, moving, handling and detonation of explosives.  Application for examination as a blaster shall be in writing upon a form furnished
   by the department and shall be accompanied by a fee of ten dollars ($10).  If the applicant is successful in passing the examination, a license indicating
   his competency to detonate explosives shall be issued upon the payment of an additional
   fee of five dollars ($5).  Anything hereinbefore to the contrary notwithstanding, the department shall issue
   a license without examination to any applicant who shall show to the department that
   he has, at the effective date hereof, had three years experience in the handling and
   use of explosives.  Each blaster shall be required to renew his license each year by application to
   the department, which application shall be accompanied by a fee of three dollars and
   fifty cents ($3.50).  The Secretary of Labor and Industry may suspend any license for due cause but no
   license may be revoked until the licensee has been granted a hearing.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 168. Penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 168. Penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 168. Penalties (2023)
content:
Any person violating any of the provisions of this act, or any of the rules or regulations
   of the Department of Labor and Industry made pursuant thereto, shall, upon conviction
   in a summary proceeding, be sentenced to pay a fine of not less than ten dollars ($10)
   nor more than one hundred dollars ($100), and upon failure to pay such fine and costs,
   shall undergo imprisonment for not more than thirty days.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 162. Penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 162. Penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 162. Penalties (2023)
content:
Any person or persons who shall violate any of the provisions of this act or the rules
   and regulations of the department as herein provided for, or who shall hinder or interfere
   with a duly authorized officer of the Commonwealth in the performance of his duties
   as herein provided, shall, upon conviction in a summary proceeding, be punished by
   a fine of not less than ten dollars ($10) or more than one hundred dollars ($100),
   and in default of the payment of such fine and costs shall be sentenced to imprisonment
   for not more than thirty days.  Any person or persons who shall, on second offense, violate any of the provisions
   of this act or the rules and regulations of the department as herein provided for,
   shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction, shall be sentenced to pay
   a fine of not less than one hundred dollars ($100) and not more than one thousand
   dollars ($1,000), or to suffer imprisonment for not more than one year, or both, at
   the discretion of the court.  Prosecution for violation of this act may be instituted by the Secretary of Labor
   and Industry or his duly authorized representative.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-1. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-1. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-1. Short title (2023)
content:
This act shall be known and may be cited as the “Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer
   Protection Law.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 155. Duties of department; cancellation of license
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 155. Duties of department; cancellation of license
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 155. Duties of department; cancellation of license (2023)
content:
The department shall determine the amount of explosives that may be stored or placed
   in magazines and shall issue a license to the person applying therefor, as hereinafter
   provided, such license to stipulate the maximum amount of explosives permitted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 166. Blasting operations conducted in accordance with regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 166. Blasting operations conducted in accordance with regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 166. Blasting operations conducted in accordance with regulations (2023)
content:
(a) The use of explosives for the purpose of blasting in the neighborhood of any public
      highway, stream of water, dwelling house, public building, school, church, commercial
      or institutional building, or pipe line, shall be done in accordance with the provisions
      of this section, and rules and regulations promulgated by the Department of Labor
      and Industry.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation›PA ST 73 P.S. § 167. Promulgation of rules and regulations authorized
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 3. Explosives, Regulation › PA ST 73 P.S. § 167. Promulgation of rules and regulations authorized
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 167. Promulgation of rules and regulations authorized (2023)
content:
The Department of Labor and Industry may promulgate additional rules or regulations
   it deems necessary not inconsistent with law to effectuate the provisions of this
   act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-9.2. Private actions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-9.2. Private actions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-9.2. Private actions (2023)
content:
(a) Any person who purchases or leases goods or services primarily for personal, family
      or household purposes and thereby suffers any ascertainable loss of money or property,
      real or personal, as a result of the use or employment by any person of a method,
      act or practice declared unlawful by section 31of this act, may bring a private action to recover actual damages or one hundred
      dollars ($100), whichever is greater.  The court may, in its discretion, award up to three times the actual damages sustained,
      but not less than one hundred dollars ($100), and may provide such additional relief
      as it deems necessary or proper.  The court may award to the plaintiff, in addition to other relief provided in this
      section, costs and reasonable attorney fees.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-2. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-2. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-2. Definitions (2023)
content: As used in this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-3.1. Regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-3.1. Regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-3.1. Regulations (2023)
content:
The Attorney General may adopt, after public hearing, such rules and regulations as
   may be necessary for the enforcement and administration of this act.  Such rules and regulations when promulgated pursuant to the act of July 31, 1968
   (P.L. 769, No. 240), known as the “Commonwealth Documents Law,”1shall have the force and effect of law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-4. Restraining prohibited acts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-4. Restraining prohibited acts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-4. Restraining prohibited acts (2023)
content:
Whenever the Attorney General or a District Attorney has reason to believe that any
   person is using or is about to use any method, act or practice declared by section
   3 of this act1to be unlawful, and that proceedings would be in the public interest, he may bring
   an action in the name of the Commonwealth against such person to restrain by temporary
   or permanent injunction the use of such method, act or practice.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-5. Assurances of voluntary compliance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-5. Assurances of voluntary compliance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-5. Assurances of voluntary compliance (2023)
content:
In the administration of this act, the Attorney General may accept an assurance of
   voluntary compliance with respect to any method, act or practice deemed to be violative
   of the act from any person who has engaged or was about to engage in such method,
   act or practice.  Such assurance may include a stipulation for voluntary payment by the alleged violator
   providing for the restitution by the alleged violator to consumers, of money, property
   or other things received from them in connection with a violation of this act.  Any such assurance shall be in writing and be filed with the court.  Such assurance of voluntary compliance shall not be considered an admission of violation
   for any purpose.  Matters thus closed may at any time be reopened by the Attorney General for further
   proceedings in the public interest, pursuant to section 4.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-7. Contracts; effect of rescission
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-7. Contracts; effect of rescission
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-7. Contracts; effect of rescission (2023)
content:
(a) Where goods or services having a sale price of twenty-five dollars ($25) or more
      are sold or contracted to be sold to a buyer, as a result of, or in connection with,
      a contact with or call on the buyer or resident at his residence either in person
      or by telephone, that consumer may avoid the contract or sale by notifying, in writing,
      the seller within three full business days following the day on which the contract
      or sale was made and by returning or holding available for return to the seller, in
      its original condition, any merchandise received under the contract or sale.  Such notice of rescission shall be effective upon depositing the same in the United
      States mail or upon other service which gives the seller notice of rescission.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-3. Unlawful acts or practices; exclusions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-3. Unlawful acts or practices; exclusions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-3. Unlawful acts or practices; exclusions (2023)
content:
(a) Unfair methods of competition and unfair or deceptive acts or practices in the
      conduct of any trade or commerce as defined by subclauses (i) through (xxi) of clause
      (4) of section 21of this act and regulations promulgated under section 3.12of this act are hereby declared unlawful.  The provisions of this act shall not apply to any owner, agent or employe of any
      radio or television station, or to any owner, publisher, printer, agent or employe
      of an Internet service provider or a newspaper or other publication, periodical or
      circular, who, in good faith and without knowledge of the falsity or deceptive character
      thereof, publishes, causes to be published or takes part in the publication of such
      advertisement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-4.1. Payment of costs and restitution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-4.1. Payment of costs and restitution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-4.1. Payment of costs and restitution (2023)
content:
Whenever any court issues a permanent injunction to restrain and prevent violations
   of this act as authorized in section 41above, the court may in its discretion direct that the defendant or defendants restore
   to any person in interest any moneys or property, real or personal, which may have
   been acquired by means of any violation of this act, under terms and conditions to
   be established by the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-9. Forfeiture of franchise or right to do business; appointment of receiver
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-9. Forfeiture of franchise or right to do business; appointment of receiver
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-9. Forfeiture of franchise or right to do business; appointment of receiver (2023)
content:
Upon petition by the Attorney General, the court having jurisdiction, may, in its
   discretion, order the dissolution, suspension or forfeiture of the franchise or right
   to do business of any person, firm or corporation which violates the terms of an injunction
   issued under section 4 of this act.1In addition, the court may appoint a receiver of the assets of the company.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-8. Civil penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-8. Civil penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-8. Civil penalties (2023)
content:
(a) Any person who violates the terms of an injunction issued under section 41of this act or any of the terms of an assurance of voluntary compliance duly filed
      in court under section 52of this act shall forfeit and pay to the Commonwealth a civil penalty of not more
      than five thousand dollars ($5,000) for each violation.  For the purposes of this section the court issuing an injunction or in which an
      assurance of voluntary compliance is filed shall retain jurisdiction, and the cause
      shall be continued;  and, in such cases, the Attorney General, or the appropriate
      District Attorney, acting in the name of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, may petition
      for recovery of civil penalties and any other equitable relief deemed needed or proper.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-9.1. Powers of receiver
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-9.1. Powers of receiver
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 201-9.1. Powers of receiver (2023)
content:
When a receiver is appointed by the court pursuant to this act, he shall have the
   power to sue for, collect, receive and take into his possession all the goods and
   chattels, rights and credits, moneys, and effects, lands and tenements, books, records,
   documents, papers, choses in action, bills, notes and property of every description
   of the person or persons for whom the receiver is appointed, received by means of
   any practice declared to be illegal and prohibited by this act, including property
   with which such property has been mingled if it cannot be identified in kind because
   of such commingling, and to sell, convey, and assign the same and hold and dispose
   of the proceeds thereof under the direction of the court.  Any person who has suffered damages as a result of the use or employment of any
   unlawful practices and submits proof to the satisfaction of the court that he has
   in fact been damaged, may participate with general creditors in the distribution of
   the assets to the extent he has sustained provable losses.  The court shall have jurisdiction of all questions arising in such proceedings and
   may make such orders and judgments therein as may be required.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Gasoline, Petroleum Products and Motor Vehicle Accessories›PA ST 73 P.S. § 202-1. Legislative findings and purposes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Gasoline, Petroleum Products and Motor Vehicle Accessories › PA ST 73 P.S. § 202-1. Legislative findings and purposes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 202-1. Legislative findings and purposes (2023)
content:
The General Assembly of this Commonwealth finds and declares that the distribution
   and sales of gasoline and petroleum products in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania,
   including the rights and obligations of suppliers and dealers, vitally affects its
   general economy.  In order to promote the public interest and public welfare of this Commonwealth;
   to avoid undue control of the dealer by suppliers;  to foster and keep alive vigorous
   and healthy competition for the benefit of the public by prohibiting practices through
   which fair and honest competition is destroyed or prevented;  to promote the public
   safety;  to prevent deterioration of facilities for servicing motor vehicles on the
   highways of this Commonwealth;  and to prevent dealers from unnecessarily going out
   of business, thereby resulting in unemployment with loss of tax revenue to the Commonwealth
   and its inevitable train of undesirable consequences;  it is necessary to legislate
   standards pursuant to the exercise of the police power of this Commonwealth governing
   the relationship between suppliers and distributors of gasoline and petroleum products
   and the dealers who sell the products to the public.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Gasoline, Petroleum Products and Motor Vehicle Accessories›PA ST 73 P.S. § 202-3. Cancellation, termination or failure to renew an agreement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Gasoline, Petroleum Products and Motor Vehicle Accessories › PA ST 73 P.S. § 202-3. Cancellation, termination or failure to renew an agreement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 202-3. Cancellation, termination or failure to renew an agreement (2023)
content:
(a) The lessor supplier shall not cancel, terminate or fail to renew an agreement
      unless it furnishes prior notification, pursuant to this subsection, to the other
      party.  The notification shall be in writing and sent to the lessee dealer by certified
      mail not less than 90 days prior to the date on which the franchise will be cancelled,
      terminated or not renewed.  The notification shall contain a statement of intention to cancel, terminate or
      not renew, together with the reasons therefor, which reasons shall be limited to those
      set forth in subsection (b) and the date on which such action shall take effect.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Gasoline, Petroleum Products and Motor Vehicle Accessories›PA ST 73 P.S. § 202-6. Action against lessor supplier; damages; injunction; costs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Gasoline, Petroleum Products and Motor Vehicle Accessories › PA ST 73 P.S. § 202-6. Action against lessor supplier; damages; injunction; costs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 202-6. Action against lessor supplier; damages; injunction; costs (2023)
content:
Any lessee dealer may bring an action against its lessor supplier for violation of
   this act in the respective court of common pleas wherein the business is located to
   recover damages sustained by reason of a wilful and intentional violation of this
   act and, where appropriate, shall be entitled to injunctive relief.  Such lessee dealer, if successful and if it be adjudged that such violation was
   wilful and intentional, shall also be entitled to the costs of the action including,
   but not limited to, reasonable attorneys' fees.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 202-8. Limitation of liability of lessor supplier, its officers, agent or employees for furnishing information (2023)
content:
No liability on the part of and no cause of action of any nature shall arise against
   any lessor supplier, its officers, agents or employees furnishing information as to
   reasons for termination, cancellation, intent not to renew, failure to renew, unacceptability
   of a proposed transferee, or relating to the character, financial ability or business
   experience of a proposed transferee, or for statements made or evidence submitted
   at any hearing or trial conducted in connection therewith.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 202-10. Severability (2023)
content:
The provisions of this act are severable and if any provision or part hereof shall
   be held invalid or unconstitutional or inapplicable to any person or circumstances,
   such invalidity, unconstitutionality or inapplicability shall not affect or impair
   the remaining provisions of the act.  It is hereby declared to be the legislative intent that this act would have been
   adopted if such invalid, unconstitutional or inapplicable provisions had not been
   included therein.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Feature Motion Picture Fair Business Practices Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 203-4. Blind bidding
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Feature Motion Picture Fair Business Practices Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 203-4. Blind bidding
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 203-4. Blind bidding (2023)
content:
Blind bidding is hereby prohibited within the Commonwealth.  No negotiations between exhibitors and distributors for the licensing or exhibition
   of a feature motion picture shall take place and no license agreement or any of its
   terms shall be agreed to for the exhibition of any feature motion picture within the
   Commonwealth before the feature motion picture has been trade screened within the
   Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Feature Motion Picture Fair Business Practices Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 203-6. Advances

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 203-6. Advances (2023)
content:
(a) Advances prohibited.--It shall be unlawful for any license agreement for the exhibition of a feature motion
      picture at a theatre within the Commonwealth to contain or be conditioned upon a provision,
      agreement or understanding that the exhibitor shall advance any funds prior to the
      exhibition of the picture as security for the performance of the license agreement
      or to be applied to payments under such an agreement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Feature Motion Picture Fair Business Practices Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 203-11. Liability of exhibitor for furnishing information
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Feature Motion Picture Fair Business Practices Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 203-11. Liability of exhibitor for furnishing information
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 203-11. Liability of exhibitor for furnishing information (2023)
content:
No liability on the part of and no cause of action of any nature shall arise against
   any exhibitor, its officers, agents or employees furnishing information as to violations
   of this act, or for statements made or evidence submitted at any hearing or trial
   conducted in connection therewith.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Feature Motion Picture Fair Business Practices Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 203-7. Length of run
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Feature Motion Picture Fair Business Practices Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 203-7. Length of run
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 203-7. Length of run (2023)
content:
No license agreement shall be entered into between distributor and exhibitor to grant
   an exclusive first run or an exclusive multiple first run for more than 42 days without
   provision to expand the run to second run or subsequent run theatres within the geographical
   area and license agreements and prints of said feature motion picture shall be made
   available by the distributor to those subsequent run theatres that would normally
   be served on subsequent run availability.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Feature Motion Picture Fair Business Practices Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 203-10. Actions against distributors and exhibitors

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 203-10. Actions against distributors and exhibitors (2023)
content:
Any exhibitor may bring an action against a distributor or exhibitor or both in the
   respective court of common pleas wherein the exhibitor's business is located to recover
   damages sustained by reason of a willful and intentional violation of this act and,
   where appropriate, shall be entitled to injunctive relief.  Such exhibitor, if successful, shall also be awarded the costs of the action including,
   but not limited to, reasonable attorneys' fees.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Cash Consumer Protection Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-3. Refusal to provide property prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Cash Consumer Protection Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-3. Refusal to provide property prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-3. Refusal to provide property prohibited (2023)
content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to refuse to rent or sell property or services
   to any individual for the reason that the individual does not possess a credit card.  Nothing in this section requires the acceptance of any particular form of payment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Cash Consumer Protection Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-4. Reasonable security authorized; excessive security prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Cash Consumer Protection Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-4. Reasonable security authorized; excessive security prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-4. Reasonable security authorized; excessive security prohibited (2023)
content:
(a) Demand for security.--A person may, prior to providing property or services to an individual who does not
      possess a credit card, demand and receive reasonable security from the individual
      to secure payment for the property or services requested.  Reasonable security may take the form of a payment in cash on account reasonably
      related to the value of the property or services to be provided or any other appropriate
      assurance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Cash Consumer Protection Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-6. Payment of costs and restitution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Cash Consumer Protection Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-6. Payment of costs and restitution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-6. Payment of costs and restitution (2023)
content:
Whenever any court issues a permanent injunction to restrain and prevent violations
   of this act as authorized in section 5,1the court may in its discretion direct that the defendant or defendants restore to
   any individual in interest any moneys or property which may have been acquired by
   means of any violation of this act, under terms and conditions to be established by
   the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Cash Consumer Protection Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-8. Civil penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Cash Consumer Protection Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-8. Civil penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-8. Civil penalties (2023)
content:
(a) Violation of injunction.--Any person who violates the terms of an injunction issued under section 51or any of the terms of an assurance of voluntary compliance duly filed in court under
      section 72shall forfeit and pay to the Commonwealth a civil penalty of not more than $1,000
      for each violation.  For the purposes of this section, the court issuing an injunction or in which an
      assurance of voluntary compliance is filed shall retain jurisdiction and the cause
      shall be continued and, in such cases, the Attorney General or the appropriate district
      attorney, acting in the name of the Commonwealth may petition for recovery of civil
      penalties and any other equitable relief deemed needed or proper.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Cash Consumer Protection Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-7. Assurances of voluntary compliance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Cash Consumer Protection Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-7. Assurances of voluntary compliance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-7. Assurances of voluntary compliance (2023)
content:
In the administration of this act, the Attorney General may accept an assurance of
   voluntary compliance with respect to any method, act or practice deemed to be violative
   of the act from any person who has engaged or was about to engage in the method, act
   or practice.  The assurance may include a stipulation for voluntary payment by the alleged violator
   providing for the restitution by the alleged violator to individuals of money or other
   things received from them in connection with a violation of this act.  Any assurance shall be in writing and be filed with the court.  The assurance of voluntary compliance shall not be considered an admission of violation
   for any purpose.  Matters thus closed may at any time be reopened by the Attorney General for further
   proceedings in the public interest, pursuant to section 5.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Cash Consumer Protection Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-5. Injunctive relief
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Cash Consumer Protection Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-5. Injunctive relief
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-5. Injunctive relief (2023)
content:
Whenever the Attorney General or a district attorney has reason to believe that any
   person is violating or is about to violate section 3 or 41and that proceedings would be in the public interest, the Attorney General or a district
   attorney may bring an action in the name of the Commonwealth against the person to
   restrain by temporary or permanent injunction violations of section 3 or 4.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Cash Consumer Protection Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-9. Private actions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Cash Consumer Protection Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-9. Private actions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 204-9. Private actions (2023)
content:
(a) Amount of damages.--Any person who suffers any ascertainable loss of money or property, as a result of
      the use or employment by any person of a method, act or practice declared unlawful
      by section 3 or 41may bring a private action to recover actual damages or $100, whichever is greater.  The court may, in its discretion, award up to three times the actual damages sustained,
      but not less than $100, and may provide additional relief as it deems necessary or
      proper.  The court shall award reasonable attorney's fees to a person who prevails in an
      action brought pursuant to this subsection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-3. Termination of dealer agreement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-3. Termination of dealer agreement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-3. Termination of dealer agreement (2023)
content:
(a) General provisions.--It shall be unlawful for a supplier to terminate, cancel or fail to renew a dealer
      agreement except as provided in subsection (b) or (c).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-1. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-1. Short title

content: The provisions of this act shall not require the repurchase from a dealer of:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-5. Death or incapacitation of dealer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-5. Death or incapacitation of dealer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-5. Death or incapacitation of dealer (2023)
content:
In the event of the death or incapacity of a dealer, the supplier shall repurchase,
   at the option of the heir or authorized representative of such person or stockholder,
   the equipment, repair parts and specialized repair tools of the dealer as if the supplier
   had terminated, canceled or failed to renew the contract.  The heir or authorized representative shall have 120 days from the date of the death
   of such dealer or from the date such dealer is determined to be incapacitated or becomes
   totally disabled, as applicable, to exercise the option under this section.  Nothing in this act requires the repurchase of any equipment, repair parts and specialized
   repair tools if the heir and supplier enter into a new contract to operate the retail
   dealership.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-8. Failure to repurchase
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-8. Failure to repurchase
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-8. Failure to repurchase (2023)
content:
Any supplier that shall fail to repurchase and make the payments therefor as required
   by this act shall be liable to the dealer for interest on the unpaid balance of sums
   owed to the dealer as provided in section 3.1Interest shall be simple interest at the rate published by the Secretary of Revenue
   pursuant to section 806 of the act of April 9, 1929 (P.L. 343, No. 176), known as
   The Fiscal Code,2plus 10% per annum.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-7. Security interest and bulk sales
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-7. Security interest and bulk sales
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-7. Security interest and bulk sales (2023)
content:
Nothing in this act shall be construed to affect in any way any security interest
   which the supplier may have in the equipment, repair parts or specialized repair tools
   of the dealer, and any repurchase pursuant to this act is not subject to the provisions
   of 13 Pa.C.S. Ch. 611(relating to bulk transfers).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-6. Repurchase of unused specialized repair tools
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-6. Repurchase of unused specialized repair tools
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-6. Repurchase of unused specialized repair tools (2023)
content:
A supplier shall repurchase, upon the written request of a dealer, any specialized
   repair tool purchased by the dealer pursuant to the requirements of the supplier which
   remains unused for more than a 12-month period after the dealer receives the same.  The repurchase price payable to the dealer under this section shall be the original
   cost to the dealer plus a handling charge equal to 10% of such original cost.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-9. No coercion
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-9. No coercion
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-9. No coercion (2023)
content:
It shall be a violation for any supplier to require, attempt to require, coerce or
   attempt to coerce any dealer in this Commonwealth to order or accept delivery of any
   equipment or repair parts not required by law which shall not have been voluntarily
   ordered by the dealer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-10. Injunctive relief
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-10. Injunctive relief
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-10. Injunctive relief (2023)
content:
In any action brought by a dealer under this act, any violation of this act by the
   supplier shall be deemed an irreparable injury to the dealer sufficient to sustain
   issuance of a temporary injunction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-13. Effective date

content: This act shall take effect immediately.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-11. General repeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-11. General repeals

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law›PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-12. Applicability
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Pennsylvania Fair Dealership Law › PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-12. Applicability
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 205-12. Applicability (2023)
content:
The provisions of this act shall apply to existing dealer agreements which can be
   terminated at will and to dealer agreements entered into or renewed after the effective
   date of this act.  Nothing contained in this section is intended to violatesection 17 of Article I of the Constitution of Pennsylvania, relative to impairing the obligations of contracts.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Electronic Receiving and Picture Tubes›PA ST 73 P.S. § 208-2. Prohibitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Electronic Receiving and Picture Tubes › PA ST 73 P.S. § 208-2. Prohibitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 208-2. Prohibitions (2023)
content:
(a) Except as hereinafter provided, no person shall knowingly distribute or sell,
      offer to distribute or sell, expose for distribution or sale, possess with intent
      to distribute or sell or otherwise dispose of, for a consideration any reactivated
      tube, second-hand tube or used tube or tube utilizing used components without clearly
      disclosing the true or actual quality or condition of such tube by means of a stamp,
      mark, tag, notice or label attached to such tube and to any carton or container thereof
      in such manner that it cannot readily be removed or of such a nature as to remain
      in place until removed by the purchaser at retail.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Electronic Receiving and Picture Tubes›PA ST 73 P.S. § 208-3. Penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Electronic Receiving and Picture Tubes › PA ST 73 P.S. § 208-3. Penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 208-3. Penalty (2023)
content:
(a) Any person violating the provisions of this act1shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be sentenced
      to pay a fine not exceeding five hundred dollars ($500) or to undergo imprisonment
      not exceeding one year, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Electronic Receiving and Picture Tubes›PA ST 73 P.S. § 208-4. Application of act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Electronic Receiving and Picture Tubes › PA ST 73 P.S. § 208-4. Application of act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 208-4. Application of act (2023)
content:
Nothing in this act1shall apply to any television or sound radio broadcasting station or to any publisher
   or printer of a newspaper, magazine or other form of printed advertising, who broadcasts,
   publishes or prints such advertisement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Blind-Made Products›PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-3. Blind-made product defined
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Blind-Made Products › PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-3. Blind-made product defined
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-3. Blind-made product defined (2023)
content:
A blind-made product shall be one which in its manufacture and packaging has involved
   the use of blind workers to an extent constituting not less than seventy-five per
   cent of the total personnel engaged in the direct labor of manufacture and packaging
   of the product.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Electronic Receiving and Picture Tubes›PA ST 73 P.S. § 208-5. Effective date
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Electronic Receiving and Picture Tubes › PA ST 73 P.S. § 208-5. Effective date
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 208-5. Effective date (2023)
content: This act1shall take effect in ten days.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Blind-Made Products›PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-1. Sale
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Blind-Made Products › PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-1. Sale
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-1. Sale (2023)
content:
It shall be unlawful for any person, firm, corporation, company or partnership to
   sell, or offer to sell, to the public any merchandise or other products of any nature,
   which are represented to be blind-made products, unless the merchandise or other products
   have been actually made or manufactured by blind persons as defined in this act, or
   if such merchandise or other products are made or manufactured by a corporation, association
   or partnership, it shall be unlawful for such products to be sold or offered for sale
   to the public as blind-made products unless they are blind-made products as defined
   in this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 5. Unfair Sales›General Provisions›PA ST 73 P.S. § 214. Persons violating guilty of misdemeanor; penalty; separate violations; prima facie evidence
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 5. Unfair Sales › General Provisions › PA ST 73 P.S. § 214. Persons violating guilty of misdemeanor; penalty; separate violations; prima facie evidence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 214. Persons violating guilty of misdemeanor; penalty; separate violations; prima facie evidence (2023)
content:
Any retailer who shall, in contravention of the policy of this act, advertise, offer
   to sell or sell at retail any item of merchandise at less than cost to the retailer
   as defined in this act, or any wholesaler who shall, in contravention of the policy
   of this act, advertise, offer to sell or sell at wholesale any item of merchandise
   at less than cost to the wholesaler as defined in this act, or any person, partnership,
   corporation or association engaged in business both as a wholesaler and retailer as
   defined in this act who shall, in contravention of the policy of this act, advertise,
   offer to sell or sell any item of merchandise at less than cost, subject to both the
   retail and wholesale mark-ups provided by this act, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor,
   and, upon conviction thereof, be sentenced to pay a fine of not less than fifty dollars
   ($50) nor more than two hundred dollars ($200) and costs of prosecution, and, in default
   thereof, shall undergo imprisonment for not more than thirty (30) days.  Each advertisement, offer to sell or sale shall constitute a separate violation
   of the provisions of this act and shall subject the offender to the penalties hereby
   prescribed.  Proof of any such advertisement, offer to sell or sale by any retailer or wholesaler
   in contravention of the policy of this act shall be prima facie evidence of a violation
   of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Blind-Made Products›PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-2. Name or title of seller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Blind-Made Products › PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-2. Name or title of seller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-2. Name or title of seller (2023)
content:
It shall be unlawful for any person, firm, corporation, company or partnership having
   products for sale to use the word blind in the name or title of the person, firm,
   corporation, company or partnership, unless the person, firm, corporation, company
   or partnership limits its sales to the sale of blind-made products as defined in this
   act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Dog and Cat Product Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-2. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Dog and Cat Product Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-2. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-2. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this act shall have the meanings given
   to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Blind-Made Products›PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-4. Blind person defined
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Blind-Made Products › PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-4. Blind person defined
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-4. Blind person defined (2023)
content:
For the purposes of this act, a blind person engaged in the manufacture and packaging
   of blind-made products shall be one who has visual acuity not to exceed twenty two-hundredths
   in the better eye with correcting lenses or visual acuity greater than twenty two-hundredths
   but with a limitation in the fields of vision such that the widest diameter of the
   visual field subtends an angle no greater than twenty degrees.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Dog and Cat Product Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-1. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Dog and Cat Product Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-1. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-1. Short title (2023)
content: This act shall be known and may be cited as the Dog and Cat Product Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Blind-Made Products›PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-5. “Blinds” products; name “Blind”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Blind-Made Products › PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-5. “Blinds” products; name “Blind”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-5. “Blinds” products; name “Blind” (2023)
content:
The provisions of section 2 of this act1shall not apply to the sale, or the offer to sell, merchandise or products known
   as “blinds,” nor to persons whose given individual names are “Blind”.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Blind-Made Products›PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-6. Penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Blind-Made Products › PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-6. Penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 209-6. Penalty (2023)
content:
Any person who violates any provisions of this act shall, upon summary conviction
   thereof, be sentenced to pay a fine not exceeding one hundred dollars ($100) and costs
   of prosecution, and in default of payment thereof, shall undergo imprisonment not
   exceeding thirty days.  Each sale, or offer to sell, merchandise or products in violation of the provisions
   of this act shall be deemed a separate offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Dog and Cat Product Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-4. Criminal offense
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Dog and Cat Product Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-4. Criminal offense
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-4. Criminal offense (2023)
content:
(a) Criminal offense.--A person who knowingly sells or offers for sale, wholesale or retail, the fur, skin
      or hair of a dog or cat or any product or part of a product containing the fur, skin
      or hair of a dog or cat commits a criminal offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Dog and Cat Product Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-7. Effective date
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Dog and Cat Product Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-7. Effective date
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-7. Effective date (2023)
content: This act shall take effect in 60 days.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Dog and Cat Product Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-6. Unfair trade practice
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Dog and Cat Product Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-6. Unfair trade practice
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-6. Unfair trade practice (2023)
content:
A violation of the prohibition under section 31shall be considered a violation of the act of December 17, 1968 (P.L. 1224, No. 387),2known as the Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law, and the provisions
   of that act shall apply insofar as they are not inconsistent with this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Dog and Cat Product Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-5. Duty to report and investigate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Dog and Cat Product Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-5. Duty to report and investigate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-5. Duty to report and investigate (2023)
content:
(a) Report.--A person who has reason to suspect that a product sold or offered for sale, wholesale
      or retail, contains the fur, skin or hair of a dog or cat shall report that information
      to the bureau.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices›Dog and Cat Product Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-3. Prohibition
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 4. Fair Trade and Business Practices › Dog and Cat Product Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-3. Prohibition
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 210-3. Prohibition (2023)
content:
No person shall sell or offer for sale, wholesale or retail, the fur, skin or hair
   of a dog or cat or any product or part of a product containing the fur, skin or hair
   of a dog or cat.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 5. Unfair Sales›General Provisions›PA ST 73 P.S. § 211. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 5. Unfair Sales › General Provisions › PA ST 73 P.S. § 211. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 211. Short title (2023)
content: This act shall be known and designated and may be cited as the “Unfair Sales Act”.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 5. Unfair Sales›General Provisions›PA ST 73 P.S. § 212. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 5. Unfair Sales › General Provisions › PA ST 73 P.S. § 212. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 212. Definitions (2023)
content:
(1) When used in this act the term“cost to the retailer”shall mean the invoice cost of the merchandise to the retailer or the replacement
      cost of the merchandise to the retailer, whichever is lower, less all trade discounts,
      except customary discounts for cash, advertising allowances, promotional allowances,
      display allowances and any other allowances for services rendered and any other commission
      or remuneration received for services performed on behalf of any governmental agencies,
      to which shall be added (a) freight charges not otherwise included in the invoice
      or the replacement cost of the merchandise, (b) a mark-up to cover in part the cost
      of doing business, which mark-up in the absence of proof of a lesser cost, shall be
      not less than four per cent of the total cost at retail outlet.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 5. Unfair Sales›General Provisions›PA ST 73 P.S. § 213. Sale, offer to sell or advertisement at less than cost prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 5. Unfair Sales › General Provisions › PA ST 73 P.S. § 213. Sale, offer to sell or advertisement at less than cost prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 213. Sale, offer to sell or advertisement at less than cost prohibited (2023)
content:
It is hereby declared that advertisement, offer to sell or sale of any merchandise,
   either by retailers or wholesalers, at less than cost as defined in this act with
   the intent of unfairly diverting trade from or otherwise injuring a competitor or
   with the result of deceiving any purchaser or prospective purchaser, substantially
   lessening competition, unreasonably restraining trade or tending to create a monopoly
   in any line of commerce is an unfair method of competition contrary to public policy
   and in contravention of the policy of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 5. Unfair Sales›General Provisions›PA ST 73 P.S. § 216. Excepted sales
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 5. Unfair Sales › General Provisions › PA ST 73 P.S. § 216. Excepted sales
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 216. Excepted sales (2023)
content:
The provisions of this act shall not apply to sales at retail or sales at wholesale
   (a) where merchandise is sold in bona fide clearance sales, if advertised, marked
   and sold as such;  (b) where perishable merchandise must be sold promptly in order
   to forestall loss;  (c) where merchandise is imperfect or damaged or is being discontinued
   and is advertised, marked and sold as such;  (d) where merchandise is sold upon the
   final liquidation of any business;  (e) where merchandise is sold for charitable purposes
   or to relief agencies;  (f) where merchandise is sold on contract to departments of
   the government or governmental institutions;  (g) when the price of merchandise is
   made in good faith to meet competition;  (h) where merchandise is sold by any officer
   acting under the order or direction of any court;  (i) where tools, equipment and
   materials used by employes in their trade or business or appliances and products which
   are used therein and are or may be beneficial to the safety, health and working conditions
   of such employes are sold to employes of the seller.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 5. Unfair Sales›General Provisions›PA ST 73 P.S. § 215. Injunctive relief
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 5. Unfair Sales › General Provisions › PA ST 73 P.S. § 215. Injunctive relief
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 215. Injunctive relief (2023)
content:
In addition to the penalties provided in this act, the courts of this State are hereby
   invested with jurisdiction to prevent and restrain violations of this act, and any
   person, partnership, corporation or association shall be entitled to sue for and have
   injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction against any loss or injury
   by reason of a violation of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 5A. Price Gouging Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 232.4. Price gouging prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 5A. Price Gouging Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 232.4. Price gouging prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 232.4. Price gouging prohibited (2023)
content:
(a) Prohibition.--During and within 30 days of the termination of a state of disaster emergency declared
      by the Governor pursuant to the provisions of35 Pa.C.S. § 7301(c)(relating to general authority of Governor), it shall be a violation of this act
      for any party within the chain of distribution of consumer goods or services or both
      to sell or offer to sell the goods or services within the geographic region that is
      the subject of the declared emergency for an amount which represents an unconscionably
      excessive price.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 5A. Price Gouging Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 232.1. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 5A. Price Gouging Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 232.1. Short title

content: This act shall be known and may be cited as the Price Gouging Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 5A. Price Gouging Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 232.5. Investigation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 5A. Price Gouging Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 232.5. Investigation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 232.5. Investigation (2023)
content:
(a) Authority.--The Bureau of Consumer Protection in the Office of Attorney General shall investigate
      any complaints received concerning violations of this act.  If, after investigating any complaint, the Attorney General finds that there has
      been a violation of this act, the Attorney General may bring an action to impose a
      civil penalty up to $10,000 for each violation and to seek other relief, including
      injunctive relief, restitution and costs under the act of December 17, 1968 (P.L.
      1224 No. 387),1known as the Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 6. Second-Hand Articles›Second-Hand Watches›PA ST 73 P.S. § 241. Watches to be tagged as second-hand
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 6. Second-Hand Articles › Second-Hand Watches › PA ST 73 P.S. § 241. Watches to be tagged as second-hand
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 241. Watches to be tagged as second-hand (2023)
content:
Any person who sells, exchanges, offers to sell, or exchange, exposes or displays
   for sale, or exchange, or possesses, with intent to sell, or exchange, a second-hand
   watch, shall affix and keep affixed to the same a tag with the words “second-hand”
   legibly written or printed thereon in the English language.
