path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2123. Consignment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2123. Consignment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2123. Consignment (2023)
content:
When an artist or other person delivers or causes the delivery of a craft or work
   of fine art to an art dealer, to be sold by the art dealer for a commission, the transfer
   to and acceptance by the art dealer of the craft or work of fine art shall be considered
   on consignment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2124. Property and proceeds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2124. Property and proceeds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2124. Property and proceeds (2023)
content:
(a) Trust property.--A craft or work of fine art accepted on consignment is trust property being held by
      the consignee for the benefit of the consignor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 31. Fine Arts Preservation Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2107. Rights and duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 31. Fine Arts Preservation Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2107. Rights and duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2107. Rights and duties (2023)
content: The rights and duties created under this act:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2127. Receipt
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2127. Receipt
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2127. Receipt (2023)
content:
An art dealer shall not accept a craft or work of fine art for a commission on consignment
   unless, before the time of acceptance, the art dealer conveys to the consignor a written
   receipt describing the craft or work of fine art delivered to the art dealer and setting
   out the terms of the consignment agreement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 31. Fine Arts Preservation Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2106. Evidence
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 31. Fine Arts Preservation Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2106. Evidence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2106. Evidence (2023)
content:
In determining by a preponderance of the evidence whether a work of art is of recognized
   quality and thus fine art, as defined in this act, the trier of fact shall rely on
   the testimony of artists, art dealers, collectors of fine art, curators of art museums
   and other persons involved with the creation or commercial trade of fine art.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2126. Property and funds not subject to claims, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2126. Property and funds not subject to claims, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2126. Property and funds not subject to claims, etc. (2023)
content:
Property or funds which are held in trust under section 41are not subject to the claims, liens or security interest of the creditors of an
   art dealer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2125. Sale of works
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2125. Sale of works
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2125. Sale of works (2023)
content:
A craft or work of fine art initially received on consignment shall remain trust property
   under section 4,1notwithstanding the subsequent purchase of the craft or work of fine art by the consignee,
   directly or indirectly, for the consignee's own account, until the terms of the purchase
   are completed.  If the craft or work is resold to a third party who is a bona fide purchaser before
   the consignor has been paid in full, the work of fine art shall cease to be trust
   property, and the proceeds of the resale shall be trust funds under section 4 to the
   extent necessary to pay the balance due the consignor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2128. Liability for loss or damage
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2128. Liability for loss or damage
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2128. Liability for loss or damage (2023)
content:
An art dealer who accepts a craft or work of fine art on consignment shall be liable
   in a civil action brought by the consignor for the loss of or damages to the craft
   or work of fine art.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2129. Waiver of rights
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2129. Waiver of rights
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2129. Waiver of rights (2023)
content: A consignor may not waive his rights under this act unless the waiver is in writing.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2130. Application of act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2130. Application of act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2130. Application of act (2023)
content:
This act applies to crafts and works of art accepted on consignment on and after the
   effective date of this act.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 33. Gasoline Additive Information › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2141. Definitions

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 33. Gasoline Additive Information›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2142. Posting of gasoline additive information
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 33. Gasoline Additive Information › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2142. Posting of gasoline additive information
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2142. Posting of gasoline additive information (2023)
content:
(a) Requirement.--All retail service station dealers shall conspicuously post on each pump from which
      gasoline containing gasoline additives is dispensed a sign clearly indicating that
      the gasoline contains gasoline additives, the type or types of gasoline additives
      contained in the gasoline and the maximum percentage by volume, to the nearest whole
      percent, of each gasoline additive.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2131. Effective date
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 32. Artworks Consignment Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2131. Effective date
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2131. Effective date (2023)
content: This act shall take effect in 60 days.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 34. Insurance on Rented and Leased Motor Vehicles›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2152. Duty of lessor of motor vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 34. Insurance on Rented and Leased Motor Vehicles › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2152. Duty of lessor of motor vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2152. Duty of lessor of motor vehicles (2023)
content:
It shall be the duty of the lessor of motor vehicles to ensure that, in the event
   the rented motor vehicle is not returned during the contracted rental period, all
   liability or first party coverage continues until such time as the motor vehicle is
   reported to the police as stolen.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 33. Gasoline Additive Information›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2143. Notification by manufacturers of gasoline additive information
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 33. Gasoline Additive Information › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2143. Notification by manufacturers of gasoline additive information
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2143. Notification by manufacturers of gasoline additive information (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Manufacturers of gasoline which contains gasoline additives shall notify gasoline
      purchasers, in writing, as to the presence of the additives.  This requirement shall continue for each seller until the product is resold to the
      public.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 34. Insurance on Rented and Leased Motor Vehicles›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2151. Limitation on exclusion of certain benefits under insurance policies or self-insurance arrangements covering rented or leased motor vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 34. Insurance on Rented and Leased Motor Vehicles › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2151. Limitation on exclusion of certain benefits under insurance policies or self-insurance arrangements covering rented or leased motor vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2151. Limitation on exclusion of certain benefits under insurance policies or self-insurance arrangements covering rented or leased motor vehicles (2023)
content:
No motor vehicle rented or leased from any location in this Commonwealth may be covered
   by an insurance policy or self-insurance arrangement which excludes benefits if the
   lessee or any other authorized driver is involved in a vehicular accident while under
   the influence of drugs or intoxicating beverages at the time of the accident.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 33. Gasoline Additive Information›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2144. Federal requirements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 33. Gasoline Additive Information › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2144. Federal requirements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2144. Federal requirements (2023)
content:
It shall be unlawful to sell or offer for sale any gasoline additives where the blend
   or mixture is in violation of the specifications or the registration requirements
   established by the United States Environmental Protection Agency pursuant to section
   211 of the Clean Air Act (Public Law 95-95,42 U.S.C. § 7545).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 34. Insurance on Rented and Leased Motor Vehicles›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2153. Liability of motor vehicle lessor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 34. Insurance on Rented and Leased Motor Vehicles › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2153. Liability of motor vehicle lessor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2153. Liability of motor vehicle lessor (2023)
content:
Failure of a person engaged in the rental of motor vehicles to comply with sections
   1 and 21shall, as a matter of law, render such person responsible for the mandated minimum
   limits of financial responsibility set forth in the Motor Vehicle Financial Responsibility
   Law arising out of the use of the motor vehicle for which the lessee would otherwise
   be responsible.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 34. Insurance on Rented and Leased Motor Vehicles›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2154. Application of Consumer Protection Law
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 34. Insurance on Rented and Leased Motor Vehicles › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2154. Application of Consumer Protection Law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2154. Application of Consumer Protection Law (2023)
content:
A violation of this act constitutes a violation of the act of December 17, 1968 (P.L.
   1224, No. 387), known as the Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 33. Gasoline Additive Information›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2145. Penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 33. Gasoline Additive Information › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2145. Penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2145. Penalties (2023)
content:
Any retail service station dealer who fails to comply with the provisions of this
   act after being notified by the manufacturer under section 3, and a manufacturer who
   fails to comply with the provisions of this act, commits a summary offense and shall,
   upon conviction, for the first offense, be sentenced to pay a fine not exceeding $100
   and, for a second and each subsequent offense, be sentenced to pay a fine not exceeding
   $200.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 35. Health Club Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2161. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 35. Health Club Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2161. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2161. Short title (2023)
content: This act shall be known and may be cited as the Health Club Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 35. Health Club Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2167. Noncomplying contract voidable
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 35. Health Club Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2167. Noncomplying contract voidable
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2167. Noncomplying contract voidable (2023)
content:
A health club contract which does not comply with this act shall be voidable at the
   option of the buyer.

content: This act shall take effect in 90 days.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 35. Health Club Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2168. Effect of facility closing on certain contracts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 35. Health Club Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2168. Effect of facility closing on certain contracts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2168. Effect of facility closing on certain contracts (2023)
content:
Any health club contract entered into by the buyer within 30 days of the closing of
   a health club shall be voidable at the option of the buyer.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 35. Health Club Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2162. Definitions

content:

   to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2163. Contents of health club contract (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--Every health club contract shall be in writing and shall contain the following provisions:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 35. Health Club Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2164. Duration of contract
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 35. Health Club Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2164. Duration of contract
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2164. Duration of contract (2023)
content: (a) Term.--The maximum term of a health club contract shall be 36 months.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 35. Health Club Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2174. Employee available to administer CPR
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 35. Health Club Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2174. Employee available to administer CPR
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2174. Employee available to administer CPR (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as provided under subsection (c.1), every health club shall employ and have
      on the health club's premises during the club's hours of operation a person who is
      trained and certified to administer CPR.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 35. Health Club Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2165. Initiation fees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 35. Health Club Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2165. Initiation fees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2165. Initiation fees (2023)
content:
Except as provided in section 13,1the amount of any initiation fees imposed by a health club shall be reasonably related
   to the club's costs for establishing the initial health club membership.  An initiation fee shall not be imposed for the purpose of circumventing the requirements
   of this act.  Initiation fees shall be included in the computation of any refunds due under this
   act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 35. Health Club Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2175. Offenses defined
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 35. Health Club Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2175. Offenses defined
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2175. Offenses defined (2023)
content:
(a) Unfair trade practices.--A violation of this act shall constitute a violation of the act of December 17, 1968
      (P.L. 1224, No. 387), known as the Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection
      Law,1and shall be subject to the enforcement provisions and private rights of action contained
      in that act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 35. Health Club Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2166. Provisions of act not exclusive
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 35. Health Club Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2166. Provisions of act not exclusive
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2166. Provisions of act not exclusive (2023)
content:
The provisions of this act are not exclusive and do not relieve the parties or the
   contracts subject to this act from the duty to comply with all other applicable provisions
   of law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 36. Credit Services Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2188. Restrictions on loan brokers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 36. Credit Services Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2188. Restrictions on loan brokers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2188. Restrictions on loan brokers (2023)
content:
(a) Registration requirement.--Loan brokers shall be registered with the Department of Banking pursuant to regulations
      promulgated by the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 35. Health Club Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2170. Waiver of provisions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 35. Health Club Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2170. Waiver of provisions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2170. Waiver of provisions (2023)
content:
An attempted waiver by the buyer of the provisions of this act shall be deemed contrary
   to public policy and shall be void and unenforceable.

content:
(a) Filing of financial security.--Before entering into a health club contract for health club services, a health club
      shall file and maintain with the director, in form and substance satisfactory to him,
      a bond with corporate surety from a company authorized to transact business in this
      Commonwealth or an irrevocable letter of credit from a bank insured by the Federal
      Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) in the amounts indicated below:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 35. Health Club Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2173. Health club exempt from financial security
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 35. Health Club Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2173. Health club exempt from financial security
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2173. Health club exempt from financial security (2023)
content:
A health club shall be exempt from filing and maintaining financial security upon
   providing the director satisfactory proof that all of its health club contracts meet
   all of the following requirements:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 35. Health Club Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2169. Misrepresentation rendering contract voidable
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 35. Health Club Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2169. Misrepresentation rendering contract voidable
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2169. Misrepresentation rendering contract voidable (2023)
content:
A health club contract entered into by the buyer due to false or misleading information,
   representation or advertisement of the health club or its agents shall be voidable
   at the option of the buyer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 35. Health Club Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2172. Protection afforded
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 35. Health Club Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2172. Protection afforded
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2172. Protection afforded (2023)
content:
(a) Refund to buyer.--The financial security required by section 111shall be for the benefit of a buyer who sustains any loss or damage as a result of
      the breach of contract or bankruptcy by a health club.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 35. Health Club Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2176. Rules and regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 35. Health Club Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2176. Rules and regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2176. Rules and regulations (2023)
content:
The director may adopt rules and regulations necessary to enforce and administer this
   act.  These rules and regulations, when promulgated pursuant to the act of July 31, 1968
   (P.L. 769, No. 240), referred to as the Commonwealth Documents Law,1shall have the force and effect of law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 36. Credit Services Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2181. Short title

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2177. Registration required (2023)
content:
At least 30 days prior to advertising, offering for sale, selling or providing health
   club services pursuant to a health club contract, a health club shall register with
   the director on a form and in a substance satisfactory to the director.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 36. Credit Services Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2184. Information sheet
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 36. Credit Services Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2184. Information sheet
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2184. Information sheet (2023)
content:
Prior to the execution of a contract or agreement between the buyer and a credit services
   organization or prior to the receipt by the credit services organization of any money
   or other valuable consideration, whichever occurs first, the credit services organization
   shall provide the buyer a statement in writing containing all the information required
   by section 5.1The credit services organization shall maintain on file or microfilm for a period
   of three years an exact copy of the information sheet, personally signed by the buyer,
   acknowledging receipt of a copy of the information sheet.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 36. Credit Services Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2189. Waivers and burden of proof
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 36. Credit Services Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2189. Waivers and burden of proof
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2189. Waivers and burden of proof (2023)
content:
(a) Waiver.--Any waiver by a buyer or borrower of the provisions of this act shall be deemed contrary
      to public policy and shall be void and unenforceable.  Any attempt by a credit services organization or a loan broker to have a buyer or
      borrower waive rights given by this act shall constitute a violation of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 37. Plain Language Consumer Contract Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2201. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 37. Plain Language Consumer Contract Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2201. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2201. Short title (2023)
content: This act shall be known and may be cited as the Plain Language Consumer Contract Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 36. Credit Services Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2191. Damages
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 36. Credit Services Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2191. Damages
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2191. Damages (2023)
content:
Any buyer or borrower injured by a violation of this act or by the credit services
   organization's or loan broker's breach of a contract subject to this act may bring
   an action for recovery of damages.  Judgment shall be entered for actual damages, but in no case less than the amount
   paid by the buyer or borrower to the credit services organization or loan broker,
   plus reasonable attorney fees and costs.  An award, if the trial court deems it proper, may be entered for punitive damages.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 36. Credit Services Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2192. Construction of act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 36. Credit Services Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2192. Construction of act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2192. Construction of act (2023)
content:
(a) Act not exclusive.--The provisions of this act are not exclusive and do not relieve the parties or the
      contracts subject thereto from compliance with any other applicable provision of law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 36. Credit Services Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2190. Enforcement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 36. Credit Services Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2190. Enforcement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2190. Enforcement (2023)
content:

      act of December 17, 1968 (P.L. 1224, No. 387), known as the Unfair Trade Practices
      and Consumer Protection Law.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 37. Plain Language Consumer Contract Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2202. Legislative findings and intent
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 37. Plain Language Consumer Contract Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2202. Legislative findings and intent
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2202. Legislative findings and intent (2023)
content:
(a) Legislative findings.--The General Assembly finds that many consumer contracts are written, arranged and
      designed in a way that makes them hard for consumers to understand.  Competition would be aided if these contracts were easier to understand.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 37. Plain Language Consumer Contract Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2206. Language required by other law
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 37. Plain Language Consumer Contract Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2206. Language required by other law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2206. Language required by other law (2023)
content:
The use of language required, recommended or approved by a Federal or State statute,
   rule, regulation, commentary or official interpretation thereunder, including, but
   not limited to, the Truth in Lending Act (Public Law 90-321,15 U.S.C. § 1601 et seq.), or the use of model forms required, authorized, approved or recommended by Federal
   or State authorities shall not violate this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 37. Plain Language Consumer Contract Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2204. Application of act and interpretation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 37. Plain Language Consumer Contract Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2204. Application of act and interpretation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2204. Application of act and interpretation (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--This act applies to all contracts that are made, solicited or intended to be performed
      in this Commonwealth after the effective date of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 37. Plain Language Consumer Contract Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2205. Test of readability
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 37. Plain Language Consumer Contract Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2205. Test of readability
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2205. Test of readability (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--All consumer contracts executed after the effective date of this act shall be written,
      organized and designed so that they are easy to read and understand.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 39. Motorized Wheelchair Warranty Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2233. Express warranty provision
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2233. Express warranty provision (2023)
content:
A manufacturer who sells a motorized wheelchair to a consumer, either directly or
   through a motorized wheelchair dealer, shall furnish the consumer with an express
   warranty for the motorized wheelchair.  The duration of the express warranty shall be not less than one year after first
   delivery of the motorized wheelchair to the consumer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 39. Motorized Wheelchair Warranty Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2234. Nonconformities

content:
(a) General rule.--If a new motorized wheelchair does not conform to an applicable express warranty and
      the consumer reports the nonconformity to the manufacturer, the motorized wheelchair
      lessor or any of the manufacturer's authorized motorized wheelchair dealers and makes
      the motorized wheelchair available for repair before one year after first delivery
      of the motorized wheelchair to a consumer, the nonconformity shall be repaired.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 39. Motorized Wheelchair Warranty Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2237. Damage action

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2237. Damage action (2023)

   for any damages caused by a violation of this act.  The court shall award a consumer who prevails in such an action twice the amount
   of any pecuniary loss, together with costs, disbursements and reasonable attorney
   fees, and any equitable relief that the court determines is appropriate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 40. Telemarketer Registration Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2243. Registration requirement

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2243. Registration requirement (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In addition to any other requirements imposed by law, a telemarketer or the telemarketing
      business which employs the telemarketer is required to register with the Office of
      Attorney General at least 30 days prior to offering for sale consumer goods or services
      through any medium.  This section will not apply, however, to persons or businesses licensed by or registered
      with a Federal or Commonwealth agency.  Notwithstanding any other provision of this act, any business which provides telemarketing
      services to other entities and has been under the same ownership and control for less
      than five years shall register under this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 40. Telemarketer Registration Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2245.2. Unwanted telephone solicitation calls prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 40. Telemarketer Registration Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2245.2. Unwanted telephone solicitation calls prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2245.2. Unwanted telephone solicitation calls prohibited (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No telemarketer shall initiate or cause to be initiated a telephone solicitation call
      to a telephone number of a residential or business telephone subscriber who does not
      wish to receive telephone solicitation calls and has caused his name, address and
      telephone number to be enrolled on a do-not-call list maintained by the list administrator.  This prohibition shall be effective 30 days after a quarterly do-not-call list is
      issued by the list administrator which first contains a residential or business telephone
      subscriber's name, address and residential telephone number.  In the event that the Federal Trade Commission and/or the Federal Communications
      Commission establish a national No Call Registry, the Director of the Bureau of Consumer
      Protection in the Office of Attorney General is authorized to release to the list
      administrator of such national No Call Registry sufficient data to include all those
      residential and business telephone subscribers currently enrolled on the do-not-call
      list and any residential or business telephone subscribers who subsequently enroll
      with the Bureau of Consumer Protection in the Office of Attorney General.  Prior to releasing any such data to a national No Call Registry, the Bureau of Consumer
      Protection in the Office of Attorney General shall provide those residential and business
      telephone subscribers currently enrolled with the opportunity to remove their information
      from the do-not-call list.

      received, stored or otherwise processed or used by electronic means or in electronic

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 41. Electronic Transactions Act › Chapter 3. Uniform Electronic Transactions › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.303. Legal recognition of electronic records, electronic signatures and electronic contracts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.303. Legal recognition of electronic records, electronic signatures and electronic contracts (2023)
content:
(a) Form.--A record or signature may not be denied legal effect or enforceability solely because
      it is in electronic form.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 41. Electronic Transactions Act›Chapter 3. Uniform Electronic Transactions›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.304. Provision of information in writing; presentation of records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 41. Electronic Transactions Act › Chapter 3. Uniform Electronic Transactions › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.304. Provision of information in writing; presentation of records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.304. Provision of information in writing; presentation of records (2023)
content:
(a) Writing.--If parties have agreed to conduct a transaction by electronic means and a law requires
      a person to provide, send or deliver information in writing to another person, the
      requirement is satisfied if the information is provided, sent or delivered, as the
      case may be, in an electronic record capable of retention by the recipient at the
      time of receipt.  An electronic record is not capable of retention by the recipient if the sender
      or its information processing system inhibits the ability of the recipient to print
      or store the electronic record.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 41. Electronic Transactions Act›Chapter 3. Uniform Electronic Transactions›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.307. Notarization and acknowledgment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 41. Electronic Transactions Act › Chapter 3. Uniform Electronic Transactions › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.307. Notarization and acknowledgment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.307. Notarization and acknowledgment (2023)
content:
If a law requires a signature or record to be notarized, acknowledged, verified or
   made under oath, the requirement is satisfied if the electronic signature of the person
   authorized to perform those services, together with all other information required
   to be included by other applicable law, is attached to or logically associated with
   the signature or record.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 41. Electronic Transactions Act›Chapter 3. Uniform Electronic Transactions›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.305. Attribution and effect of electronic records and signatures
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 41. Electronic Transactions Act › Chapter 3. Uniform Electronic Transactions › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.305. Attribution and effect of electronic records and signatures
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.305. Attribution and effect of electronic records and signatures (2023)
content:
(a) Attribution.--An electronic record or electronic signature is attributable to a person if it was
      the act of the person.  The act of the person may be shown in any manner, including a showing of the efficacy
      of any security procedure applied to determine the person to which the electronic
      record or electronic signature was attributable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 41. Electronic Transactions Act›Chapter 3. Uniform Electronic Transactions›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.312. Transferable records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 41. Electronic Transactions Act › Chapter 3. Uniform Electronic Transactions › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.312. Transferable records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.312. Transferable records (2023)
content:
(a) Control.--A person has control of a transferable record if a system employed for evidencing
      the transfer of interests in the transferable record reliably establishes that person
      as the person to which the transferable record was issued or transferred.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 41. Electronic Transactions Act›Chapter 5. Governmental Agencies›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.501. Creation and retention of electronic records and conversion of written records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 41. Electronic Transactions Act › Chapter 5. Governmental Agencies › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.501. Creation and retention of electronic records and conversion of written records

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 41. Electronic Transactions Act›Chapter 7. Attribution of Records and Signatures›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.704. Inapplicability to consumers

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 42. Fair Credit Extension Uniformity Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2270.5. Enforcement and penalties

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2270.5. Enforcement and penalties (2023)

      17, 1968 (P.L. 1224, No. 387), known as the Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 41. Electronic Transactions Act›Chapter 9. Consumer Agreements›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.901. Limitation on consumer agreements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 41. Electronic Transactions Act › Chapter 9. Consumer Agreements › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.901. Limitation on consumer agreements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.901. Limitation on consumer agreements (2023)
content:
In the case of a nonelectronic consumer contract or agreement, the contract or agreement
   may not contain a provision authorizing the conducting of the transaction or any part
   thereof by electronic means unless the consumer agrees to such a provision by a separate
   and express acknowledgment.  Such an agreement shall specifically indicate the parts of the transaction to be
   conducted by electronic means and shall indicate the manner in which the electronic
   transaction or a part thereof shall be conducted.  An agreement to conduct a consumer transaction or a part thereof electronically
   may not be inferred solely from the fact that the consumer has used electronic means
   to pay an account or register a purchase or warranty.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 41. Electronic Transactions Act › Chapter 9. Consumer Agreements › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2260.902. Sending and receipt

   purportedly sent to or purportedly received by the other party was not actually sent
   to or received by the other party, the purported sending or receipt of the electronic
   record shall be of no legal force or effect.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 42. Fair Credit Extension Uniformity Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2270.4. Unfair or deceptive acts or practices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 42. Fair Credit Extension Uniformity Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2270.4. Unfair or deceptive acts or practices

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 43. Breach of Personal Information Notification Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2305. Notification of consumer reporting agencies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 43. Breach of Personal Information Notification Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2305. Notification of consumer reporting agencies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2305. Notification of consumer reporting agencies (2023)
content:
When an entity provides notification under this act to more than 500 persons at one
   time, the entity shall also notify, without unreasonable delay, all consumer reporting
   agencies that compile and maintain files on consumers on a nationwide basis, as defined
   in section 603 of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (Public Law 91-508,15 U.S.C. § 1681a), of the timing, distribution and number of notices.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 43. Breach of Personal Information Notification Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2304. Exceptions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 43. Breach of Personal Information Notification Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2304. Exceptions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2304. Exceptions (2023)
content:
The notification required by this act may be delayed if a law enforcement agency determines
   and advises the entity in writing specifically referencing this section that the notification
   will impede a criminal or civil investigation.  The notification required by this act shall be made after the law enforcement agency
   determines that it will not compromise the investigation or national or homeland security.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 43. Breach of Personal Information Notification Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2303. Notification of the breach of the security of the system
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 43. Breach of Personal Information Notification Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2303. Notification of the breach of the security of the system
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2303. Notification of the breach of the security of the system (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--An entity that maintains, stores or manages computerized data that includes personal
      information shall provide notice of any breach of the security of the system following
      determination of the breach of the security of the system to any resident of this
      Commonwealth whose unencrypted and unredacted personal information was or is reasonably
      believed to have been accessed and acquired by an unauthorized person.  Except as provided in section 41or in order to take any measures necessary to determine the scope of the breach and
      to restore the reasonable integrity of the data system, the notice shall be made without
      unreasonable delay.  For the purpose of this section, a resident of this Commonwealth may be determined
      to be an individual whose principal mailing address, as reflected in the computerized
      data which is maintained, stored or managed by the entity, is in this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 43. Breach of Personal Information Notification Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2305a. Encryption required
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 43. Breach of Personal Information Notification Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2305a. Encryption required
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2305a. Encryption required (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--An entity that maintains, stores or manages computerized data on behalf of the Commonwealth
      that constitutes personal information shall utilize encryption, or other appropriate
      security measures, to reasonably protect the transmission of personal information
      over the Internet from being viewed or modified by an unauthorized third party.

   Act of 1996 (Public Law 104-191, 110 Stat. 1936)1and the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act (Public Law 111-5, 123 Stat. 226-279 and 467-496)2shall be deemed to be in compliance with the provisions of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 43. Breach of Personal Information Notification Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2306. Preemption
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 43. Breach of Personal Information Notification Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2306. Preemption
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2306. Preemption (2023)
content:
This act deals with subject matter that is of Statewide concern, and it is the intent
   of the General Assembly that this act shall supersede and preempt all rules, regulations,
   codes, statutes or ordinances of all cities, counties, municipalities and other local
   agencies within this Commonwealth regarding the matters expressly set forth in this
   act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 43. Breach of Personal Information Notification Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2305b. Data storage policy

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2305b. Data storage policy (2023)
content:
(a) Storage policy.--An entity that maintains, stores or manages computerized data on behalf of the Commonwealth
      that constitutes personal information shall develop a policy to govern reasonably
      proper storage of the personal information.  A goal of the policy shall be to reduce the risk of future breaches of the security
      of the system.

content:

   of the system that occurs on or after the effective date of this section.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2307. Notice exemption (2023)
content:
(a) Information privacy or security policy.--An entity that maintains its own notification procedures as part of an information
      privacy or security policy for the treatment of personal information and is consistent
      with the notice requirements of this act shall be deemed to be in compliance with
      the notification requirements of this act if it notifies subject persons in accordance
      with its policies in the event of a breach of security of the system.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 45. Credit Reporting Agency Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2505. Personal identification
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2505. Personal identification (2023)
content:
A consumer may request in writing a replacement personal identification number or
   password.  The request must comply with the requirements for requesting a security freeze under
   section 3.1The consumer reporting agency shall, no later than ten business days after the date
   the agency receives the request for a replacement personal identification number or
   password, provide the consumer with a new, unique personal identification number or
   password to be used by the consumer instead of the number or password that was provided
   under section 4.2

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 45. Credit Reporting Agency Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2504. Consumer reporting agency
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce › Chapter 45. Credit Reporting Agency Act › PA ST 73 P.S. § 2504. Consumer reporting agency
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 73 P.S. § 2504. Consumer reporting agency (2023)
content:
The consumer reporting agency shall, no later than ten business days after the date
   the agency receives a request from a consumer for a security freeze, send the consumer
   a written confirmation that provides the consumer with a unique personal identification
   number or password to be used by the consumer when providing authorization for the
   access to his consumer report for a specific period of time or for a specific third
   party or removing the security freeze.  In addition, the consumer reporting agency shall simultaneously provide to the consumer
   in writing notification of the process of removing a security freeze and the process
   of temporarily lifting a security freeze and the process for allowing access to information
   from the consumer report for a specific party or for a specific period while the security
   freeze is in effect.

      by certified mail or by a toll-free telephone number which shall be provided by the
      consumer reporting agency and may be able to contact the consumer reporting agency
      through a secure Internet connection which may be established by the consumer reporting
      agency and request that the security freeze be temporarily lifted or removed and provide
      all of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 73 P.S. Trade and Commerce›Chapter 45. Credit Reporting Agency Act›PA ST 73 P.S. § 2508. Secure procedures

   Internet or other electronic media, to receive and process a request from a consumer
   to place a security freeze, temporarily lift a security freeze or remove a security
   freeze on a consumer report pursuant to this act in an expedited manner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Lighthouses on Delaware and Schuylkill Rivers›PA ST 74 P.S. § 17. Condemnation proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Lighthouses on Delaware and Schuylkill Rivers › PA ST 74 P.S. § 17. Condemnation proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 17. Condemnation proceedings (2023)
content:
In case the United States shall decide to resort to condemnation in acquiring land
   for the purposes specified in the first and second sections of this act,1the said United States shall, in all respects, be governed by the laws of this state
   regulating the appropriation of private property for public use, and said laws are
   hereby made applicable:  Provided, That the United States may pay the costs and refuse
   to take the land if, in their judgment, the compensation assessed therefor is excessive.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Federal Buildings in General›PA ST 74 P.S. § 1. Jurisdiction of state ceded to the United States, in certain cases
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Federal Buildings in General › PA ST 74 P.S. § 1. Jurisdiction of state ceded to the United States, in certain cases
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 1. Jurisdiction of state ceded to the United States, in certain cases (2023)
content:
The jurisdiction of this State is hereby ceded to the United States of America over
   all such pieces or parcels of land, not exceeding ten acres in any one township, ward
   or city, or borough, within the limits of this State, as have been or shall hereafter
   be selected and acquired by the United States for the purpose of erecting post offices,
   custom houses or other structures, exclusively owned by the general government, and
   used for its purposes:  Provided, That an accurate description and plan of such lands,
   so acquired, verified by the oath of some officer of the general government having
   knowledge of the facts, shall be filed with the Department of Internal Affairs of
   this State, as soon as said United States shall have acquired possession of the same.
