path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Retrocession of Federal Jurisdiction›PA ST 74 P.S. § 3. General provisions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Retrocession of Federal Jurisdiction › PA ST 74 P.S. § 3. General provisions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 3. General provisions (2023)
content:
The consent of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania is hereby given to the retrocession
   of jurisdiction by the United States over land within the boundaries of the Commonwealth.  The Governor is hereby authorized to accept for the Commonwealth such retrocession
   to partial, concurrent, or exclusive jurisdiction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Lands for Dams, Locks, Etc.›PA ST 74 P.S. § 11. Consent to acquisition of lands for dams, locks, etc., by the United States
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Lands for Dams, Locks, Etc. › PA ST 74 P.S. § 11. Consent to acquisition of lands for dams, locks, etc., by the United States
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 11. Consent to acquisition of lands for dams, locks, etc., by the United States (2023)
content:
Whenever the United States shall make an appropriation, and shall be about to begin
   the improvement of any of the navigable waters within the state of Pennsylvania, by
   means of locks and permanent and moveable dam or dams with adjustable chutes, the
   consent of the state of Pennsylvania, through the governor thereof, is hereby given
   to the acquisition by the United States, by purchase, or by condemnation in the manner
   hereinafter provided, of any lands, buildings or other property, necessary for the
   purpose of erecting thereon dams, abutments, locks, lockhouses, chutes and other necessary
   structures for the construction and maintenance of slack water navigation on said
   rivers, and the United States shall have, hold, use and occupy the said land or lands,
   buildings, or other property, when purchased or acquired as provided by this act,
   and shall exercise jurisdiction and control over the same, concurrently with the state
   of Pennsylvania.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Lands for Dams, Locks, Etc.›PA ST 74 P.S. § 13. Penalty for injuring property so acquired
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Lands for Dams, Locks, Etc. › PA ST 74 P.S. § 13. Penalty for injuring property so acquired
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 13. Penalty for injuring property so acquired (2023)
content:
If any person or persons shall wilfully or maliciously injure any of the lands, buildings
   or other property acquired or held under the provisions of this act, such person or
   persons shall be liable to a fine of not exceeding one hundred dollars, and to an
   imprisonment not exceeding six months, or both or either, at the discretion of the
   court, said offense to be prosecuted and punished in any court of competent jurisdiction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Lands for Dams, Locks, Etc.›PA ST 74 P.S. § 12. Manner of acquiring land
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Lands for Dams, Locks, Etc. › PA ST 74 P.S. § 12. Manner of acquiring land
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 12. Manner of acquiring land (2023)
content:
If the United States shall determine to take lands, buildings or other property, necessary
   for the purposes mentioned in the first section1of this act, and cannot agree with the owner or owners of such lands, buildings or
   other property for the compensation to be made for such taking, the court of common
   pleas having jurisdiction in the county where such lands, buildings or other property
   is situated, shall, upon application by either the United States, or the owner or
   owners, or any one in behalf of either, appoint three disinterested freeholders, who,
   having duly qualified before said court, and having given such public notice and such
   notice to owners of the premises to be viewed and appraised of the time and place
   of meeting, as the said court may direct, shall ascertain and determine the amount
   of compensation to be paid to said owner or owners, and shall make reports to said
   court of their award, on or before the first day of the term next after their appointment:
   Provided, That the said United States shall not be authorized to take possession of
   or use or occupy the lands, buildings or other property taken under the provision
   of this section until the amount of said award shall be paid to the owner or owners
   thereof:  Provided further, That the said court may set aside the report of said viewers,
   upon being satisfied that the amount of said award is excessive or insufficient: 
   And provided further, That, upon the application of any party aggrieved, made within
   thirty days after the filing of the report of the viewers, for an issue to try the
   facts in controversy between the respective parties and to determine the amount of
   compensation due for property condemned and taken or for property injured or destroyed
   by the construction or enlargement of the works and improvements contemplated by this
   act, it shall be the duty of said court to award said issue, and any appeal taken
   pursuant to this act, shall be signed by the party or parties taking the same, or
   by his or their agent or attorney, and shall be accompanied by an affidavit of the
   party appellant, or by his or their agent or attorney, that the same is not taken
   for the purpose of delay, but because the affiant firmly believes that injustice has
   been done.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Lighthouses on Delaware and Schuylkill Rivers›PA ST 74 P.S. § 15. Acquisition of land by United States; consent
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Lighthouses on Delaware and Schuylkill Rivers › PA ST 74 P.S. § 15. Acquisition of land by United States; consent
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 15. Acquisition of land by United States; consent (2023)
content:
The consent of the state of Pennsylvania is hereby given to the acquisition by the
   United States, by purchase or by condemnation, under the laws of this state, of such
   pieces of land situate in the state of Pennsylvania, or the navigable waters within
   the limits of the jurisdiction of the state of Pennsylvania, each piece not to contain
   more than ten acres, as may be selected by the light house board of the United States,
   for the purpose of erecting light houses and beacons on the rivers Delaware and Schuylkill;
   and the said United States shall have, hold, use, occupy and own the said land or
   lands when purchased or acquired, and exercise jurisdiction and control over the same
   and every part thereof, subject to the restrictions hereinafter mentioned.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Lighthouses on Delaware and Schuylkill Rivers›PA ST 74 P.S. § 18. Jurisdiction ceded to United States
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Lighthouses on Delaware and Schuylkill Rivers › PA ST 74 P.S. § 18. Jurisdiction ceded to United States
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 18. Jurisdiction ceded to United States (2023)
content:
The jurisdiction of the state of Pennsylvania in and over the said land or lands,
   when purchased by the United States, shall be and the same is hereby ceded to the
   United States;  but the jurisdiction hereby ceded shall continue no longer than the
   said United States shall own the said land or lands.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Lighthouses on Delaware and Schuylkill Rivers›PA ST 74 P.S. § 16. When Governor authorized to sell or donate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Lighthouses on Delaware and Schuylkill Rivers › PA ST 74 P.S. § 16. When Governor authorized to sell or donate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 16. When Governor authorized to sell or donate (2023)
content:
Whenever the site so selected shall be a shoal or land covered by waters of the said
   rivers not owned by any individual, and owned by or under the jurisdiction of the
   state, the governor of the state of Pennsylvania is hereby authorized to sell or donate
   to the United States so much of the said shoal or bed of the said rivers, as shall
   be required for such purposes, and to execute such assurances as shall be necessary
   to vest the title of the state of Pennsylvania thereto in the United States, and to
   secure the use and occupation of the same to the United States, for the purpose of
   erecting a light house or light houses thereon.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Frankford Arsenal›PA ST 74 P.S. § 52. Frankford Arsenal in Philadelphia
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Frankford Arsenal › PA ST 74 P.S. § 52. Frankford Arsenal in Philadelphia
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 52. Frankford Arsenal in Philadelphia (2023)
content:
Exclusive jurisdiction over the lands so purchased is hereby ceded to the United States
   by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, and said lands shall be exempt from the payment
   of all taxes, State and local:  Provided, That the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania shall
   retain a concurrent jurisdiction with the United States over the lands so acquired
   by the United States, for the purpose of serving all civil processes:  And provided
   further, That such criminal processes as may issue under the authority of the Commonwealth,
   against any person or persons charged with crimes committed without the area so acquired,
   may be executed therein, in the same manner as though this cession had not been granted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Roads at Gettysburg›PA ST 74 P.S. § 36. Jurisdiction of crimes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Roads at Gettysburg › PA ST 74 P.S. § 36. Jurisdiction of crimes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 36. Jurisdiction of crimes (2023)
content:
Provided, further, That all offenses against the criminal laws of Pennsylvania, committed
   upon said road, shall remain as before cognizable in the courts of this Commonwealth;
   but nothing herein contained shall in any wise interfere with the jurisdiction of
   the United States over any matters embraced in the act of congress establishing said
   National Park, approved the eleventh day of February, Anno Domini one thousand eight
   hundred and ninety-five, nor with any laws, rules, or regulations which have been
   or may be adopted by the Government of the United States for the preservation and
   protection of its property and rights in said ceded road, and proper maintenance of
   good order thereon.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Lighthouses on Delaware and Schuylkill Rivers›PA ST 74 P.S. § 20. Jurisdiction ceded, when to vest; exemption from taxation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Lighthouses on Delaware and Schuylkill Rivers › PA ST 74 P.S. § 20. Jurisdiction ceded, when to vest; exemption from taxation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 20. Jurisdiction ceded, when to vest; exemption from taxation (2023)
content:
The jurisdiction hereby ceded shall not vest until the United States shall have acquired
   the title to said land or lands, as herein provided;  and so long as the said land
   or lands shall remain the property of the United States, when acquired as aforesaid,
   and no longer, the same shall be and continue exonerated from all taxes, assessments
   and other charges which may be levied under the authority of this state.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Frankford Arsenal›PA ST 74 P.S. § 51. Land adjoining Frankford Arsenal in Philadelphia
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Frankford Arsenal › PA ST 74 P.S. § 51. Land adjoining Frankford Arsenal in Philadelphia
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 51. Land adjoining Frankford Arsenal in Philadelphia (2023)
content:
The consent of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania is hereby granted to the purchase
   by the government of the United States of certain tracts of land, in all approximately
   twenty-eight acres in extent, adjoining the Frankford Arsenal in the city and county
   of Philadelphia, for an addition to the said arsenal for arsenal purposes;  said tracts
   of land being more particularly described as follows:--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Marine Corps Supply Depot›PA ST 74 P.S. § 41. Land at corner of Broad Street and Washington Avenue, Philadelphia
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Marine Corps Supply Depot › PA ST 74 P.S. § 41. Land at corner of Broad Street and Washington Avenue, Philadelphia
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 41. Land at corner of Broad Street and Washington Avenue, Philadelphia (2023)
content:
When the United States of America shall acquire, by purchase, condemnation, or otherwise,
   the lands, tenements, and hereditaments situate at the southwest corner of Broad Street
   and Washington Avenue, in the county of Philadelphia, now occupied as a depot of supplies
   for the United States Marine Corps, and the other real property contiguous to and
   adjoining the same, not exceeding in all eighty thousand square feet in area, the
   Commonwealth of Pennsylvania hereby cedes jurisdiction over said real estate, so acquired,
   unto the United States of America.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Real Estate of Monongahela Navigation Company›PA ST 74 P.S. § 21. Jurisdiction over real estate of the Monongahela navigation company ceded to the United States
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Real Estate of Monongahela Navigation Company › PA ST 74 P.S. § 21. Jurisdiction over real estate of the Monongahela navigation company ceded to the United States
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 21. Jurisdiction over real estate of the Monongahela navigation company ceded to the United States (2023)
content:
When the United States of America shall acquire by purchase, condemnation or otherwise
   any or all of the real estate belonging to the Monongahela navigation company, consisting
   of locks, dams, abutments, lockhouses or other real estate used in connection with
   the slack-water improvements on the Monongahela river, the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
   hereby cedes to the government of the United States jurisdiction over the said real
   estate so acquired.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Lighthouses on Delaware and Schuylkill Rivers›PA ST 74 P.S. § 19. Conditions upon which consent given and jurisdiction ceded
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Lighthouses on Delaware and Schuylkill Rivers › PA ST 74 P.S. § 19. Conditions upon which consent given and jurisdiction ceded
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 19. Conditions upon which consent given and jurisdiction ceded (2023)
content:
The said consent is given, and the said jurisdiction ceded, upon the express condition
   that the state of Pennsylvania shall retain concurrent jurisdiction with the United
   States in and over the said land or lands, so far as that all civil process in all
   cases, and such criminal or other process as may issue under the laws or authority
   of the state of Pennsylvania, against any person or persons charged with crimes or
   misdemeanors committed within said state, including said lands, may be executed therein
   in the same way and manner as if such consent had not been given or jurisdiction ceded,
   except so far as such process may affect the real or personal property of the United
   States.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Frankford Arsenal›PA ST 74 P.S. § 54. Exclusive jurisdiction, cession of
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Frankford Arsenal › PA ST 74 P.S. § 54. Exclusive jurisdiction, cession of
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 54. Exclusive jurisdiction, cession of (2023)
content:
Exclusive jurisdiction in and over the aforesaid lands is hereby ceded to the United
   States of America by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania for the erection of forts, magazines,
   arsenals, dock yards and other needful buildings, with the exception of roads abutting
   on said lands to be used by the United States for military and other public purposes
   which are not already under the jurisdiction of the United States.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Roads at Gettysburg›PA ST 74 P.S. § 31. Jurisdiction over certain roads at Gettysburg ceded to the United States
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Roads at Gettysburg › PA ST 74 P.S. § 31. Jurisdiction over certain roads at Gettysburg ceded to the United States
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 31. Jurisdiction over certain roads at Gettysburg ceded to the United States (2023)
content:
The jurisdiction of this Commonwealth is hereby ceded to the United States of America
   over the public roads and parts of the same hereinafter specified and described, included
   within the limits of the national park at Gettysburg, as defined by the act of Congress,
   entitled “An act to establish a National Military Park at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania,”
   approved February eleven, one thousand eight hundred and ninety-five,1to wit:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Frankford Arsenal›PA ST 74 P.S. § 55. Civil and criminal process; duration of jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Frankford Arsenal › PA ST 74 P.S. § 55. Civil and criminal process; duration of jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 55. Civil and criminal process; duration of jurisdiction (2023)
content:
The jurisdiction so ceded to the United States of America is granted upon the express
   condition that the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania shall retain concurrent jurisdiction
   with the United States in and over the lands and buildings aforesaid, in so far that
   civil process in all cases and such criminal process as may issue under the authority
   of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania against anyone charged with crime committed outside
   said land, may be executed thereon in the same manner as if this jurisdiction had
   not been ceded.  The United States shall retain such jurisdiction so long as the said land shall
   be used for the purposes for which jurisdiction is ceded and no longer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Roads at Gettysburg›PA ST 74 P.S. § 35. Jurisdiction over part of Emmitsburg road ceded to United States
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Roads at Gettysburg › PA ST 74 P.S. § 35. Jurisdiction over part of Emmitsburg road ceded to United States
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 35. Jurisdiction over part of Emmitsburg road ceded to United States (2023)
content:
The jurisdiction of this Commonwealth is hereby ceded to the United States of America
   over that portion of the public road, known as the Emmitsburg Road, within the limits
   of the National Park at Gettysburg, as defined by the act of Congress, entitled “An
   act to establish a National Military Park at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania,” approved the
   eleventh day of February, Anno Domini one thousand eight hundred and ninety-five,1extending from the borough line, southwesterly, eight thousand two hundred and sixty-three
   feet to the public road known as the Wheatfield Road:  Provided, nevertheless, That
   this cession is upon the express condition that the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania so
   far retains concurrent jurisdiction with the United States, over that part of said
   road which is hereby ceded, as that all civil and criminal process issued under the
   authority of this Commonwealth may be executed thereon, in like manner as if this
   act had not passed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Frankford Arsenal›PA ST 74 P.S. § 56. Taxation of property, persons and franchises
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Frankford Arsenal › PA ST 74 P.S. § 56. Taxation of property, persons and franchises
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 56. Taxation of property, persons and franchises (2023)
content:
The jurisdiction so ceded to the United States shall be upon the further condition
   that the Commonwealth reserves to itself and its political subdivisions whatever power
   of taxation it may constitutionally reserve to levy and collect all taxes now or hereafter
   imposed by the Commonwealth and its political subdivisions upon property, persons
   and franchises within the boundaries so ceded.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Lazaretto on Island of Tinicum›PA ST 74 P.S. § 61. Consent to purchase
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Lazaretto on Island of Tinicum › PA ST 74 P.S. § 61. Consent to purchase
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 61. Consent to purchase (2023)
content:
The consent of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania is hereby granted to the purchase
   by the Government of the United States of a tract of land, with the buildings and
   improvements thereon situate, lying and being on the Island of Tinicum, in the township
   of Tinicum, in the county of Delaware, in the said Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, bounded
   and described as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Frankford Arsenal›PA ST 74 P.S. § 53. Main reservation; consent to acquisition
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Frankford Arsenal › PA ST 74 P.S. § 53. Main reservation; consent to acquisition
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 53. Main reservation; consent to acquisition (2023)
content:
The consent of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania is hereby granted, in accordance with
   the seventeenth clause eighth section of the first article of the Constitution of
   the United States,1to the acquisition by the United States of America of two tracts of land in the City
   and County of Philadelphia, known as the Frankford Arsenal, the first tract known
   as the “Main Reservation” being bounded and described as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Federal Buildings at Wilkes-Barre›PA ST 74 P.S. § 71. Federal government authorized to acquire land in Wilkes-Barre
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Federal Buildings at Wilkes-Barre › PA ST 74 P.S. § 71. Federal government authorized to acquire land in Wilkes-Barre
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 71. Federal government authorized to acquire land in Wilkes-Barre (2023)
content:
The consent of the state of Pennsylvania is hereby given to the acquisition by the
   United States by purchase, or by condemnation under the laws of this state, of one
   or more pieces of land situate in the city of Wilkes-Barre, not exceeding in quantity
   one acre, on which to erect a court-house, post-office, and other government buildings
   and appurtenances, and the said United States shall have, hold, use, occupy and own
   the said land or lands when purchased, and exercise jurisdiction and control over
   the same and every part thereof, subject to the restrictions hereinafter named.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Lazaretto on Island of Tinicum›PA ST 74 P.S. § 62. Jurisdiction ceded
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Lazaretto on Island of Tinicum › PA ST 74 P.S. § 62. Jurisdiction ceded
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 62. Jurisdiction ceded (2023)
content:
The city of Philadelphia is authorized to sell at private sale the said property to
   the United States;  and, upon a conveyance thereof, exclusive jurisdiction over the
   lands so purchased is hereby ceded to the United States by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania,
   and said lands shall be exempt from the payment of all taxes, State and local:  Provided,
   That the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania shall retain a concurrent jurisdiction with
   the United States over the land so acquired by the United States, for the purpose
   of serving all civil processes:  And provided further, That such criminal processes
   as may issue under the authority of the Commonwealth, against any person or persons
   charged with crimes committed without the area so acquired, may be executed therein,
   in the same manner as though this cession had not been granted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Federal Buildings at Wilkes-Barre›PA ST 74 P.S. § 75. Acquiring land by eminent domain proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Federal Buildings at Wilkes-Barre › PA ST 74 P.S. § 75. Acquiring land by eminent domain proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 75. Acquiring land by eminent domain proceedings (2023)
content:
In case the United States shall decide to resort to condemnation or appropriation
   under the right of eminent domain, in acquiring land for the purposes specified in
   this act, it shall be lawful for the United States so to acquire said land:  Provided,
   That the United States may pay the costs and refuse to take the land, if in their
   judgment the compensation assessed therefor is excessive.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Federal Buildings at Wilkes-Barre›PA ST 74 P.S. § 72. Time jurisdiction vests; exoneration from taxes, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Federal Buildings at Wilkes-Barre › PA ST 74 P.S. § 72. Time jurisdiction vests; exoneration from taxes, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 72. Time jurisdiction vests; exoneration from taxes, etc. (2023)
content:
The jurisdiction ceded by the said state of Pennsylvania shall vest in the United
   States as soon as the United States shall have acquired title to said land or lands
   by purchase or grant, by condemnation or by lawful appropriation under the right of
   eminent domain, and so long as said land or lands remain the property of the United
   States, when acquired as aforesaid, and no longer, the same shall be and continue
   exonerated from all taxes, assessments and other charges which may be levied or imposed
   under the authority of this state.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Federal Buildings at Wilkes-Barre›PA ST 74 P.S. § 76. Punishment for injuring grounds, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Federal Buildings at Wilkes-Barre › PA ST 74 P.S. § 76. Punishment for injuring grounds, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 76. Punishment for injuring grounds, etc. (2023)
content:
It is further enacted that any malicious, wilful, reckless or voluntary injury to,
   or mutilation of, the grounds, buildings or appurtenances, shall subject the offender
   or offenders to a fine of not less than twenty dollars, to which may be added, for
   an aggravated offense, imprisonment not exceeding six months in the county jail or
   workhouse, to be prosecuted before any court of competent jurisdiction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Federal Buildings at Wilkes-Barre›PA ST 74 P.S. § 74. State to retain concurrent jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Federal Buildings at Wilkes-Barre › PA ST 74 P.S. § 74. State to retain concurrent jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 74. State to retain concurrent jurisdiction (2023)
content:
The said consent is given, and the said jurisdiction ceded, upon the express condition
   that the state of Pennsylvania shall retain concurrent jurisdiction with the United
   States in and over the land or lands, so far as that all civil process, in all cases,
   and such criminal and other process as may issue under the laws or authority of the
   state of Pennsylvania, against any person or persons charged with crimes or misdemeanors
   committed within said state, including said lands, may be executed in the same way
   and manner as if such consent had not been given or jurisdiction ceded, except so
   far as such process may affect the real or personal property of the United States.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Carlisle Indian School Farm›PA ST 74 P.S. § 81. Land in Cumberland County
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Carlisle Indian School Farm › PA ST 74 P.S. § 81. Land in Cumberland County
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 81. Land in Cumberland County (2023)
content:
The consent of the state of Pennsylvania is hereby given to the acquisition by the
   United States, under the laws of this state, of a certain farm or tract of land, from
   Christopher C. Kutz, situate in the township of North Middleton and Middlesex, county
   of Cumberland;  bounded on the west by Henderson's farm, on the north by Hackenberger's
   farm, on the east by Charles Kutz's farm, and on the south by the Witmer farm, county
   farm and Huston farm, containing one hundred and seventy-five acres, more or less--on
   which to instruct the pupils of the Carlisle Indian industrial school in the avocation
   of agriculture;  and the said United States shall have and hold, use, occupy and own
   the said land, and exercise control over the same, and every part thereof, subject
   to the restrictions hereinafter mentioned.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Carlisle Indian School Farm›PA ST 74 P.S. § 86. State to have concurrent jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Carlisle Indian School Farm › PA ST 74 P.S. § 86. State to have concurrent jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 86. State to have concurrent jurisdiction (2023)
content:
The jurisdiction, so ceded to the United States of America, is granted upon the express
   condition that the said State of Pennsylvania shall retain concurrent jurisdiction
   with the United States in and over the tracts of land aforesaid, in so far that civil
   process in all cases, and such criminal process as may issue under the authority of
   the State of Pennsylvania against any person or persons charged with crimes committed
   outside the limits of said lands, may be executed thereon in the same way and manner
   as if this jurisdiction had not been ceded.  The United States shall retain such jurisdiction so long as the said tracts or parcels
   of land shall be used for the purposes for which jurisdiction is ceded, and no longer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Federal Buildings at Wilkes-Barre›PA ST 74 P.S. § 73. Jurisdiction ceded to United States
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Federal Buildings at Wilkes-Barre › PA ST 74 P.S. § 73. Jurisdiction ceded to United States
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 73. Jurisdiction ceded to United States (2023)
content:
The jurisdiction of the state of Pennsylvania in and over the said land or lands,
   when purchased or taken by the United States, shall be and the same is hereby ceded
   to the United States;  but the jurisdiction hereby ceded shall continue no longer
   than the said United States shall own the said land or lands.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Carlisle Indian School Farm›PA ST 74 P.S. § 87. Additional lands, jurisdiction to be ceded
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Carlisle Indian School Farm › PA ST 74 P.S. § 87. Additional lands, jurisdiction to be ceded
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 87. Additional lands, jurisdiction to be ceded (2023)
content:
If at any time hereafter, any additional lands adjoining those above described shall
   be purchased by the United States for use of the said Carlisle Barracks Military Reservation
   or the New Cumberland General Depot, respectively, or for any other military purpose,
   this act shall be construed to vest in the United States jurisdiction over such additional
   lands to the same extent as is vested by this act over the tracts or parcels above
   described.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Carlisle Indian School Farm›PA ST 74 P.S. § 84. Punishment for injuries to grounds, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Carlisle Indian School Farm › PA ST 74 P.S. § 84. Punishment for injuries to grounds, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 84. Punishment for injuries to grounds, etc. (2023)
content:
Any wilful injury to the grounds, buildings or appurtenances, aforesaid, shall be
   punishable in any court of competent jurisdiction, as like misdemeanors are now punishable
   under the laws of Pennsylvania.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Land in O'hara Township›PA ST 74 P.S. § 92. Jurisdiction of United States and Commonwealth
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Land in O'hara Township › PA ST 74 P.S. § 92. Jurisdiction of United States and Commonwealth
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 92. Jurisdiction of United States and Commonwealth (2023)
content:
Exclusive jurisdiction over the lands so purchased is hereby ceded to the United States
   by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, and said lands shall be exempt from the payment
   of all taxes, State and local:  Provided, That the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania shall
   retain a concurrent jurisdiction with the United States, over the lands so acquired
   by the United States, for the purpose of serving of all civil processes:  And provided
   further, That such criminal processes as may issue under the authority of the Commonwealth,
   against any person or persons charged with crimes committed without the area so acquired,
   may be executed therein, in the same manner as though this cession had not been granted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Carlisle Indian School Farm›PA ST 74 P.S. § 82. State to have concurrent jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Carlisle Indian School Farm › PA ST 74 P.S. § 82. State to have concurrent jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 82. State to have concurrent jurisdiction (2023)
content:
The said consent is given, and the said jurisdiction ceded, upon the express condition
   that the state of Pennsylvania shall have concurrent jurisdiction with the United
   States on and over the said ground or lands, so far as that all civil process in all
   cases, and such criminal or other process as may issue under the laws or authority
   of the state of Pennsylvania against any person or persons charged with any crime
   or misdemeanor committed within this state, including said farm or tract of land,
   may be executed therein in the same manner as if the consent had not been given or
   jurisdiction ceded, except so far as such process may affect the real or personal
   property of the United States.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Carlisle Indian School Farm›PA ST 74 P.S. § 85. Carlisle Barracks Military Reservation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Carlisle Indian School Farm › PA ST 74 P.S. § 85. Carlisle Barracks Military Reservation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 85. Carlisle Barracks Military Reservation (2023)
content:
The jurisdiction of the State of Pennsylvania is hereby ceded to the United States
   of America, for the occupation and use, for purposes of national defense, and for
   the erection and maintenance of the necessary buildings for the military or other
   public use of the United States, over all the lands now embraced within the boundaries
   of Carlisle Barracks Military Reservation, situate in Cumberland County, State of
   Pennsylvania, excepting roads abutting on said reservation, and that portion of the
   Carlisle-Harrisburg turnpike located within the boundaries thereof;  and over all
   that tract of land comprising the New Cumberland General Depot, situate in York County,
   State of Pennsylvania, excepting roads abutting thereon, and those portions of the
   Marsh Run Road which lie within the boundaries thereof, and that portion of U.S. Highway
   No. 111 (old State Highway No. 333), which extends across the southeast corner for
   a distance of approximately two hundred seventy and one-half (2701/2) feet.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Land in Fairview Township, York County›PA ST 74 P.S. § 95. Conveyance to Federal Government authorized
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Land in Fairview Township, York County › PA ST 74 P.S. § 95. Conveyance to Federal Government authorized
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 95. Conveyance to Federal Government authorized (2023)
content:
The Secretary of Property and Supplies,1with the approval of the Governor of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, is hereby
   authorized to convey to the United States of America title to the following described
   lands:  All that certain plot of ground situate in the Township of Fairview, and County
   of York, beginning at a point at the intersection of the lands owned by the Commonwealth
   of Pennsylvania and the lands owned by W. J. Stonesifer;  thence north 57°27 minutes
   west for a distance of 911.47 feet along the lands of W. J. Stonesifer;  thence along
   the lands of the Newton Ryder tract following four courses, north 40°091/2minutes east a distance of 115.95 feet, north 58° 551/2minutes west a distance of 674.90 feet;  thence north 40°051/2minutes east a distance of 219.42 feet;  thence north 54° 19 minutes west a distance
   of 809.25 feet to the lands owned by the United States Government;  thence along the
   lands of the United States Government north 35°22 minutes east a distance of 910.90
   feet to a point in the Marsh Run Road;  thence along the said Marsh Run Road and along
   the lands owned by the United States Government, the following nine courses:  south
   55°06 minutes east a distance of 291.48 feet;  thence south 53°59 minutes east a distance
   of 624.47 feet;  thence south 58°27 minutes east a distance of 925.00 feet;  thence
   south 55°541/2minutes east a distance of 173.30 feet;  thence south 40°201/2minutes east a distance of 143.34 feet;  thence south 15°561/2minutes east a distance of 403.83 feet;  thence south 23°57 minutes east a distance
   of 700.00 feet;  thence south 40°111/2minutes east a distance of 260.00 feet;  thence south 46°281/2minutes east a distance of 150.00 feet to a point in Marsh Run Road;  thence along
   the lands of the United States Government, south 41°311/2minutes west a distance of 280.00 feet to a point at the intersection of the lands
   of the United States Government and the lands of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania;
   thence along the lands of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, north 65°53 minutes 08
   seconds west a distance of 1078.88 feet, to the point of beginning, comprising a tract
   of 72.96 acres neat measure, this conveyance being made pursuant to an agreement between
   the Secretary of War of the United States of America and the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania,
   dated May twenty-ninth, one thousand nine hundred thirty-six.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Carlisle Indian School Farm›PA ST 74 P.S. § 83. Time jurisdiction vests; exoneration from taxes, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Carlisle Indian School Farm › PA ST 74 P.S. § 83. Time jurisdiction vests; exoneration from taxes, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 83. Time jurisdiction vests; exoneration from taxes, etc. (2023)
content:
The jurisdiction hereby ceded shall not vest until the United States shall have acquired
   the title to said land, and shall continue so long as the said land shall remain the
   property of the United States, and no longer, and the same shall be and continue,
   while so held, exonerated from all taxes, assessments and other charges which may
   be levied under the authority of the state of Pennsylvania.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Land in Fairview Township, York County›PA ST 74 P.S. § 96. Evidence of title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Land in Fairview Township, York County › PA ST 74 P.S. § 96. Evidence of title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 96. Evidence of title (2023)
content:
The Governor of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania is authorized to furnish the Attorney
   General of the United States, without cost to the United States, such evidences of
   a valid title to the aforesaid lands as may be necessary to permit the said Attorney
   General to approve said title.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Land in O'hara Township›PA ST 74 P.S. § 91. Federal government authorized to acquire land in O'Hara Township, Allegheny County; purpose
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Land in O'hara Township › PA ST 74 P.S. § 91. Federal government authorized to acquire land in O'Hara Township, Allegheny County; purpose
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 91. Federal government authorized to acquire land in O'Hara Township, Allegheny County; purpose (2023)
content:
The consent of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania is hereby granted to the purchase
   by the Government of the United States of a certain tract of land, containing approximately

   use in the care and treatment of discharged sick and disabled soldiers, or for other
   uses of the United States;  said tract of land being situate in O'Hara Township, Allegheny
   County, Pennsylvania, and bounded and described as follows, to wit:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Land for President's Home›PA ST 74 P.S. § 103. Highway to lands
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Land for President's Home › PA ST 74 P.S. § 103. Highway to lands
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 103. Highway to lands (2023)
content:
As of the date of the grant and conveyance aforesaid, a State highway is hereby established
   the route of which shall be as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Land for President's Home›PA ST 74 P.S. § 102. Jurisdiction over land; exemption from taxation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Land for President's Home › PA ST 74 P.S. § 102. Jurisdiction over land; exemption from taxation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 102. Jurisdiction over land; exemption from taxation (2023)
content:
As of the date of the grant and conveyance aforesaid, the exclusive jurisdiction over
   the lands so granted and conveyed is hereby ceded to the United States of America
   by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania;  and said lands shall be exempt from the payment
   of all taxes, State and local:  Provided, That the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania shall
   retain a concurrent jurisdiction with the United States over the land so granted and
   conveyed for the purpose of serving all civic processes:  And provided further, That
   such criminal processes as may issue under the authority of the Commonwealth against
   any person or persons charged with crimes or misdemeanors committed without the area
   so granted and conveyed may be executed therein in the same manner as though this
   cession had not been made.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Land for President's Home›PA ST 74 P.S. § 101. Land for home for President may be ceded to United States
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Land for President's Home › PA ST 74 P.S. § 101. Land for home for President may be ceded to United States
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 101. Land for home for President may be ceded to United States (2023)
content:
Subject to the terms and conditions and limitation in this act contained, the Governor
   of this Commonwealth, for and in behalf of, and in the name of, this Commonwealth,
   be and he is hereby authorized and empowered to grant and convey unto the United States
   of America a tract of land, not to exceed one thousand acres in area, to be selected
   by the duly authorized officers and agents of the United States of America from any
   lands heretofore reserved or acquired and now owned and held for forest reserves,
   to be used for erecting thereon a dwelling and home for the President of the United
   States, and such other buildings and improvements as may be deemed incidental and
   necessary for the proper maintenance of such dwelling and home, for the purchase price
   therefor of one cent for each acre of land so granted and conveyed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Land for President's Home›PA ST 74 P.S. § 105. Cost of highway
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Land for President's Home › PA ST 74 P.S. § 105. Cost of highway

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Land in Fairview Township, York County›PA ST 74 P.S. § 97. Jurisdiction ceded; exemption from taxation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Land in Fairview Township, York County › PA ST 74 P.S. § 97. Jurisdiction ceded; exemption from taxation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 97. Jurisdiction ceded; exemption from taxation (2023)
content:
The consent of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania is hereby given, in accordance with
   the seventeenth clause, eighth section, of the first article of the Constitution of
   the United States,1to the acquisition by the United States of the aforesaid lands;  and exclusive jurisdiction
   in and over the aforesaid lands, when acquired by the United States, is hereby ceded
   to the United States for all purposes except the service thereon of all civil and
   criminal processes of the courts of this Commonwealth;  but the jurisdiction so ceded
   shall continue no longer than the said United States shall own such lands;  and so
   long as the said lands shall remain the property of the United States, and no longer,
   the same shall be and continue exempt and exonerated from all State, county, and municipal
   assessment, taxation, or other charges which may be levied or imposed under the authority
   of this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Land for President's Home›PA ST 74 P.S. § 106. Jurisdiction over highway
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Land for President's Home › PA ST 74 P.S. § 106. Jurisdiction over highway
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 106. Jurisdiction over highway (2023)
content:
On and after the grant and conveyance aforesaid, and upon the acceptance of the same
   by the United States of America, the exclusive jurisdiction over the highway herein
   established is hereby ceded to the United States of America by the Commonwealth of
   Pennsylvania:  Provided, That this cession is made upon the express condition that
   the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania so far retains concurrent jurisdiction with the United
   States over said highway as that all civil and criminal process issued under the authority
   of this Commonwealth may be executed thereon in like manner as if this cession had
   not been made:  And provided further, That all offenses against the criminal laws
   of Pennsylvania, committed upon said highway, shall remain, as before cognizable in
   the courts of this Commonwealth;  but nothing herein contained shall in any wise interfere
   with the right and power and jurisdiction of the United States to enact and enforce
   laws for the protection of said highway, and for the protection and comfort of travelers
   on said highway, and for insuring unto the President of the United States, his family,
   his officers and agents, and his guests, free and unobstructed and safe passage over
   and along said highway.

content:

   Crawford County, Pennsylvania, known as the Keystone Ordnance Plant, bounded and described

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 120.32. Cession of exclusive jurisdiction; roads excepted (2023)
content:
Exclusive jurisdiction in and over the aforesaid lands is hereby ceded to the United
   States of America by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, for the erection of forts,
   magazines, arsenals, dock yards and other needful buildings, with the exception of
   roads abutting on said lands to be used by the United States for military and other
   public purposes, which are not already under the jurisdiction of the United States.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States›Keystone Ordnance Plant›PA ST 74 P.S. § 120.33. Civil and criminal process; duration of jurisdiction of United States
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 1. Land and Jurisdiction Ceded to the United States › Keystone Ordnance Plant › PA ST 74 P.S. § 120.33. Civil and criminal process; duration of jurisdiction of United States
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 120.33. Civil and criminal process; duration of jurisdiction of United States (2023)
content:
The jurisdiction so ceded to the United States of America is granted upon the express
   condition that the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania shall retain concurrent jurisdiction
   with the United States in and over the lands and buildings aforesaid, in so far that
   civil process in all cases and such criminal process as may issue under the authority
   of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, against anyone charged with crime committed outside
   said land may be executed thereon in the same manner as if this jurisdiction had not
   been ceded.  The United States shall retain such jurisdiction so long as the said land shall
   be used for the purposes for which jurisdiction is ceded, and no longer.

content:
This conveyance is made to the grantee upon the express condition that if the grantee
   shall cease to use the above described premises for National Cemetery purposes, or
   shall alienate or attempt to alienate such land, title thereto shall, at the option
   of the grantor, revert to the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, provided, however, if
   permanent improvements or facilities relating to the National Cemetery are erected
   on the land, including but not limited to interment, memorial, administration, maintenance
   and visitor improvements or facilities, service roads, drainage and sprinkling systems,
   and grading and landscaping, this right of reverter will terminate immediately upon
   the expenditure of any funds appropriated for the construction of any such improvements
   or facilities with respect to the land so improved and such additional land within
   the acreage hereby transferred as may be reasonably required by the grantee to protect
   the integrity of the area being developed, which portion of land shall be described
   and set forth in a document to be prepared and recorded by the grantee for each phase
   of development of the said National Cemetery.

content:
The Department of Environmental Resources and The General State Authority, with the
   approval of the Governor, are hereby authorized on behalf of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
   to lease to the Government of the United States of America for use as a National Park,
   the tracts of land hereinafter described in section 2 of this act;1such land situate in the City and County of Philadelphia and the Commonwealth of
   Pennsylvania.  Said lease shall be for a period of five years, and from year to year thereafter,
   for a consideration of one dollar ($1) per year, until such time as all bonds issued
   with respect to said tracts by The General State Authority of the Commonwealth of
   Pennsylvania are retired.

content:
Any person employed under and by virtue of any1act of congress of the United States, passed the tenth day of February, 1807, and
   of the supplements thereto,2or under the direction of congress, to form a geodetic connection between the Atlantic
   and Pacific coasts, and to furnish triangulation points for state surveys, may enter
   upon lands within this state, for the purpose of exploring, triangulating, leveling,
   surveying, and of doing any other work which may be necessary to carry out the objects
   of said laws, and may erect any works, stations, buildings and appendages requisite
   for that purpose, doing no unnecessary injury thereby.

   thereby, either of them may petition the court of common pleas in the county in which
   the land is situated, which court shall appoint a time for a hearing as soon as may

   witnesses, and assess damages.

   Commonwealth reserves to itself and its political subdivisions such power of taxation
   as it may constitutionally reserve, to levy and collect all taxes now or hereafter
   imposed by the Commonwealth and its political subdivisions upon property, persons
   and franchises within the boundaries so ceded.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 2. United States Coast Survey›PA ST 74 P.S. § 124. Costs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 2. United States Coast Survey › PA ST 74 P.S. § 124. Costs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 124. Costs (2023)
content:
The costs to be allowed in all such cases shall be the same as allowed according to
   rules by the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 2. United States Coast Survey›PA ST 74 P.S. § 123. Tender of amends
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 2. United States Coast Survey › PA ST 74 P.S. § 123. Tender of amends
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 123. Tender of amends (2023)
content:
The party so entering upon land may tender to the party injured amends therefor, and
   if, in case of application to the court of common pleas by the party injured, the
   damages finally assessed do not exceed the amount tendered, the party making said
   application shall not recover costs, otherwise the prevailing party shall recover
   costs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 2. United States Coast Survey›PA ST 74 P.S. § 125. Penalty for injuring works
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 2. United States Coast Survey › PA ST 74 P.S. § 125. Penalty for injuring works
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 125. Penalty for injuring works (2023)
content:
If any person shall wilfully deface, injure or remove any signal monument, building
   or other property of the United States coast survey, constructed or used under or
   by virtue of the acts of congress aforesaid, he shall forfeit a sum not exceeding
   fifty dollars for each offense, and shall be liable for damages sustained by the United
   States in consequence of such defacing, injury or removal, or be recovered in action
   on the case in any court of competent jurisdiction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 2. United States Coast Survey›PA ST 74 P.S. § 127. Damages to owner
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 2. United States Coast Survey › PA ST 74 P.S. § 127. Damages to owner
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 127. Damages to owner (2023)
content:
The engineer or surveyor, or his duly accredited assistants or representatives, shall
   do no unnecessary damage to the property on which a survey station stands.  The owner of the land shall be reimbursed for all damage done in so entering, the
   amount of damages to be agreed upon before hand and paid promptly upon completion
   of work at said survey station.  Where the amount of damages to be paid has not been or can not be agreed upon beforehand,
   the party proposing to enter upon said property shall file good and sufficient bond
   in the court of quarter sessions of the county in an amount to be approved by the
   court, conditioned for the payment of all damages and costs when the same are finally
   ascertained and fixed.  The amount of damages to be paid shall be determined by three viewers of the county
   in which the property is located, appointed by the court of quarter sessions from
   the county board of viewers.  The proceedings for the ascertainment of damages shall be in accordance with the
   general road laws of the Commonwealth for the ascertainment of damages for the taking,
   injuring or destruction of property in the laying out and opening of public roads.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 2. United States Coast Survey›PA ST 74 P.S. § 126. Engineers and surveyors may enter upon private lands
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 2. United States Coast Survey › PA ST 74 P.S. § 126. Engineers and surveyors may enter upon private lands
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 126. Engineers and surveyors may enter upon private lands (2023)
content:
Any person duly registered as a qualified engineer or surveyor under the laws of this
   Commonwealth or entitled to exemption from registration as an engineer or surveyor
   under the laws of this Commonwealth, and his duly accredited assistants and representatives
   may, in the execution of surveys, enter upon any private land whereon there is a marked
   survey station for which the horizontal or vertical position has been determined by
   or under the direction of the United States Coast and Geodetic Survey, or which is
   a part of the Pennsylvania Coordinate System, if such entry is for the purpose of
   utilizing the horizontal or vertical position data in controlling surveys of land
   for cadastral purposes, or for other engineering purposes, private or public.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 3A. Uniform Federal Lien Registration Act › PA ST 74 P.S. § 157-3. Place of filing

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 3A. Uniform Federal Lien Registration Act › PA ST 74 P.S. § 157-5. Duties of filing officer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 157-5. Duties of filing officer (2023)
content:
(a) Notice of Federal lien.--If a notice of Federal lien, a refiling of a notice of Federal lien or a notice of
      revocation of any certificate described in subsection (b) is presented to the filing
      officer described in section 3, he shall endorse thereon his identification and the
      date and time of receipt and forthwith file it alphabetically, or enter it in an alphabetical
      index, showing the name and address of the person named in the notice, the date and
      time of receipt, the title and address of the official or entity certifying the lien
      and the total amount appearing on the notice of lien.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 2. United States Coast Survey›PA ST 74 P.S. § 128. Costs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 2. United States Coast Survey › PA ST 74 P.S. § 128. Costs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 128. Costs (2023)
content:
Where the engineer or surveyor or his representatives entering on private property
   for the purposes stated in section 1 of this act,1shall tender damages to owner of said property and said proffer is not accepted,
   and the amount of damages determined according to procedure stated in section 2 of
   this act,2shall not exceed amount of damages so proffered, then all costs in the matter shall
   be borne by the owner of the property, otherwise the cost shall be assessed against
   the party entering.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 2. United States Coast Survey›PA ST 74 P.S. § 129. Penalty for defacing survey mark
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 2. United States Coast Survey › PA ST 74 P.S. § 129. Penalty for defacing survey mark
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 129. Penalty for defacing survey mark (2023)
content:
If any person shall wilfully injure, deface or destroy the mark or monument at any
   survey station established by or under the direction of the United States Coast and
   Geodetic Survey, or by the State Agency administering the Pennsylvania Coordinate
   System, or shall offer any obstacles to the proper, reasonable, and legal use of any
   such station, such person shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction thereof,
   shall be sentenced to pay a fine not to exceed $250 for each offence and costs, or
   shall be imprisoned for a term of not less than 6 months, or both, in the discretion
   of the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 3A. Uniform Federal Lien Registration Act›PA ST 74 P.S. § 157-4. Execution of notices and certificates
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 3A. Uniform Federal Lien Registration Act › PA ST 74 P.S. § 157-4. Execution of notices and certificates

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 74 P.S. United States›Chapter 7. Real ID Compliance Act›PA ST 74 P.S. § 403. Participation in the REAL ID Act of 2005
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 P.S. United States › Chapter 7. Real ID Compliance Act › PA ST 74 P.S. § 403. Participation in the REAL ID Act of 2005
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 P.S. § 403. Participation in the REAL ID Act of 2005 (2023)
content:
The department and any other Commonwealth agency shall comply with the REAL ID Act
   of 20051and regulations promulgated under that act.  In complying with the requirements of the REAL ID Act of 2005, the department shall
   provide an eligible applicant with an option to obtain either a standard-issued driver's
   license or photo identification card or a REAL ID.  The department shall provide the applicant with a brief description that reasonably
   describes the content, requirements and restrictions of a standard-issued driver's
   license or photo identification card or a REAL ID.

(a) Initial report.--Within 90 days of the effective date of this section, the department shall present
      an initial report to the individuals listed under subsection (c) providing details
      on estimated costs associated with the implementation and maintenance of all requirements
      for compliance with the REAL ID Act of 2005,1as determined by the United States Department of Homeland Security.  The report shall also include all estimated initial and recurring costs to establish
      and maintain a two-tiered system which allows individuals to apply for either a REAL
      ID or a standard-issued driver's license or photo identification card.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 74 Pa.C.S.A. Transportation › Part II. Public Transportation › Chapter 15. Sustainable Mobility Options › PA ST 74 Pa.C.S.A. § 1510.1. State Safety Oversight Office
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 74 Pa.C.S.A. § 1510.1. State Safety Oversight Office (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment.--The State Safety Oversight Office is established in the department and shall be under
      the jurisdiction of the secretary.  The secretary, in consultation with the Federal Transit Administration, shall determine
      an appropriate staffing level for the SSO Office that is commensurate with the number,
      size and complexity of fixed guideway public transportation systems in this Commonwealth.  The SSO Office shall adhere to and have the authority and capability to perform
      and enforce the provisions and functions specified under this section,49 U.S.C. § 5329(relating to public transportation safety program) and the associated Federal regulations
      set forth and adopted for oversight for each fixed guideway public transportation
      system.

      that permits full cooperation between Federal, State and local governments, agencies
      and instrumentalities, local transportation organizations and private interests, so
      as to result in as effective and economical a program as possible.
