citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3306. Limitations on driving on left side of roadway (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No vehicle shall be driven on the left side of the roadway under any of the following
      conditions:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3308. One-way roadways and rotary traffic islands
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3308. One-way roadways and rotary traffic islands
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3308. One-way roadways and rotary traffic islands (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment and marking.--The department and local authorities with respect to highways under their respective
      jurisdictions may designate any highway, roadway, part of a roadway or specific lanes
      upon which vehicular traffic shall proceed in one direction at all or such times as
      shall be indicated by official traffic-control devices.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3304. Overtaking vehicle on the right
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3304. Overtaking vehicle on the right
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3304. Overtaking vehicle on the right (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The driver of a vehicle may overtake and pass upon the right of another vehicle only
      under one of the following conditions:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3311. Driving on divided highways
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3311. Driving on divided highways
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3311. Driving on divided highways (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Whenever any highway has been divided into two or more roadways by leaving an intervening
      space, physical barrier or clearly indicated dividing section so constructed as to
      impede vehicular traffic, every vehicle shall be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
      unless directed or permitted to use another roadway by official traffic-control devices,
      police officers or appropriately attired persons authorized to direct, control or
      regulate traffic.  No vehicle shall be driven over, across or within any such dividing space, barrier
      or section except through an opening in the physical barrier or dividing section or
      space or at a crossover or intersection as established.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3327. Duty of driver in emergency response areas and in relation to disabled vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3327. Duty of driver in emergency response areas and in relation to disabled vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3327. Duty of driver in emergency response areas and in relation to disabled vehicles (2023)
content:
(a) Emergency response areas.--When approaching or passing an emergency response area, a person, unless otherwise
      directed by an emergency service responder, shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3322. Vehicle turning left
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3322. Vehicle turning left
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3322. Vehicle turning left (2023)
content:
The driver of a vehicle intending to turn left within an intersection or into an alley,
   private road or driveway shall yield the right-of-way to any vehicle approaching from
   the opposite direction which is so close as to constitute a hazard.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3314. Prohibiting use of hearing impairment devices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3314. Prohibiting use of hearing impairment devices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3314. Prohibiting use of hearing impairment devices (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No driver shall operate a vehicle while wearing or using one or more headphones or
      earphones.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3321. Vehicle approaching or entering intersection
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3321. Vehicle approaching or entering intersection
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3321. Vehicle approaching or entering intersection (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--When two vehicles approach or enter an intersection from different highways at approximately
      the same time, the driver of the vehicle on the left shall yield the right-of-way
      to the vehicle on the right.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3312. Limited access highway entrances and exits
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3312. Limited access highway entrances and exits
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3312. Limited access highway entrances and exits (2023)
content:
No person shall drive a vehicle onto or from any limited access highway except at
   such entrances and exits as are established by public authority.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3315. Passing and overtaking streetcars
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3315. Passing and overtaking streetcars
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3315. Passing and overtaking streetcars (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Notwithstanding any other provision of this subchapter, the driver of a vehicle may
      not overtake and pass to the left of a streetcar proceeding in the same direction,
      whether the streetcar is actually in motion or temporarily halted to receive or discharge
      passengers, if overtaking or passing requires driving in a lane normally used by traffic
      moving in the opposite direction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3316. Prohibiting text-based communications
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3316. Prohibiting text-based communications
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3316. Prohibiting text-based communications (2023)
content:
(a) Prohibition.--No driver shall operate a motor vehicle on a highway or trafficway in this Commonwealth
      while using an interactive mobile device to send, read or write a text-based communication
      while the vehicle is in motion.  A person does not send, read or write a text-based communication when the person
      reads, selects or enters a telephone number or name in an interactive mobile device
      for the purpose of activating or deactivating a voice communication or a telephone
      call.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3316.1. Prohibiting use of interactive mobile device
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3316.1. Prohibiting use of interactive mobile device
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3316.1. Prohibiting use of interactive mobile device (2023)
content:
(a) Motor vehicle.--Except as provided under subsection (b), no driver shall use an interactive mobile
      device while driving a motor vehicle.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3324. Vehicle entering or crossing roadway
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3324. Vehicle entering or crossing roadway
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3324. Vehicle entering or crossing roadway (2023)
content:
The driver of a vehicle about to enter or cross a roadway from any place other than
   another roadway shall yield the right-of-way to all vehicles approaching on the roadway
   to be entered or crossed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3326. Duty of driver in construction and maintenance areas or on highway safety corridors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3326. Duty of driver in construction and maintenance areas or on highway safety corridors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3326. Duty of driver in construction and maintenance areas or on highway safety corridors (2023)
content:
(a) Areas indicated by traffic-control devices.--The driver of a vehicle shall yield the right-of-way to any authorized vehicle or
      pedestrian actually engaged in work upon a highway within any highway or utility construction
      or maintenance area indicated by official traffic-control devices placed in accordance
      with department regulations, including advanced warning signs or a vehicle having
      flashing or revolving yellow lights.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3325. Duty of driver on approach of emergency vehicle
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3325. Duty of driver on approach of emergency vehicle
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3325. Duty of driver on approach of emergency vehicle (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Upon the immediate approach of an emergency vehicle making use of an audible signal
      and visual signals meeting the requirements and standards set forth in regulations
      adopted by the department, the driver of every other vehicle shall yield the right-of-way
      and shall immediately drive to a position parallel to, and as close as possible to,
      the right-hand edge or curb of the roadway clear of any intersection and shall stop
      and remain in that position until the emergency vehicle has passed, except when otherwise
      directed by a police officer or an appropriately attired person authorized to direct,
      control or regulate traffic.  On one-way roadways a driver may comply by driving to the edge or curb which is
      nearest to the lane in which he is traveling.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3328. Unmarked police vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3328. Unmarked police vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3328. Unmarked police vehicles (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The Pennsylvania State Police, in consultation with the department, shall promulgate
      regulations for the use of unmarked vehicles by police officers.  The regulations shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3329. Duty of driver in litter enforcement corridors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter B. Right-Of-Way › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3329. Duty of driver in litter enforcement corridors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3329. Duty of driver in litter enforcement corridors (2023)
content:
(a) Areas indicated by traffic-control devices.--The driver of a vehicle shall yield the right-of-way to any authorized vehicle or
      pedestrian actually engaged in work upon a highway within a litter enforcement corridor
      indicated by official traffic-control devices placed in accordance with department
      regulations, including advanced warning signs or a vehicle having flashing or revolving
      yellow lights.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter C. Turning, Starting and Signals›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3333. Moving stopped or parked vehicle
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter C. Turning, Starting and Signals › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3333. Moving stopped or parked vehicle
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3333. Moving stopped or parked vehicle (2023)
content:
No person shall move a vehicle which is stopped, standing or parked unless and until
   the movement can be made with safety.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter C. Turning, Starting and Signals›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3334. Turning movements and required signals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter C. Turning, Starting and Signals › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3334. Turning movements and required signals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3334. Turning movements and required signals (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Upon a roadway no person shall turn a vehicle or move from one traffic lane to another
      or enter the traffic stream from a parked position unless and until the movement can
      be made with reasonable safety nor without giving an appropriate signal in the manner
      provided in this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter C. Turning, Starting and Signals›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3331. Required position and method of turning
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter C. Turning, Starting and Signals › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3331. Required position and method of turning
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3331. Required position and method of turning (2023)
content:
(a) Right turn.--The driver of a vehicle intending to turn right shall approach the turn and make the
      turn as close as practicable to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter C. Turning, Starting and Signals›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3335. Signals by hand and arm or signal lamps
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter C. Turning, Starting and Signals › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3335. Signals by hand and arm or signal lamps
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3335. Signals by hand and arm or signal lamps (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Any stop or turn signal shall be given either by means of the hand and arm or by signal
      lamps, except as otherwise provided in subsection (b).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter C. Turning, Starting and Signals›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3332. Limitations on turning around
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter C. Turning, Starting and Signals › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3332. Limitations on turning around
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3332. Limitations on turning around (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The driver of any vehicle shall not turn the vehicle so as to proceed in the opposite
      direction unless the movement can be made in safety and without interfering with other
      traffic.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter C. Turning, Starting and Signals›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3336. Method of giving hand and arm signals

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3336. Method of giving hand and arm signals (2023)
content:
All signals given by hand and arm shall be given from the left side of the vehicle
   in the following manner except as indicated for pedalcycles and motorcycles and the
   signals shall indicate as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter D. Special Stops Required›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3341. Obedience to signal indicating approach of train
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter D. Special Stops Required › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3341. Obedience to signal indicating approach of train
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3341. Obedience to signal indicating approach of train (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Whenever any person driving a vehicle approaches a railroad grade crossing under any
      of the circumstances stated in this section, the driver of the vehicle shall stop
      within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail of the railroad and
      shall not proceed until it can be done safely.  The foregoing requirements shall apply upon the occurrence of any of the following
      circumstances:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter D. Special Stops Required›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3342. Vehicles required to stop at railroad crossings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter D. Special Stops Required › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3342. Vehicles required to stop at railroad crossings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3342. Vehicles required to stop at railroad crossings (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as provided in subsection (c), the driver of any vehicle described in subsection
      (b), before crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad, shall stop the vehicle
      within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail of the railroad crossing
      and while so stopped shall listen and look in both directions along the track for
      any approaching train, and for signals indicating the approach of a train.  When it is safe to do so, the driver of the vehicle shall drive the vehicle across
      the tracks only in such gear of the vehicle that there will be no necessity for manually
      changing gears while traversing the crossing.  The driver shall not manually shift gears while crossing the track or tracks.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3361. Driving vehicle at safe speed
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3361. Driving vehicle at safe speed
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3361. Driving vehicle at safe speed (2023)
content:
No person shall drive a vehicle at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent
   under the conditions and having regard to the actual and potential hazards then existing,
   nor at a speed greater than will permit the driver to bring his vehicle to a stop
   within the assured clear distance ahead.  Consistent with the foregoing, every person shall drive at a safe and appropriate
   speed when approaching and crossing an intersection or railroad grade crossing, when
   approaching and going around a curve, when approaching a hill crest, when traveling
   upon any narrow or winding roadway and when special hazards exist with respect to
   pedestrians or other traffic or by reason of weather or highway conditions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter D. Special Stops Required›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3344. Emerging from alley, driveway or building
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter D. Special Stops Required › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3344. Emerging from alley, driveway or building
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3344. Emerging from alley, driveway or building (2023)
content:
Unless otherwise directed by official traffic-control devices erected in accordance
   with provisions of Subchapter B of Chapter 31 (relating to traffic-control devices),1the driver of a vehicle emerging from an alley, building, private road or driveway
   within an urban district shall stop the vehicle immediately prior to driving onto
   a sidewalk or onto the sidewalk area extending across the alley, building entrance,
   private road or driveway or, in the event there is no sidewalk area, shall stop at
   the point nearest the street to be entered where the driver has a view of approaching
   traffic.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter D. Special Stops Required›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3343. Moving heavy equipment at railroad grade crossings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter D. Special Stops Required › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3343. Moving heavy equipment at railroad grade crossings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3343. Moving heavy equipment at railroad grade crossings (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No person shall operate or move any crawler-type tractor, power shovel, derrick, roller
      or any equipment or structure having a normal operating speed of ten or less miles
      per hour or a vertical body or load clearance of less than one-half inch per foot
      of the distance between any two adjacent axles or in any event of less than nine inches
      measured above the level surface of a roadway, upon or across any tracks at a railroad
      grade crossing without first complying with this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter D. Special Stops Required›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3345. Meeting or overtaking school bus
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter D. Special Stops Required › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3345. Meeting or overtaking school bus
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3345. Meeting or overtaking school bus (2023)
content:
(a) Duty of approaching driver when red signals are flashing.--Except as provided in subsection (g), the driver of a vehicle meeting or overtaking
      any school bus stopped on a highway or trafficway shall stop at least ten feet before
      reaching the school bus when the red signal lights on the school bus are flashing
      and the side stop signal arms are activated under section 4552(b.1) (relating to general
      requirements for school buses).  The driver shall not proceed until the flashing red signal lights are no longer
      actuated.  In no event shall a driver of a vehicle resume motion of the vehicle until the school
      children who may have alighted from the school bus have reached a place of safety.  The driver of a vehicle approaching an intersection at which a school bus is stopped
      shall stop his vehicle at that intersection until the flashing red signal lights are
      no longer actuated.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter D. Special Stops Required›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3346. Emergency vehicles entering or leaving official garage
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter D. Special Stops Required › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3346. Emergency vehicles entering or leaving official garage
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3346. Emergency vehicles entering or leaving official garage (2023)
content:
If an emergency vehicle is leaving or returning to its garage and the emergency lights
   of the emergency vehicle are engaged, the driver of an approaching vehicle shall stop
   and give the emergency vehicle the right-of-way to leave or enter the garage and may
   not proceed until the emergency vehicle is safely out of the driver's path.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter D. Special Stops Required›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3345.1. Automated enforcement of failure to stop for school bus with flashing red lights
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter D. Special Stops Required › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3345.1. Automated enforcement of failure to stop for school bus with flashing red lights
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3345.1. Automated enforcement of failure to stop for school bus with flashing red lights (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A school entity may install and operate a side stop signal arm enforcement system
      for the purpose of enforcing this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter E. Stopping, Standing and Parking›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3352. Removal of vehicle by or at direction of police
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter E. Stopping, Standing and Parking › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3352. Removal of vehicle by or at direction of police
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3352. Removal of vehicle by or at direction of police (2023)
content:
(a) Outside business and residence districts.--Whenever any police officer finds a vehicle in violation of any of the provisions
      of section 3351 (relating to stopping, standing and parking outside business and residence
      districts), the officer may move the vehicle, or cause the vehicle to be moved, or
      require the driver or other person in charge of the vehicle to move the vehicle, to
      a position off the roadway where the vehicle will not interfere unduly with the normal
      movement of traffic or constitute a safety hazard.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3362. Maximum speed limits
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3362. Maximum speed limits
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3362. Maximum speed limits (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except when a special hazard exists that requires lower speed for compliance with
      section 3361 (relating to driving vehicle at safe speed), the limits specified in
      this section or established under this subchapter shall be maximum lawful speeds and
      no person shall drive a vehicle at a speed in excess of the following maximum limits:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter E. Stopping, Standing and Parking›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3351. Stopping, standing and parking outside business and residence districts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter E. Stopping, Standing and Parking › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3351. Stopping, standing and parking outside business and residence districts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3351. Stopping, standing and parking outside business and residence districts (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Outside a business or residence district, no person shall stop, park or stand any
      vehicle, whether attended or unattended, upon the roadway when it is practicable to
      stop, park or stand the vehicle off the roadway.  In the event it is necessary to stop, park or stand the vehicle on the roadway or
      any part of the roadway, an unobstructed width of the highway opposite the vehicle
      shall be left for the free passage of other vehicles and the vehicle shall be visible
      from a distance of 500 feet in each direction upon the highway.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3370. Automated speed enforcement system on designated highways
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3370. Automated speed enforcement system on designated highways

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3353. Prohibitions in specified places (2023)
content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter E. Stopping, Standing and Parking›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3354. Additional parking regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter E. Stopping, Standing and Parking › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3354. Additional parking regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3354. Additional parking regulations (2023)
content:
(a) Two-way highways.--Except as otherwise provided in this section, every vehicle standing or parked upon
      a two-way highway shall be positioned parallel to and with the right-hand wheels within
      12 inches of the right-hand curb or, in the absence of a curb, as close as practicable
      to the right edge of the right-hand shoulder.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter E. Stopping, Standing and Parking›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3355. Removal of vehicles in a city of the first class

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3364. Minimum speed regulation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3364. Minimum speed regulation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3364. Minimum speed regulation (2023)
content:
(a) Impeding movement of traffic prohibited.--Except when reduced speed is necessary for safe operation or in compliance with law,
      no person shall drive a motor vehicle at such a slow speed as to impede the normal
      and reasonable movement of traffic.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3365. Special speed limitations

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3365. Special speed limitations (2023)
content: (a) Bridges and elevated structures.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3363. Alteration of maximum limits
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3363. Alteration of maximum limits
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3363. Alteration of maximum limits (2023)
content:
On highways under their respective jurisdictions, local authorities subject to section
   6109(e) (relating to specific powers of department and local authorities) or the department,
   upon the basis of an engineering and traffic investigation, may determine that the
   maximum speed permitted under this subchapter is greater or less than is reasonable
   and safe under the conditions found to exist upon any such highway or part thereof
   and establish a reasonable and safe maximum limit.  The maximum speed limit may be made effective at all times or at times indicated
   and may vary for different weather conditions and other factors bearing on safe speeds.  No maximum speed greater than 55 miles per hour shall be established under this
   section except on highways listed in section 3362(a)(1.1) (relating to maximum speed
   limits), where the maximum speed for all vehicles shall not be greater than 70 miles
   per hour.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3369. Automated speed enforcement systems in active work zones
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3369. Automated speed enforcement systems in active work zones
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3369. Automated speed enforcement systems in active work zones (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment.--A program is established to provide for automated speed enforcement systems in active
      work zones.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3366. Charging speed violations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3366. Charging speed violations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3366. Charging speed violations (2023)
content:
In every charge of violation of a speed provision in this subchapter, except for a
   violation of section 3361 (relating to driving vehicle at safe speed), the citation
   or complaint shall specify the speed at which the defendant is alleged to have driven
   and the applicable speed limit.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3368. Speed timing devices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3368. Speed timing devices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3368. Speed timing devices (2023)
content:
(a) Speedometers authorized.--The rate of speed of any vehicle may be timed on any highway by a police officer using
      a motor vehicle equipped with a speedometer.  In ascertaining the speed of a vehicle by the use of a speedometer, the speed shall
      be timed for a distance of not less than three-tenths of a mile.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3371. Pilot program for automated speed enforcement systems in designated school zones
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3371. Pilot program for automated speed enforcement systems in designated school zones
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3371. Pilot program for automated speed enforcement systems in designated school zones (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A pilot program is established to provide for an automated speed enforcement system
      in designated school zones in a city of the first class.  The following shall apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 41. Equipment Standards›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4102. Definitions

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4102. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this part shall have, unless the context
   clearly indicates otherwise, the meanings given to them in this section:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 41. Equipment Standards›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4101. Purpose of part
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 41. Equipment Standards › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4101. Purpose of part
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4101. Purpose of part (2023)
content:
The purpose of this chapter and Chapters 43 (relating to lighting equipment) and 45
   (relating to other required equipment) is to establish minimum standards for vehicle
   equipment the performance of which is related to vehicle safety, noise control and
   air quality and to make unlawful the sale and use of items which do not comply with
   the requirements of this part or with the standards and regulations promulgated by
   the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 41. Equipment Standards›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4103. Promulgation of vehicle equipment standards
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 41. Equipment Standards › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4103. Promulgation of vehicle equipment standards
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4103. Promulgation of vehicle equipment standards (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The department shall promulgate vehicle equipment standards for vehicles, equipment
      and devices required under this part.  To the maximum extent possible, consistent with safety, the standards shall be expressed
      in terms of minimum acceptable performance levels, measured against objective testing
      parameters.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 41. Equipment Standards›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4104. Testing and approval of equipment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 41. Equipment Standards › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4104. Testing and approval of equipment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4104. Testing and approval of equipment (2023)
content:
(a) Authority of department.--The department may require new vehicles and equipment to be tested and approved for
      compliance with the requirements of this part or any vehicle equipment standard adopted
      pursuant to section 4103(a) (relating to promulgation of vehicle equipment standards).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 41. Equipment Standards›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4105. Revocation and renewal of certificates of approval
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 41. Equipment Standards › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4105. Revocation and renewal of certificates of approval
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4105. Revocation and renewal of certificates of approval (2023)
content:
(a) Hearing to review approved devices.--When the department has reason to believe that an approved device being sold commercially
      does not comply with the requirements of this part, it may, after giving 30 days'
      notice to the person holding the certificate of approval for the device, conduct a
      hearing upon the question of compliance of the approved device.  After the hearing, the department shall determine whether the approved device meets
      the requirements of this part and shall notify the person holding the certificate
      of approval of the determination.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4303. General lighting requirements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4303. General lighting requirements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4303. General lighting requirements (2023)
content:
(a) Head lamps.--Every vehicle, except trailers, operated on a highway shall be equipped with a head
      lamp system in conformance with regulations of the department. The regulations shall not prohibit a bus from being equipped with devices used to
      carry pedalcycles on the front of the bus.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part III. Operation of Vehicles›Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General›Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3370.1. Automated speed enforcement study
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part III. Operation of Vehicles › Chapter 33. Rules of the Road in General › Subchapter F. Speed Restrictions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3370.1. Automated speed enforcement study
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 3370.1. Automated speed enforcement study (2023)
content:
The Local Government Commission shall conduct a study of expanding automated speed
   enforcement on highways and streets owned by municipalities.  No later than two years after the effective date of this section, the Local Government
   Commission shall submit a report to the General Assembly and shall provide findings
   and recommendations on the expansion of automated speed enforcement on highways and
   streets owned by municipalities.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 41. Equipment Standards›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4106. Market surveillance program
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 41. Equipment Standards › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4106. Market surveillance program
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4106. Market surveillance program (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The department shall maintain a continuing program of market surveillance to insure
      that any items of vehicle equipment offered for sale in this Commonwealth and for
      which approvals are required are in compliance with the law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 41. Equipment Standards›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4107. Unlawful activities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 41. Equipment Standards › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4107. Unlawful activities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4107. Unlawful activities (2023)
content: (a) Violation of vehicle equipment standards.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 41. Equipment Standards›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4108. Injunctive relief
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 41. Equipment Standards › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4108. Injunctive relief
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4108. Injunctive relief (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Upon petition by the department, any court of competent jurisdiction in this Commonwealth
      may, for cause shown, restrain violations of this part or restrain the sale, offer
      for sale or use of any item of vehicle equipment which is determined to be in violation
      of this part or regulations promulgated pursuant thereto.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4302. Periods for requiring lighted lamps
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4302. Periods for requiring lighted lamps
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4302. Periods for requiring lighted lamps (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The operator of a vehicle upon a highway shall display the lighted head lamps and
      other lamps and illuminating devices required under this chapter for different classes
      of vehicles, subject to exceptions with respect to parked vehicles, at the following
      times:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4304. Obstructed lights not required
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4304. Obstructed lights not required
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4304. Obstructed lights not required (2023)
content:
Whenever motor and other vehicles are operated in combination during the time that
   lights are required, any lamp (except a tail lamp) need not be lighted which, by reason
   of its location on a vehicle of the combination, is obscured by another vehicle of
   the combination, but this does not affect the requirement that lighted clearance lamps
   be displayed on the front of the foremost vehicle required to have clearance lamps,
   nor that all lights required on the rear of the rearmost vehicle of any combination
   shall be lighted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4305. Vehicular hazard signal lamps
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4305. Vehicular hazard signal lamps
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4305. Vehicular hazard signal lamps (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Simultaneous flashing of the two front and two rear signal lamps shall indicate a
      vehicular traffic hazard.  The driver of a motor vehicle equipped with simultaneous flashing signals shall
      use the signals when the vehicle is stopped or disabled on a highway, except when
      the vehicle is stopped in compliance with a traffic-control device or when legally
      parked.  Drivers of other vehicles shall exercise extraordinary care in approaching, overtaking
      and passing a vehicle displaying vehicular hazard warning signals.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4301. Promulgation of regulations by department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4301. Promulgation of regulations by department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4301. Promulgation of regulations by department (2023)
content:
The department shall promulgate regulations governing the number, visibility, color,
   size, type, construction, location and use of lamps, other lighting equipment and
   any retroreflective surfaces on vehicles.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4307. Use and display of illuminated signs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4307. Use and display of illuminated signs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4307. Use and display of illuminated signs (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in this section, no vehicle shall bear or display any
      illuminated signs, letters, numerals or figures of any kind whatsoever.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4309. Lighted head lamps in work zones
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4309. Lighted head lamps in work zones
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4309. Lighted head lamps in work zones (2023)
content:
(a) Lighted head lamps required.--Head lamps shall be lighted on every vehicle driving through a signed work zone.  The department, local authorities or utilities, as the case may be, shall post or
      require its contractor to post, in advance of every work zone, an official sign warning
      drivers to light their vehicles' head lamps for an upcoming work zone.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4310. Motorcycle lighting
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4310. Motorcycle lighting
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4310. Motorcycle lighting (2023)
content:
Auxiliary lighting may be added to a motorcycle to protect the driver, including blue
   dot illumination, standard bulb running lights and light-emitting diode (LED) pods
   and strips.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4306. Use of multiple-beam road lighting equipment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4306. Use of multiple-beam road lighting equipment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4306. Use of multiple-beam road lighting equipment (2023)
content:
(a) Approaching an oncoming vehicle.--Whenever the driver of a vehicle approaches an oncoming vehicle within 500 feet, the
      driver shall use the low beam of light.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4308. Lighted head lamps on school buses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 43. Lighting Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4308. Lighted head lamps on school buses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4308. Lighted head lamps on school buses (2023)
content:
Every school bus shall display lighted head lamps during the entire period that the
   school bus is in operation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4521. Promulgation of regulations by department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4521. Promulgation of regulations by department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4521. Promulgation of regulations by department (2023)
content:
The department shall promulgate regulations governing the number, size, color, type,
   construction, location and use of other equipment on vehicles consistent with but
   not limited by the provisions of this subchapter and taking into consideration different
   requirements for different classes or types of vehicles.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4523. Exhaust systems, mufflers and noise control
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4523. Exhaust systems, mufflers and noise control
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4523. Exhaust systems, mufflers and noise control (2023)
content:
(a) Compliance with established sound levels.--Every motor vehicle operated on a highway shall be constructed, equipped, maintained
      and operated so as not to exceed the sound level for the vehicle as prescribed in
      regulations promulgated by the department.  The test procedures and instrumentation to be utilized shall also be established
      by regulation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4524. Windshield obstructions and wipers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4524. Windshield obstructions and wipers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4524. Windshield obstructions and wipers (2023)
content:
(a) Obstruction on front windshield.--No person shall drive any motor vehicle with any sign, poster or other nontransparent
      material upon the front windshield which materially obstructs, obscures or impairs
      the driver's clear view of the highway or any intersecting highway except an inspection
      certificate, sticker identification sign on a mass transit vehicle or other officially
      required sticker and no person shall drive any motor vehicle with any ice or snow
      on the front windshield which materially obstructs, obscures or impairs the driver's
      clear view of the highway or any intersecting highway.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter A. Brake Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4501. Promulgation of regulations by department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter A. Brake Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4501. Promulgation of regulations by department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4501. Promulgation of regulations by department (2023)
content:
The department shall promulgate regulations governing the type, size, construction,
   location and use of brake equipment taking into consideration different requirements
   for different classes or types of vehicles.  The authority granted in this section includes the power to regulate the performance
   of the brake system on a vehicle.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter A. Brake Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4502. General requirements for braking systems
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter A. Brake Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4502. General requirements for braking systems
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4502. General requirements for braking systems (2023)
content:
(a) Parking brakes.--Every vehicle or combination, except a motorcycle, operated on a highway shall be
      equipped with a parking brake system adequate to hold the vehicle or combination on
      any grade on which it is operated, under all conditions of loading, on a surface free
      of ice or snow.  The system shall not be designed to require a continuous or intermittent source
      of energy for full effectiveness after initial application.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4527. Image display device
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4527. Image display device
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4527. Image display device (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No motor vehicle shall be operated on a highway with an image display device where
      a broadcast television image, a live stream video image from the Internet, satellite
      or any other source or a prerecorded video image is visible to the driver while the
      vehicle is in motion.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4526. Safety glass
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4526. Safety glass
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4526. Safety glass (2023)
content:
(a) Safety glass required.--It is unlawful to sell or to operate on any highway in this Commonwealth any vehicle
      manufactured or assembled after January 1, 1934, and registered in this Commonwealth
      unless the vehicle is equipped with safety glass or similar material, which is in
      compliance with regulations promulgated by the department, wherever transparent or
      translucent material is used in the vehicle in doors, windows, windshields and wings.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4525. Tire equipment and traction surfaces
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4525. Tire equipment and traction surfaces
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4525. Tire equipment and traction surfaces (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No vehicle shall be operated on the highway unless the vehicle is equipped with tires
      of a type, size and construction approved by the department for the vehicle and unless
      the tires are in a safe operating condition as determined in accordance with regulations
      of the department, except that commercial implements of husbandry may be equipped
      with tires marked for nonhighway use.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter D. Equipment of Authorized and Emergency Vehicles›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4571. Visual and audible signals on emergency vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter D. Equipment of Authorized and Emergency Vehicles › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4571. Visual and audible signals on emergency vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4571. Visual and audible signals on emergency vehicles (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Every emergency vehicle shall be equipped with one or more revolving or flashing red
      lights and an audible warning system.  Spotlights with adjustable sockets may be attached to or mounted on emergency vehicles.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4529. Slow moving vehicle emblem
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4529. Slow moving vehicle emblem
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4529. Slow moving vehicle emblem (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--All implements of husbandry, commercial implements of husbandry and special mobile
      equipment designed to operate at 25 miles per hour or less and all animal-drawn vehicles
      shall, when traveling on a highway, display on the rear of the vehicle a reflective
      slow moving vehicle emblem as specified in regulations of the department.  The use of the slow moving vehicle emblem shall be in addition to any other lighting
      devices or equipment required by this title.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4528. Fire extinguishers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4528. Fire extinguishers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4528. Fire extinguishers (2023)
content:
Every vehicle towing a house trailer, every motor home and every motor vehicle with
   a mounted truck-camper shall be equipped with at least one fire extinguisher of a
   type and size approved by the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4535. Audible warning devices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4535. Audible warning devices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4535. Audible warning devices (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Every motor vehicle operated on a highway shall be equipped with a horn or other audible
      warning device of a type approved in regulations of the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4531. Emission control systems
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4531. Emission control systems
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4531. Emission control systems (2023)
content:
(a) Compliance with established maximum levels.--No vehicle manufactured in compliance with the requirements of the Clean Air Act (77
      Stat. 392,42 U.S.C. § 1857), or any amendments or supplements thereto, shall have emissions exceeding the maximum
      permissible levels prescribed by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4534. Rearview mirrors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4534. Rearview mirrors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4534. Rearview mirrors (2023)
content:
No person shall operate a motor vehicle or combination on a highway unless the vehicle
   or combination is equipped with at least one mirror, or similar device, which provides
   the driver an unobstructed view of the highway to the rear of the vehicle or combination.  This section shall not apply to any special mobile equipment, commercial implement
   of husbandry or implement of husbandry that is not so equipped by the original manufacturer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4530. Portable emergency warning devices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4530. Portable emergency warning devices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4530. Portable emergency warning devices (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Every truck, other than a truck registered as either a Class I or Class II having
      a gross weight of 7,000 pounds or less, truck tractor and bus and any motor vehicle
      towing a trailer shall carry at least three portable emergency warning devices of
      a type specified by regulations promulgated by the department.  The regulations shall be consistent with Motor Carrier Safety Regulations, Department
      of Transportation, Federal Highway Administration, Bureau of Motor Carrier Safety,
      section 393.95.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4532. Smoke control for diesel-powered motor vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4532. Smoke control for diesel-powered motor vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4532. Smoke control for diesel-powered motor vehicles (2023)
content:
(a) Standards and inspection.--The department shall promulgate regulations for the control of smoke from diesel-powered
      motor vehicles prescribing standards, inspection procedures and inspection equipment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter E. Occupant Protection›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4581. Restraint systems
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter E. Occupant Protection › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4581. Restraint systems
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4581. Restraint systems (2023)
content: (a) Occupant protection.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4537. Device used to carry pedalcycles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4537. Device used to carry pedalcycles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4537. Device used to carry pedalcycles (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding any other provision of this title to the contrary, a bus used for
   public transportation shall be permitted to operate with a device used to carry pedalcycles
   mounted on the front of the bus if the device, including the pedalcycles, does not
   extend more than 36 inches.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter C. Vehicles for Transportation of School Children›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4551. Safety regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter C. Vehicles for Transportation of School Children › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4551. Safety regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4551. Safety regulations (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--All school buses and all other vehicles used in the transportation of school children,
      owned by or under contract with any school district or parochial or private school,
      shall conform to standards prescribed by the department.  Regulations shall be promulgated by the department governing the safe design, construction,
      equipment and operation of vehicles engaged in the transportation of school children.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Subchapter A. Brake Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4502. General requirements for braking systems
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Subchapter A. Brake Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4502. General requirements for braking systems
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4502. General requirements for braking systems (2023)
content:
(a) Parking brakes.--Every vehicle or combination, except a motorcycle, operated on a highway shall be
      equipped with a parking brake system adequate to hold the vehicle or combination on
      any grade on which it is operated, under all conditions of loading, on a surface free
      of ice or snow.  The system shall not be designed to require a continuous or intermittent source
      of energy for full effectiveness after initial application.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Subchapter A. Brake Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4501. Promulgation of regulations by department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Subchapter A. Brake Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4501. Promulgation of regulations by department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4501. Promulgation of regulations by department (2023)
content:
The department shall promulgate regulations governing the type, size, construction,
   location and use of brake equipment taking into consideration different requirements
   for different classes or types of vehicles.  The authority granted in this section includes the power to regulate the performance
   of the brake system on a vehicle.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4533. Rear wheel shields
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Chapter 45. Other Required Equipment › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4533. Rear wheel shields
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4533. Rear wheel shields (2023)
content:
Every truck with a gross weight exceeding 11,000 pounds, trailer and truck tractor
   (without a semitrailer) driven on a highway shall be so constructed or equipped as
   to bar water or other road surface substances thrown from the rear wheels of such
   vehicle or combination at tangents exceeding 221/2degrees, measured from the road surface, from passing in a straight line to the rear
   of such vehicle or combination.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics›Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4521. Promulgation of regulations by department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part IV. Vehicle Characteristics › Subchapter B. Safety and Anti-Pollution Equipment › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4521. Promulgation of regulations by department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 4521. Promulgation of regulations by department (2023)
content:
The department shall promulgate regulations governing the number, size, color, type,
   construction, location and use of other equipment on vehicles consistent with but
   not limited by the provisions of this subchapter and taking into consideration different
   requirements for different classes or types of vehicles.
