citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6114. Limitation on sale, publication and disclosure of records (2023)
content: (a) Offenses defined.--It is unlawful for:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Chapter 61. Powers of Department and Local Authorities›Subchapter C. Reciprocity›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6150. Proportional registration not exclusive
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Chapter 61. Powers of Department and Local Authorities › Subchapter C. Reciprocity › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6150. Proportional registration not exclusive
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6150. Proportional registration not exclusive (2023)
content:
Nothing contained in this subchapter relating to proportional registration of fleet
   vehicles shall be construed as requiring any vehicle to be proportionally registered
   if the vehicle is otherwise registered in this Commonwealth for the operation in which
   it is engaged including, but not by way of limitation, regular registration, temporary
   registration, or trip permit or registration.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6115. Emergency telephones along Pennsylvania Turnpike
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6115. Emergency telephones along Pennsylvania Turnpike
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6115. Emergency telephones along Pennsylvania Turnpike (2023)
content:
The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission may provide for the installation and maintenance
   of an emergency telephone along every two miles on both sides of the highway along
   a 50-mile stretch of the Pennsylvania Turnpike between Exits 8 and 11.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Chapter 61. Powers of Department and Local Authorities›Subchapter C. Reciprocity›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6153. Existing reciprocity agreements unaffected
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Chapter 61. Powers of Department and Local Authorities › Subchapter C. Reciprocity › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6153. Existing reciprocity agreements unaffected
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6153. Existing reciprocity agreements unaffected (2023)
content:
All reciprocity and proportional registration agreements, arrangements and declarations
   relating to vehicles, in force and effect at the time this subchapter becomes effective,
   shall continue in full force and effect until specifically amended or revoked by the
   secretary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Chapter 61. Powers of Department and Local Authorities›Subchapter C. Reciprocity›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6149. Automatic reciprocity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Chapter 61. Powers of Department and Local Authorities › Subchapter C. Reciprocity › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6149. Automatic reciprocity
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6149. Automatic reciprocity (2023)
content:
If no agreement, arrangement or declaration is in effect with respect to another jurisdiction
   as authorized by this subchapter, any vehicle properly registered or licensed in the
   other jurisdiction, and for which evidence of compliance is supplied, shall receive,
   when operated in this Commonwealth, the same exemptions, benefits and privileges granted
   by the other jurisdiction to vehicles properly registered in this Commonwealth with
   the same type of registration.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6121. Uniform system of traffic-control devices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6121. Uniform system of traffic-control devices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6121. Uniform system of traffic-control devices (2023)
content:
The department shall publish a manual for a uniform system of traffic-control devices
   consistent with the provisions of this title for use upon highways within this Commonwealth.  The uniform system shall correlate with and so far as possible conform to the system
   set forth in the most recent edition of the Manual on Uniform Traffic-Control Devices
   for Streets and Highways and other standards issued or endorsed by the Federal Highway
   Administrator, United States Department of Transportation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6124. Erection of traffic-control devices at intersections
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6124. Erection of traffic-control devices at intersections
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6124. Erection of traffic-control devices at intersections (2023)
content:
The department on State-designated highways, including intersections with local highways,
   and local authorities on intersections of highways under their jurisdiction may erect
   and maintain stop signs, yield signs or other official traffic-control devices to
   designate through highways or to designate intersections at which vehicular traffic
   on one or more of the roadways should yield or stop and yield before entering the
   intersection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6125. Display of unauthorized signs, signals or markings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6125. Display of unauthorized signs, signals or markings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6125. Display of unauthorized signs, signals or markings (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No person shall place, maintain or display upon or in view of any highway any unauthorized
      sign, signal, marking or device which purports to be or is an imitation of or resembles
      an official traffic-control device or which attempts to direct the movement of traffic,
      or which hides from view or interferes with the effectiveness of an official traffic-control
      device.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6116. Payment by credit or debit card
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6116. Payment by credit or debit card
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6116. Payment by credit or debit card (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding any other provision of this title, the department is authorized to
   accept payment of a fee by a credit or debit card, even though such payment may not
   be accompanied by the required documents if the department determines that payment
   by credit or debit card will improve service to the public without adversely affecting
   the security and accuracy of departmental records.  If a payment is made by a credit or debit card, the department may, in addition
   to the fee prescribed, assess an additional service fee.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6118. Municipal police officer education and training
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6118. Municipal police officer education and training
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6118. Municipal police officer education and training (2023)
content:
Beginning July 1, 2014, and each year thereafter, the sum of $5,000,000 is appropriated
   annually to the Pennsylvania State Police from the Motor License Fund to make payments
   under53 Pa.C.S. § 2170(relating to reimbursement of expenses) consistent with the requirements ofsection 11 of Article VIII of the Constitution of Pennsylvania.  If money is not available to make full payments, the Municipal Police Officers'
   Education and Training Commission shall make payments on a pro rata basis.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6110.1. Fare evasion
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6110.1. Fare evasion
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6110.1. Fare evasion (2023)
content:
(a) Penalty.--A person that violates a regulation of the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission prohibiting
      fare evasion or attempted fare evasion commits a summary offense and shall, upon conviction,
      be sentenced to pay a fine according to the classification by the commission of the
      vehicle driven by that person at the time of violation as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6126. Interference with devices, signs or signals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6126. Interference with devices, signs or signals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6126. Interference with devices, signs or signals (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No person shall, without lawful authority, attempt to or in fact, alter, twist, obstruct,
      deface, injure, knock down, remove or interfere with the effective operation of any
      official traffic-control device, or any railroad sign or signal, or any inscription,
      shield or insignia thereon or any other part thereof.  A person shall not intentionally destroy, remove, injure or deface a temporary traffic-control
      device erected for the purpose of enhancing traffic safety or worker safety in a construction
      or maintenance workzone.  For purposes of this subsection, a traffic-control device includes a cone, tubular
      marker, delineator, warning light, drum, barricade, sign, sign truck, arrow board
      or other device specified in an approved traffic-control plan or by department regulations.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6123.1. Mandatory traffic-control devices in highway work zones
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6123.1. Mandatory traffic-control devices in highway work zones
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6123.1. Mandatory traffic-control devices in highway work zones (2023)
content:
Each Interstate highway work zone, including a work zone on the Pennsylvania Turnpike,
   with a project cost exceeding $300,000 shall be equipped with speed-monitoring devices
   for purposes of advising the operator of a vehicle of the vehicle's rate of speed.  The speed-monitoring device shall be located at least 500 feet prior to entering
   the work zone.  The entity responsible for performing the construction or maintenance work shall
   erect the speed-monitoring devices in the work zone in accordance with the department's
   regulations.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6122. Authority to erect traffic-control devices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6122. Authority to erect traffic-control devices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6122. Authority to erect traffic-control devices (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The department on State-designated highways and local authorities on any highway within
      their boundaries may erect official traffic-control devices, which shall be installed
      and maintained in conformance with the manual and regulations published by the department
      upon all highways as required to carry out the provisions of this title or to regulate,
      restrict, direct, warn, prohibit or guide traffic.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6123. Erection of traffic-control devices while working
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6123. Erection of traffic-control devices while working
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6123. Erection of traffic-control devices while working (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Any person performing any work on or near the roadway which may create hazards shall
      erect traffic-control devices in accordance with the rules and regulations of the
      department for the maintenance and protection of traffic.  The regulations of the department shall address the control of road users through
      a work zone and shall be an essential part of highway construction, utility work,
      maintenance operations and incident management.  All official traffic-control devices erected for maintenance and protection of traffic
      shall be removed as soon as practical when they are no longer needed.  When work is suspended for short periods of time, official traffic-control devices
      erected for the maintenance and protection of traffic shall be removed or covered
      when they are no longer appropriate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6119. Removal of dead deer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6119. Removal of dead deer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6119. Removal of dead deer (2023)
content:
(a) Duty.--It is the duty of the department to remove dead deer from the State right-of-way upon
      immediate notification and when the department is conducting general maintenance on
      the State right-of-way.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6127. Dealing in nonconforming traffic-control devices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6127. Dealing in nonconforming traffic-control devices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6127. Dealing in nonconforming traffic-control devices (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--It is unlawful for any person to manufacture, sell, offer for sale or to lease for
      use on the highway any traffic-control device unless it has been approved and is in
      accordance with department rules and regulations.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6117. Authority of qualified employees of department and Department of Revenue
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6117. Authority of qualified employees of department and Department of Revenue
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6117. Authority of qualified employees of department and Department of Revenue (2023)
content:
Employees of the department, the Department of Revenue and the Pennsylvania Public
   Utility Commission who have completed a training program approved by the respective
   secretaries of both departments shall be authorized to institute criminal proceedings
   by citation under the Pennsylvania Rules of Criminal Procedure for violations of the
   provisions of Chapters 13 (relating to registration of vehicles), 21 (relating to
   motor carriers road tax identification markers) and 96 (relating to motor carriers
   road tax).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6128. Dealing in official traffic-control devices or bridge parts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6128. Dealing in official traffic-control devices or bridge parts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6128. Dealing in official traffic-control devices or bridge parts (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A person commits a summary offense if he knowingly purchases, sells or offers for
      sale an official traffic-control device or an identifiable railing or other part of
      a public bridge.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part V. Administration and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6129. Maintenance of pedestrian crosswalks in school zones
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part V. Administration and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Traffic-Control Devices › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6129. Maintenance of pedestrian crosswalks in school zones
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 6129. Maintenance of pedestrian crosswalks in school zones (2023)
content:
The department may paint and maintain pedestrian crosswalks located within school
   zones on State-designated highways.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter A. Identification Number›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7105. Seizure of vehicles with removed or falsified numbers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter A. Identification Number › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7105. Seizure of vehicles with removed or falsified numbers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7105. Seizure of vehicles with removed or falsified numbers (2023)
content:
(a) Duty of police.--Every police officer having knowledge of a vehicle on which the vehicle identification
      number has been removed or falsified shall immediately seize and take possession of
      the vehicle and arrest or file a complaint for the arrest of the suspected owner or
      custodian.  In all actions involving seizure or possession of such vehicles, vehicle identification
      information shall be transmitted to the Federal or other agencies involved in recovery
      of stolen vehicles.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter C. Misuse of Documents and Plates›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7121. False application for certificate of title or registration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter C. Misuse of Documents and Plates › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7121. False application for certificate of title or registration
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7121. False application for certificate of title or registration (2023)
content:
A person is guilty of a misdemeanor of the first degree if the person uses a false
   or fictitious name or address or makes a material false statement, or fails to disclose
   a security interest, or conceals any other material fact in an application for a certificate
   of title or for registration.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7113. Reporting stolen and recovered vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7113. Reporting stolen and recovered vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7113. Reporting stolen and recovered vehicles (2023)
content:
(a) Stolen vehicle.--Every police department or police office, having knowledge of a stolen vehicle, shall
      immediately furnish the State Police with full information about the stolen vehicle.  The State Police shall forward the stolen vehicle information to the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter C. Misuse of Documents and Plates›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7122. Altered, forged or counterfeit documents and plates
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter C. Misuse of Documents and Plates › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7122. Altered, forged or counterfeit documents and plates
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7122. Altered, forged or counterfeit documents and plates (2023)
content:
A person is guilty of a misdemeanor of the first degree if the person, with fraudulent
   intent:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7111. Dealing in titles and plates for stolen vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7111. Dealing in titles and plates for stolen vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7111. Dealing in titles and plates for stolen vehicles (2023)
content:
A person is guilty of a misdemeanor of the first degree if the person with fraudulent
   intent procures or attempts to procure a certificate of title or registration plate
   for a vehicle, or passes or attempts to pass a certificate of title or an assignment
   to a vehicle, knowing or having reason to believe that the vehicle has been stolen.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter A. Identification Number›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7101. Requirement for identification number
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter A. Identification Number › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7101. Requirement for identification number
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7101. Requirement for identification number (2023)
content:
Every vehicle other than a pedalcycle shall contain a vehicle identification number
   which shall be placed upon or incorporated into the vehicle in such manner as to be
   a permanent part of the vehicle.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter A. Identification Number›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7104. State replacement vehicle identification number plate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter A. Identification Number › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7104. State replacement vehicle identification number plate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7104. State replacement vehicle identification number plate (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No vehicle on which the vehicle identification number has been removed or falsified
      shall be titled or registered without a special permit from the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Subchapter A. Identification Number›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7101. Requirement for identification number
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Subchapter A. Identification Number › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7101. Requirement for identification number
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7101. Requirement for identification number (2023)
content:
Every vehicle other than a pedalcycle shall contain a vehicle identification number
   which shall be placed upon or incorporated into the vehicle in such manner as to be
   a permanent part of the vehicle.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7112. False report of theft or conversion of vehicle
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7112. False report of theft or conversion of vehicle
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7112. False report of theft or conversion of vehicle (2023)
content:
A person is guilty of a misdemeanor of the third degree if the person knowingly makes
   a false report of the theft or conversion of a vehicle to a police officer or to the
   department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter D. Tampering with Odometers›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7132. Prohibited activities relating to odometers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter D. Tampering with Odometers › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7132. Prohibited activities relating to odometers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7132. Prohibited activities relating to odometers (2023)
content:
(a) Devices causing improper odometer reading.--No person shall advertise for sale, sell, use or install, or cause to be installed,
      any device which causes an odometer to register any mileage other than the true mileage
      driven which is that mileage driven by the vehicle as registered by the odometer within
      the manufacturer's designed tolerance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter D. Tampering with Odometers›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7134. Odometer disclosure requirements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter D. Tampering with Odometers › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7134. Odometer disclosure requirements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7134. Odometer disclosure requirements (2023)
content:
(a) Odometer mileage statement.--Prior to or simultaneously with the execution of any ownership transfer document relating
      to a motor vehicle, each transferor of a motor vehicle shall furnish to the transferee
      a statement signed by the transferor containing the following information:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter C. Misuse of Documents and Plates›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7124. Fraudulent use or removal of registration plate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter C. Misuse of Documents and Plates › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7124. Fraudulent use or removal of registration plate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7124. Fraudulent use or removal of registration plate (2023)
content:
A person who either removes a registration plate from a vehicle or affixes to a vehicle
   a registration plate not authorized by law for use on the vehicle, with intent to
   conceal or misrepresent the identity of the vehicle or its owner, is guilty of a summary
   offense punishable by a fine of not less than $100 nor more than $500 or imprisonment
   for not more than 90 days, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter D. Tampering with Odometers›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7133. Permissible activities relating to odometers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter D. Tampering with Odometers › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7133. Permissible activities relating to odometers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7133. Permissible activities relating to odometers (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Nothing in this subchapter prevents the service, repair or replacement of an odometer
      if the mileage indicated remains the same as before the service, repair or replacement.  Where the odometer is incapable of registering the same mileage as before the service,
      repair or replacement, the odometer shall be adjusted to read zero and a notice in
      writing shall be attached to the left door frame of the vehicle by the owner or his
      agent specifying the mileage prior to repair or replacement of the odometer and the
      date on which it was repaired or replaced.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Subchapter A. Identification Number›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7105. Seizure of vehicles with removed or falsified numbers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Subchapter A. Identification Number › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7105. Seizure of vehicles with removed or falsified numbers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7105. Seizure of vehicles with removed or falsified numbers (2023)
content:
(a) Duty of police.--Every police officer having knowledge of a vehicle on which the vehicle identification
      number has been removed or falsified shall immediately seize and take possession of
      the vehicle and arrest or file a complaint for the arrest of the suspected owner or
      custodian.  In all actions involving seizure or possession of such vehicles, vehicle identification
      information shall be transmitted to the Federal or other agencies involved in recovery
      of stolen vehicles.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Subchapter A. Identification Number›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7104. State replacement vehicle identification number plate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Subchapter A. Identification Number › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7104. State replacement vehicle identification number plate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7104. State replacement vehicle identification number plate (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No vehicle on which the vehicle identification number has been removed or falsified
      shall be titled or registered without a special permit from the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7116. Fraudulent removal of vehicle from garage
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7116. Fraudulent removal of vehicle from garage
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7116. Fraudulent removal of vehicle from garage (2023)
content:
No person shall remove or cause to be removed, by any false pretension or with intent
   to defraud, any vehicle that has been placed in a garage or automobile shop for storage,
   repair or garage service.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter C. Misuse of Documents and Plates›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7123. Sale or purchase of certificate or other document
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter C. Misuse of Documents and Plates › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7123. Sale or purchase of certificate or other document
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7123. Sale or purchase of certificate or other document (2023)
content:
It is unlawful to purchase or sell a certificate or any other document issued by the
   department.  Police officers or department representatives may confiscate the documents when
   unlawfully possessed or used.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7111. Dealing in titles and plates for stolen vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7111. Dealing in titles and plates for stolen vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7111. Dealing in titles and plates for stolen vehicles (2023)
content:
A person is guilty of a misdemeanor of the first degree if the person with fraudulent
   intent procures or attempts to procure a certificate of title or registration plate
   for a vehicle, or passes or attempts to pass a certificate of title or an assignment
   to a vehicle, knowing or having reason to believe that the vehicle has been stolen.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter D. Tampering with Odometers›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7136. Conspiracy to violate odometer requirements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter D. Tampering with Odometers › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7136. Conspiracy to violate odometer requirements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7136. Conspiracy to violate odometer requirements (2023)
content:
No person shall conspire with any other person to violate section 7132 (relating to
   prohibited activities relating to odometers), 7133 (relating to permissible activities
   relating to odometers) or 7134 (relating to odometer disclosure requirements).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7115. Application for certificate of title of a stolen vehicle
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7115. Application for certificate of title of a stolen vehicle
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7115. Application for certificate of title of a stolen vehicle (2023)
content:
Upon receipt of an application for a certificate of title of a stolen vehicle, the
   department shall notify the State Police and the rightful owner and shall withhold
   the issuing of the certificate of title until the proper investigation is made.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7114. Records of stolen vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7114. Records of stolen vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7114. Records of stolen vehicles (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The department shall, upon receiving a report of the theft of a vehicle, make an entry
      onto the vehicle's record that it has been reported as stolen, which entry shall remain
      until a report of recovery has been received as provided in section 7113(b) (relating
      to reporting stolen and recovered vehicles).  If the vehicle is not reported as recovered within five years, the department may
      remove the record from its files.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter D. Tampering with Odometers›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7135. Odometer mileage statement retention
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter D. Tampering with Odometers › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7135. Odometer mileage statement retention
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7135. Odometer mileage statement retention (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Each dealer or motor vehicle auction company who is required by this subchapter to
      execute or receive an odometer mileage statement shall retain for four years each
      odometer mileage statement which he receives.  He shall also retain for four years a photostat, carbon or other facsimile copy
      of each odometer mileage statement which he issues.  The dealer shall retain each odometer mileage statement at the primary place of
      business in an order that is appropriate to his business requirements and that permits
      systematic retrieval.  The statement may be reproduced as long as no information or identifying marks such
      as signatures are lost in the reproduction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7113. Reporting stolen and recovered vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7113. Reporting stolen and recovered vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7113. Reporting stolen and recovered vehicles (2023)
content:
(a) Stolen vehicle.--Every police department or police office, having knowledge of a stolen vehicle, shall
      immediately furnish the State Police with full information about the stolen vehicle.  The State Police shall forward the stolen vehicle information to the department.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter D. Tampering with Odometers › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7137. Violation of Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7137. Violation of Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law (2023)
content:
A violation of any provision of this subchapter or regulation promulgated thereunder
   constitutes “unfair methods of competition” and “unfair or deceptive acts or practices” within the meaning of section 2(4) of the act of December 17, 1968 (P.L. 1224, No.
   387),1known as the Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions›Subchapter D. Tampering with Odometers›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7138. Civil liability
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 71. Vehicle Theft and Related Provisions › Subchapter D. Tampering with Odometers › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7138. Civil liability
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7138. Civil liability (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A person who, with intent to defraud, violates any requirement imposed under this
      subchapter shall be liable in an amount equal to the sum of three times the amount
      of actual damages sustained or $3,000, whichever is the greater, and, in the case
      of any successful action to enforce this liability, the costs of the action together
      with reasonable attorney fees as determined by the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Subchapter B. Stolen Vehicles›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7112. False report of theft or conversion of vehicle

content:
A person is guilty of a misdemeanor of the third degree if the person knowingly makes
   a false report of the theft or conversion of a vehicle to a police officer or to the
   department.

      if the mileage indicated remains the same as before the service, repair or replacement.  Where the odometer is incapable of registering the same mileage as before the service,
      repair or replacement, the odometer shall be adjusted to read zero and a notice in
      writing shall be attached to the left door frame of the vehicle by the owner or his
      agent specifying the mileage prior to repair or replacement of the odometer and the
      date on which it was repaired or replaced.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos›Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7301. Authorization of salvors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7301. Authorization of salvors

content:
(a) General rule.--The department shall authorize and shall issue a certificate of authorization to every
      salvor that complies with the requirements of this chapter and regulations adopted
      by the department and is a currently registered vehicle salvage dealer as defined
      in section 1337(c)(2) (relating to use of “Miscellaneous Motor Vehicle Business” registration

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos›Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7304. Reports to department of possession of abandoned vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7304. Reports to department of possession of abandoned vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7304. Reports to department of possession of abandoned vehicles (2023)
content:
Any salvor taking possession of an abandoned vehicle pursuant to section 7303.1 (relating
   to duty of police and salvors) shall within 48 hours after taking possession send
   an abandoned vehicle information report to the department. If the report indicates the vehicle is a salvage vehicle, the salvor shall include
   a photograph of the vehicle to be prepared in a manner prescribed by the department.  Any nonrepairable vehicle which does not display an identifiable registration plate,
   current certificate of inspection and ascertainable vehicle identification number
   shall be taken into possession and flattened or crushed immediately.  There is no requirement to notify the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos›Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7303.1. Duty of police and salvors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7303.1. Duty of police and salvors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7303.1. Duty of police and salvors (2023)
content:
(a) Duty of police and authorized personnel.--Police officers or personnel designated by ordinance of a municipality shall process
      all vehicles presumed to be abandoned.  They shall complete an abandoned vehicle information report on a form prescribed
      by the department on each vehicle declared abandoned.  The report shall include the make, model, vehicle identification number, registration
      plate number, name and address of the owner or person who abandoned the vehicle, if
      known, and any other information the department may require.  The report shall also indicate the vehicle's status as a vehicle with value, a salvage
      vehicle or a nonrepairable vehicle.  The report shall include the name, signature and badge number of the police officer
      and the name of the respective police department.  The report shall serve as an authorized written request for a licensed salvor to
      remove, possess and further process the abandoned vehicle.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos›Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7305. Notice to owner and lienholders of abandoned vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7305. Notice to owner and lienholders of abandoned vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7305. Notice to owner and lienholders of abandoned vehicles (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The department upon receipt of an abandoned vehicle information report shall notify
      by certified mail, return receipt requested, the last known registered owner of the
      vehicle and all lienholders of record that the vehicle is being held as abandoned.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos›Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Payment of costs upon reclaiming vehicle
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Payment of costs upon reclaiming vehicle
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Payment of costs upon reclaiming vehicle (2023)
content:
In the event the owner or lienholder of an abandoned vehicle reclaims the vehicle,
   the reclaiming party shall pay the costs for towing and storage from the date the
   salvor submitted the abandoned vehicle report to the department, plus a fee of $50
   of which $25 shall be transmitted to the department by the salvor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos›Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7302. Certificate of authorization
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7302. Certificate of authorization
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7302. Certificate of authorization (2023)
content:
(a) Application and issuance.--Application for a certificate of authorization shall be made on a form prescribed
      by the department.  The department shall investigate the qualifications and fitness of the applicant
      and shall issue a certificate of authorization if it determines that the applicant
      is capable of performing the duties of a salvor in a manner consistent with the public
      interest.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos›Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7303. Suspension of authorization
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7303. Suspension of authorization
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7303. Suspension of authorization (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The department shall supervise salvors and, after providing an opportunity for a hearing,
      shall suspend the authorization of any salvor which the department finds is not properly
      operated or which has violated or failed to comply with any of the provisions of this
      chapter or regulations adopted by the department.  A suspended certificate of authorization shall be returned to the department immediately
      except an appeal from suspension as provided in subsection (b) shall operate as a
      supersedeas of any suspension by the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos›Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7307. Authorization for disposal of unclaimed vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7307. Authorization for disposal of unclaimed vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7307. Authorization for disposal of unclaimed vehicles (2023)
content:
The department shall, after the expiration of 30 days from the date of notice sent
   by certified mail to the registered owner and all lienholders of record or 30 days
   after publication of notice, where applicable, and upon receipt of a written statement
   from the holder of the vehicle that the abandoned vehicle has not been reclaimed by
   the owner or lienholder within the 30-day period, authorize the disposal of the abandoned
   vehicle in accordance with the provisions of this chapter.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7304.1. Reports and removal of abandoned vehicles within the boundaries of a city of the first class or second class
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7304.1. Reports and removal of abandoned vehicles within the boundaries of a city of the first class or second class (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Any and all vehicles reported abandoned to the police department and/or the appropriate
      designated municipal agency or department that handles the abandoned vehicle and cargo
      process shall be investigated within five business days to determine if the reported
      vehicle is abandoned as defined in section 102 (relating to definitions).  Upon the completion of the investigation, any and all reported vehicles that satisfy
      the requirements of the definition of “abandoned vehicle” shall be officially declared abandoned and removed within ten business days by the
      police department or by an authorized salvor pursuant to police or municipality directions.  Proper notification of the removal of the vehicle shall be sent pursuant to section
      7305 (relating to notice to owner and lienholders of abandoned vehicles).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos›Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7309. Processing of nonrepairable or salvage vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7309. Processing of nonrepairable or salvage vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7309. Processing of nonrepairable or salvage vehicles (2023)
content:
(a) Application for certificate of salvage.--If an abandoned vehicle is a salvage or nonrepairable vehicle as deemed by a police
      officer and salvor, the salvor and the police officer shall note that fact in the
      report to the department required in section 7304 (relating to reports to department
      of possession of abandoned vehicles) and shall apply for issuance of a certificate
      of salvage or nonrepairable vehicle as provided for in Subchapter D1of Chapter 11 (relating to salvage vehicles, theft vehicles, reconstructed vehicles
      and flood vehicles).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos›Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311. Reports by garage keepers of abandoned vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311. Reports by garage keepers of abandoned vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311. Reports by garage keepers of abandoned vehicles (2023)
content:
The person in charge of any garage or repair shop in which a vehicle of unknown ownership
   has been left for a period of 15 consecutive days or, in the case of repair or storage,
   15 consecutive days following the completion of repairs or storage agreement without
   being removed by the owner or any other person duly authorized to remove the vehicle
   shall report to the department within 24 hours of the expiration of the 15-day period
   giving the make, vehicle identification number, registration plate number and the
   name and address of the person abandoning the vehicle if known.  Upon receipt of the report the department shall make a distinctive record of the
   report and issue a private property abandoned vehicle information report under section
   7311.1 (relating to reports by private property owners of abandoned vehicles) to the
   garage keeper to complete and file with the police.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7310. Removal of abandoned or presumed abandoned vehicles from roadway
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7310. Removal of abandoned or presumed abandoned vehicles from roadway (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Police officers may immediately remove or direct removal of any vehicle abandoned
      or presumed to be abandoned from any roadway, including the roadway's berm or shoulder,
      to the nearest point off the roadway where the vehicle will not interfere with or
      obstruct traffic.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311.2. Salvors to remove abandoned vehicles in good faith
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311.2. Salvors to remove abandoned vehicles in good faith (2023)
content:
When requested to remove an abandoned vehicle, no salvor shall relocate and subsequently
   abandon the vehicle.  The salvor shall move the vehicle to a facility for the purpose of storage of abandoned
   vehicles or another place as directed by the police or approved by the department.

      of possession of abandoned vehicles) and shall apply for issuance of a certificate
      of salvage or nonrepairable vehicle as provided for in Subchapter D1of Chapter 11 (relating to salvage vehicles, theft vehicles, reconstructed vehicles
      and flood vehicles).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7310. Removal of abandoned or presumed abandoned vehicles from roadway
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7310. Removal of abandoned or presumed abandoned vehicles from roadway
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7310. Removal of abandoned or presumed abandoned vehicles from roadway (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Police officers may immediately remove or direct removal of any vehicle abandoned
      or presumed to be abandoned from any roadway, including the roadway's berm or shoulder,
      to the nearest point off the roadway where the vehicle will not interfere with or
      obstruct traffic.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311. Reports by garage keepers of abandoned vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311. Reports by garage keepers of abandoned vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311. Reports by garage keepers of abandoned vehicles (2023)
content:
The person in charge of any garage or repair shop in which a vehicle of unknown ownership
   has been left for a period of 15 consecutive days or, in the case of repair or storage,
   15 consecutive days following the completion of repairs or storage agreement without
   being removed by the owner or any other person duly authorized to remove the vehicle
   shall report to the department within 24 hours of the expiration of the 15-day period
   giving the make, vehicle identification number, registration plate number and the
   name and address of the person abandoning the vehicle if known.  Upon receipt of the report the department shall make a distinctive record of the
   report and issue a private property abandoned vehicle information report under section
   7311.1 (relating to reports by private property owners of abandoned vehicles) to the
   garage keeper to complete and file with the police.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter B. Watercraft Trailer Forfeiture › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7326. Publication
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7326. Publication (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--At any time after the date the watercraft trailer dealer receives notice from the
      department pursuant to section 7325 (relating to responsibility of department), the
      watercraft trailer dealer shall publish a notice, once a week for two consecutive
      weeks, in a newspaper of general circulation published in the county where the watercraft
      trailer dealer is located, describing the watercraft trailer and any identifying number.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos›Subchapter B. Watercraft Trailer Forfeiture›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7323. Liens
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter B. Watercraft Trailer Forfeiture › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7323. Liens
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7323. Liens (2023)
content:
A watercraft trailer dealer shall have a lien, dependent upon possession, on a watercraft
   trailer for the balance due the watercraft trailer dealer for any repair, remanufacture,
   restoration, alteration, storage, cleaning, consignment or brokerage of a boat, any
   related equipment or a watercraft trailer.  The watercraft trailer dealer may retain possession of a watercraft trailer until
   the charges are paid.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7312. Penalty for violation of chapter (2023)
content:

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter B. Watercraft Trailer Forfeiture › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7324. Notification by watercraft trailer dealer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7324. Notification by watercraft trailer dealer (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If a customer does not claim possession of a watercraft trailer within 30 days of
      the terminal date, a watercraft trailer dealer may initiate the forfeiture procedure
      by sending written notice on the same day by certified mail, return receipt requested,
      to the department and the customer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311.2. Salvors to remove abandoned vehicles in good faith
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Subchapter A. Abandoned Vehicles and Salvors › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311.2. Salvors to remove abandoned vehicles in good faith
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311.2. Salvors to remove abandoned vehicles in good faith (2023)
content:
When requested to remove an abandoned vehicle, no salvor shall relocate and subsequently
   abandon the vehicle.  The salvor shall move the vehicle to a facility for the purpose of storage of abandoned
   vehicles or another place as directed by the police or approved by the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos›Subchapter B. Watercraft Trailer Forfeiture›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7331. Construction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter B. Watercraft Trailer Forfeiture › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7331. Construction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7331. Construction (2023)
content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos›Subchapter B. Watercraft Trailer Forfeiture›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7328. Forfeiture
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter B. Watercraft Trailer Forfeiture › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7328. Forfeiture
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7328. Forfeiture (2023)
content:
A watercraft trailer that is not redeemed within 30 days of the second publication
   under section 7326 (relating to publication) is deemed forfeited to the watercraft
   trailer dealer, and any prior right, title or interest in the watercraft trailer is
   terminated.  The watercraft trailer dealer shall make application for a certificate of title
   to the department.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7327. Redemption (2023)
content:
(a) Notice.--Upon request of the customer, any lienholder or the owner of a watercraft trailer,
      the watercraft trailer dealer shall provide the amount necessary under subsection
      (b), at the time of the request, to redeem the watercraft trailer.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Subchapter B. Watercraft Trailer Forfeiture › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7329. Rights acquired by good faith purchaser
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7329. Rights acquired by good faith purchaser (2023)
content:
A purchaser in good faith of a watercraft trailer sold by a watercraft trailer dealer
   after forfeiture under this subchapter takes the watercraft trailer free of all liens
   and encumbrances despite noncompliance by the watercraft trailer dealer with the requirements
   of this subchapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos›Subchapter B. Watercraft Trailer Forfeiture›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7330. Other remedies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 73. Abandoned Vehicles and Cargos › Subchapter B. Watercraft Trailer Forfeiture › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7330. Other remedies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7330. Other remedies (2023)
content:
The provisions of this subchapter are in addition to any and all other remedies available
   to a watercraft trailer dealer.  This subchapter shall not foreclose any other remedies available to a watercraft
   trailer dealer at law or in equity.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 75. Messenger Service›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7505. Transaction of business with department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 75. Messenger Service › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7505. Transaction of business with department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7505. Transaction of business with department (2023)
content:
The department may designate those locations, facilities and hours of operation at
   which messenger or agent services may transact business with the department.  Every messenger or agent service with whom a contract has been signed pursuant to
   this chapter shall be permitted to transact business with the department at the locations
   and facilities and during the hours of operation designated by the department.  The department may prescribe such regulations as may be necessary for the administration
   of this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 75. Messenger Service›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7503.1. Bond required
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 75. Messenger Service › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7503.1. Bond required
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7503.1. Bond required (2023)
content:
Before entering into a contract with any person to act as a messenger or agent service,
   the department shall require a person to furnish and maintain a bond indemnifying
   the public and the department in an amount specified by the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 75. Messenger Service›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7502.1. Supersession
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 75. Messenger Service › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7502.1. Supersession
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7502.1. Supersession (2023)
content:
(a) Regulations.--Regulations pertaining to messengers and agents regarding the amount of a bond, hearings,
      written warnings, suspensions, revocations or fines shall not apply to messengers
      and agents who enter into contracts with the department to provide messenger or agent
      services.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 75. Messenger Service›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7506. Violations and penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 75. Messenger Service › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7506. Violations and penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7506. Violations and penalties (2023)
content:
A person violating any provision of this chapter or the rules and regulations promulgated
   thereunder for which a specific penalty is not provided is guilty of a summary offense
   and shall, upon conviction, be sentenced to pay a fine of $100.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 75. Messenger Service›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501. Authorization of messenger and agent services

content: (a) General rule.--The department shall enter into contracts for messenger and agent services.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles›Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 75. Messenger Service›PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7509. Messenger and Agent Advisory Committee
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 75. Messenger Service › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7509. Messenger and Agent Advisory Committee
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7509. Messenger and Agent Advisory Committee (2023)
content:
(a) Purpose.--The Messenger and Agent Advisory Committee, consisting of 13 members, shall be created
      by the department to develop contract language and propose regulations governing messenger
      and agent services.

content:

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 75 Pa.C.S.A. Vehicles › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 77. Snowmobiles and All-Terrain Vehicles › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7705. Records and reports
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 75 Pa.C.S.A. § 7705. Records and reports (2023)
content:
The provisions of Subchapter B1of Chapter 63 (relating to records of traffic cases) relating to records and reports
   shall be applicable to proceedings under this chapter.
