      of this act or the Occupational Disease Act or with any rules promulgated thereunder,
      the department may revoke its permit after notice and opportunity for a hearing.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.1. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.1. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.1. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this article shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.3. Review of applications
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.3. Review of applications
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.3. Review of applications (2023)
content:
(a)(1) The department shall, in accordance with section 802,1review, approve or disapprove fund applications under such rules and requirements
         relating to applications under section 3052and the Occupational Disease Act3as may be applicable and such rules and regulations as are specifically adopted with
         regard to fund applications.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.2. Employers' self-insuring pooling
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.2. Employers' self-insuring pooling
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.2. Employers' self-insuring pooling (2023)
content:
(a) Employers shall be permitted to pool their liabilities under this act and the
      Occupational Disease Act1and their employers' liability through participation in a fund approved by the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.4. Permits
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.4. Permits
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.4. Permits (2023)
content:
All permits issued under this article shall remain in effect unless terminated at
   the request of the fund or revoked by the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.6. Assessment of members
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.6. Assessment of members
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.6. Assessment of members (2023)
content:
(a) Members of said fund shall pay a minimum of twenty-five per centum of their annual
      assessment into the fund on or before the inception of the fund.  The balance of the annual assessments shall be paid to the fund on a monthly, quarterly
      or semiannual basis as required by the fund's bylaws and approved by the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.7. Applications for membership
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.7. Applications for membership
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.7. Applications for membership (2023)
content:
After the final permit approval date of the fund, prospective new members of the fund
   shall submit an application for membership to the fund's plan committee or administrator
   in a form approved by the department.  This application shall include an agreement of joint and several liability as required
   in section 803.1The administrator or plan committee may approve the application for membership pursuant
   to the bylaws of the fund.  The application approved by the fund shall be filed with the department.  The fund shall retain the authority to reject any applicant.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.9. Return of dividends
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.9. Return of dividends
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.9. Return of dividends (2023)
content:
Any fund may return to its members dividends based upon the recommendation of an independent
   actuary.  Dividends shall not be returned if the payment of such dividends would impair the
   fund's ability to meet its obligations under this act or the Occupational Disease
   Act,1nor shall dividends be returned prior to the beginning of the thirteenth month following
   the expiration of the preceding annual reporting period.  The initial dividend payment for any annual reporting period shall not exceed thirty
   per centum of the surplus available for the applicable annual reporting period.  The fund may, however, seek annual approval for payment of dividends from the surplus
   remaining from any annual reporting period which has been completed for at least twenty-five
   months or longer and may include such dividend payments with initial dividend payments
   from the subsequent annual reporting period.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.8. Termination of participation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.8. Termination of participation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.8. Termination of participation (2023)
content:
(a) Individual members may elect to terminate their participation in a fund or be
      subject to cancellation by the fund pursuant to the bylaws of the fund for nonpayment
      of premium or other violations.  Any member withdrawing from a fund or member terminated by the fund for nonpayment
      of assessments shall remain fully obligated for claims incurred during the period
      of its membership in accord with fund bylaws, including, but not limited to, amounts
      owed as annual or supplemental assessments.  Notice of termination of any participant shall be filed with the fund.  The fund shall attach any such notices of termination to the renewal application
      filed with the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.10. Deficiency of assets
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.10. Deficiency of assets
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.10. Deficiency of assets (2023)
content:
(a) If the assets of a fund are at any time insufficient to enable the fund to discharge
      its legal liabilities and other obligations and to maintain the actuarially appropriate
      loss reserves required of it under section 802(b)(14),1the fund shall forthwith make up the deficiency or levy an assessment upon the fund
      members for the amount needed to make up the deficiency.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.12. Classifications for participants
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.12. Classifications for participants
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.12. Classifications for participants (2023)
content:
Each fund shall request classifications for its participants from the bureau or bureaus
   approved by the commissioner and shall utilize those classifications making assessments
   based upon rates as utilized by the State Workmen's Insurance Fund for such classification
   except as provided in section 811.1The fund shall pay the appropriate bureau a reasonable charge, approved by the commissioner,
   for this service.  The fund may appeal classifications as provided in the applicable sections of the
   Insurance Company Law of 1921 for other employers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.11. Annual assessment of members; deviation from rates
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.11. Annual assessment of members; deviation from rates
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.11. Annual assessment of members; deviation from rates (2023)
content:
The annual assessment of each fund member shall be based upon the annual payroll of
   fund members multiplied by the rates as utilized by the State Workmen's Insurance
   Fund for members minus any premium discounts.  A fund may deviate from these rates and establish its own rates with the approval
   of an independent actuary and the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.16. Annual assessment of funds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.16. Annual assessment of funds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.16. Annual assessment of funds (2023)
content:
Each fund shall be assessed annually by the department in a like manner and amount
   as other insurers or self-insurers are now or hereafter assessed under this act and
   the Occupational Disease Act1and shall pay such assessment in accordance with this act and the Occupational Disease
   Act.  All contributions received in accordance with this section shall be deposited into
   the appropriate fund as required by the applicable provision of law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.13. Investment of surplus moneys
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.13. Investment of surplus moneys
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.13. Investment of surplus moneys (2023)
content:
Each fund may invest any surplus moneys not needed for current obligations in United
   States Government obligations, United States Treasury notes, investment share accounts
   in any savings and loan association whose deposits are insured by a Federal agency
   and certificates of deposit issued by a duly chartered commercial bank.  Deposits in savings and loan associations and commercial banks shall be limited
   to institutions in this Commonwealth and shall not exceed the federally insured amount
   in any one account.  Investments may also be made in any permitted investments of capital or surplus
   of stock casualty insurance companies set forth in section 602 or 6031of the Insurance Company Law of 1921, as may be authorized by regulation approved
   by the commissioner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.14. Single accident and aggregate excess insurance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.14. Single accident and aggregate excess insurance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.14. Single accident and aggregate excess insurance (2023)
content:
(a) Funds approved under this article shall purchase excess insurance by reason of
      any single accident or any single occurrence as provided in section 653 of the Insurance
      Company Law of 19211and aggregate excess insurance.  The department may waive the requirement for either single accident (single occurrence)
      or aggregate excess insurance or the requirement for both single accident (single
      occurrence) and aggregate excess insurance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.15. Annual report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.15. Annual report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.15. Annual report (2023)
content:
(a) A report shall be prepared by each fund for each annual reporting period and shall
      be filed with the department and made available to each fund member.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.18. Administration and enforcement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.18. Administration and enforcement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.18. Administration and enforcement (2023)
content:
The department is authorized to promulgate rules and regulations for the administration
   and enforcement of this article.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.17. Group subscription to State Workmen's Insurance Fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.17. Group subscription to State Workmen's Insurance Fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.17. Group subscription to State Workmen's Insurance Fund (2023)
content:
Any group of five (5) homogeneous employers who will provide to the fund an annual
   volume of premium of at least five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000) may become
   subscribers as a group to the State Workmen's Insurance Fund for the purpose of insuring
   therein their liability to those of their employes.  Such group shall become legally obligated to pay any employe compensation required
   by this act because of bodily injury by accident or disease, including death at any
   time resulting therefrom, sustained by such employe arising out of and in the course
   of his employment.  Such group shall make a written application for subscription for group insurance
   to the board.  Such application shall designate the name of the group subscriber and shall include
   such information as determined by the board as will allow the board to identify the
   employers and to adequately assess risks and premiums to be charged to employers to
   be insured by the fund under the group subscription.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.19. Organization of single board of trustees to oversee operations of several groups permitted
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7C. Self-Insurance Pooling › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.19. Organization of single board of trustees to oversee operations of several groups permitted
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1036.19. Organization of single board of trustees to oversee operations of several groups permitted (2023)
content:
If an association of employers establishes more than one group under this article,
   the association may organize a single board of trustees to oversee the operations
   of the several groups:  Provided, however, That each of the several groups shall be
   equally represented on the board.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.4. Determination of default
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.4. Determination of default
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.4. Determination of default (2023)
content:
(a) When a self-insurer fails to pay compensation when due, the department shall determine
      the reasons for such failure.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.1. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.1. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.1. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this article shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.2. Establishment of Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.2. Establishment of Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.2. Establishment of Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund (2023)
content:
(a)(1) There is hereby established a special fund to be known as the Self-Insurance
         Guaranty Fund.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.6. Payment of security into custodial account
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.6. Payment of security into custodial account
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.6. Payment of security into custodial account (2023)
content:
(a)(1) Security or funds from security demanded and paid to the department under section
         9041shall be deposited into the Guaranty Fund.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.3. Payments to claimants upon default of self-insurers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.3. Payments to claimants upon default of self-insurers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.3. Payments to claimants upon default of self-insurers (2023)
content:
The fund shall be maintained to make payments to any claimant or his dependents upon
   the default of the self-insurer liable to pay compensation due under this act and
   the Occupational Disease Act or costs associated therewith and shall be maintained
   in an amount sufficient to pay such compensation and costs or reasonably anticipated
   to be needed by virtue of default by self-insurers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.5. Fund's assumption of rights and obligations of defaulting self-insurer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.5. Fund's assumption of rights and obligations of defaulting self-insurer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.5. Fund's assumption of rights and obligations of defaulting self-insurer (2023)
content:
(a) When payments are ordered from the Guaranty Fund's appropriate custodial account,
      the fund assumes the rights and obligations of the self-insurer under this act or
      the Occupational Disease Act with regard to the payment of compensation and shall
      have and may exercise the rights set forth in this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.7. Initial and subsequent assessments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.7. Initial and subsequent assessments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.7. Initial and subsequent assessments (2023)
content:
(a) On a date to be determined by the department following the effective date of this
      article, employers who are self-insurers as of that effective date shall pay an initial
      assessment of one-half per centum of the compensation paid by each self-insurer in
      the year preceding the assessment.  Self-insurers who, prior to such effective date, were not self-insurers shall pay
      an assessment based on one-half per centum of their modified manual1premium for the twelve (12) months immediately prior to becoming self-insurers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.9. Prefund Account
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.9. Prefund Account
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.9. Prefund Account (2023)
content:
(a) There is established in the Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund a restricted account
      known as the Prefund Account. The department shall annually transfer from the Workmen's Compensation Administration
      Fund to the account an amount up to three million eight hundred thousand dollars ($3,800,000)
      but not exceeding the sum of all claims for benefits payable under subsection (c).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.8. Administration and enforcement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7D. Self-Insurance Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.8. Administration and enforcement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1037.8. Administration and enforcement (2023)
content:
The department may promulgate rules and regulations for the administration and enforcement
   of this article.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7E. Health and Safety›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1038.2. Certification of safety committee
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7E. Health and Safety › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1038.2. Certification of safety committee
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1038.2. Certification of safety committee (2023)
content:
(a) An insured employer may make application to the department for the certification
      of any established safety committee operative within its workplace developed for the
      purpose of hazard detection, accident prevention and providing information regarding
      the risks associated with substance abuse, including opioid painkiller use.  The department shall develop such certification criteria.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7E. Health and Safety›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1038.1. Accident and illness prevention services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7E. Health and Safety › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1038.1. Accident and illness prevention services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1038.1. Accident and illness prevention services (2023)
content:
(a) Notwithstanding any other provision of law, an insurer desiring to write workers'
      compensation insurance in this Commonwealth shall maintain or provide accident and
      illness prevention services as a prerequisite for a license to write such insurance.  Proof of compliance with this section shall be provided to the commissioner.  Such services shall be adequate to furnish accident prevention required by the nature
      of its business or its policyholders' operations and shall include surveys, recommendations,
      training programs, consultations, analyses of accident causes, industrial hygiene
      and industrial health services to implement the program of accident prevention services.  The insurer, pursuant to its responsibilities under this section, shall employ or
      otherwise make available qualified accident and illness prevention personnel.  Such personnel shall meet the qualifications set forth in regulations issued by
      the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.2. Offenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.2. Offenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.2. Offenses (2023)
content:
A person, including, but not limited to, the employer, the employe, the health care
   provider, the attorney, the insurer, the State Workmen's Insurance Fund and self-insureds,
   commits an offense if the person does any of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.3. Compensation paid by lawyers or health care providers to secure employment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.3. Compensation paid by lawyers or health care providers to secure employment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.3. Compensation paid by lawyers or health care providers to secure employment (2023)
content:
(a) A lawyer may not compensate or give anything of value to a nonlawyer to recommend
      or secure employment by a client or as a reward for having made a recommendation resulting
      in employment by a client, except that the lawyer may pay:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.1. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.1. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.1. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this article shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.5. Punishment for offenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.5. Punishment for offenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.5. Punishment for offenses (2023)
content:
(a) A person who violates section 11021shall be guilty of a felony of the third degree and, upon conviction thereof, shall
      be sentenced to pay a fine of not more than fifty thousand dollars ($50,000) or double
      the value of the fraud or to undergo imprisonment for a period of not more than seven
      years, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.4. Electronic submission of claims
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.4. Electronic submission of claims
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.4. Electronic submission of claims (2023)
content:
If an insurance claim is made by means of computer billing tapes or other electronic
   means, it shall be a rebuttable presumption that the person knowingly made the claim
   if the person has advised the insurer in writing that claims will be submitted by
   use of computer billing tapes or other electronic means.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.8. Permitted conduct; attorneys and health care providers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.8. Permitted conduct; attorneys and health care providers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.8. Permitted conduct; attorneys and health care providers (2023)
content:
Nothing in this article shall be construed to prohibit any conduct by an attorney
   or law firm which is expressly permitted by the Rules of Professional Conduct of the
   Supreme Court, by statute or by regulation, or prohibit any conduct by a health care
   provider which is expressly permitted by law or regulation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.7. Immunity from liability for supplying information in connection with allegations of fraud
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.7. Immunity from liability for supplying information in connection with allegations of fraud
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.7. Immunity from liability for supplying information in connection with allegations of fraud (2023)
content:
An insurer and any agent, servant or employe thereof acting in the course and scope
   of his employment shall be immune from civil or criminal liability arising from the
   supply or release of written or oral information to any entity duly authorized to
   receive such information by Federal or State law or by Insurance Department regulations
   only if the information is supplied to the agency in connection with an allegation
   of fraudulent conduct on the part of any person relating to a violation of this article
   and the insurer, agent, servant or employe has reason to believe that the information
   supplied is related to the allegation of fraud.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.9. Criminal proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.9. Criminal proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.9. Criminal proceedings (2023)
content:
(a) The district attorneys of the several counties shall have authority to investigate
      and to institute criminal proceedings for any violation of this article.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.10. Authority of Commonwealth departments and agencies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.10. Authority of Commonwealth departments and agencies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.10. Authority of Commonwealth departments and agencies (2023)
content:
Nothing contained in this article shall be construed to limit the regulatory or investigative
   authority of any department or agency of the Commonwealth whose functions might relate
   to persons, enterprises or matters falling within the scope of this article.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7G. Fraud Enforcement›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1040.3. Insurance antifraud plan
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7G. Fraud Enforcement › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1040.3. Insurance antifraud plan
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1040.3. Insurance antifraud plan (2023)
content:
A workers' compensation insurer shall institute and maintain an insurance antifraud
   plan.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7G. Fraud Enforcement›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1040.1. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7G. Fraud Enforcement › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1040.1. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1040.1. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this article shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.6. Restitution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.6. Restitution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.6. Restitution (2023)
content:
The court may, in addition to any other sentence authorized by law, sentence a person
   convicted of violating this section to make restitution under18 Pa.C.S § 1106(relating to restitution for injuries to person or property).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7G. Fraud Enforcement›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1040.4. Annual summary report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7G. Fraud Enforcement › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1040.4. Annual summary report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1040.4. Annual summary report (2023)
content:
All workers' compensation insurers shall annually provide to the department a summary
   report on actions taken under an antifraud plan to prevent and combat insurance fraud,
   including, but not limited to, measures taken to protect and ensure the integrity
   of electronic data processing-generated data and manually compiled data, statistical
   data on the amount of resources committed to combating fraud and the amount of fraud
   identified and recovered during the reporting period.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.11. Fines and penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.11. Fines and penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.11. Fines and penalties (2023)
content:
(a) A person found by a court of competent jurisdiction, pursuant to a claim initiated
      by a prosecuting authority, to have violated any provision of section 11021shall be subject to civil penalties of not more than five thousand dollars ($5,000)
      for the first violation, ten thousand dollars ($10,000) for the second violation and
      fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000) for each subsequent violation.  The penalty shall be paid to the prosecuting authority to be used to defray the
      operating expenses of investigating and prosecuting violations of this article.  The court may also award court costs and reasonable attorney fees to the prosecuting
      authority.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.12. Limitations for prosecutions of offenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7F. Insurance Fraud › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.12. Limitations for prosecutions of offenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1039.12. Limitations for prosecutions of offenses (2023)
content:
A prosecution for an offense under this act must be commenced within five years after
   commission of the offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7G. Fraud Enforcement›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1040.5. Insurer referral of violations to law enforcement officials
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7G. Fraud Enforcement › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1040.5. Insurer referral of violations to law enforcement officials
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1040.5. Insurer referral of violations to law enforcement officials (2023)
content:
(a) Every workers' compensation insurer and its employes, agents and brokers are authorized
      to refer to the appropriate law enforcement official violations of Article XI if the
      insurer, employe, agent or broker has reason to believe that a person has engaged
      in or is engaging in an act or practice that violates Article XI.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1062. Notice of pending claims against insolvent carriers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1062. Notice of pending claims against insolvent carriers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1062. Notice of pending claims against insolvent carriers (2023)
content:
After the effective date of this act, upon any carrier becoming insolvent the commissioner
   shall so notify the Workmen's Compensation Board, which shall immediately advise the
   commissioner--(a) of all claims for compensation pending or thereafter made against
   every employer insured by such insolvent carrier, or against such insolvent carrier;
   (b) of all unpaid or continuing awards made upon claims for compensation prior to
   or after the date of such notice from the commissioner;  and (c) of all appeals from
   or applications for modification, recision or review of such awards.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7H. Small Business Advocate›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1041.1. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7H. Small Business Advocate › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1041.1. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1041.1. Definitions (2023)
content: As used in this article:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7G. Fraud Enforcement›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1040.2. Department referral of violations to law enforcement officials
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7G. Fraud Enforcement › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1040.2. Department referral of violations to law enforcement officials
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1040.2. Department referral of violations to law enforcement officials (2023)
content:
(a) The department is authorized to refer to the appropriate law enforcement official
      violations of Article XI1if the department has reason to believe that a person has engaged in or is engaging
      in an act or practice that violates Article XI.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7H. Small Business Advocate›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1041.3. Annual assessment on insurers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7H. Small Business Advocate › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1041.3. Annual assessment on insurers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1041.3. Annual assessment on insurers (2023)
content:
(a) In addition to any other assessment authorized by section 446,1an additional annual assessment shall be made on insurers, including the State Workmen's
      Insurance Fund but not including self-insureds, as a percentage of the total compensation
      paid for the purpose of funding the operations of the Office of Small Business Advocate
      pursuant to this act.  Assessments under this section shall be made by the department and deposited into
      the Workmen's Compensation Administration Fund in a restricted account to be used
      by the Office of Small Business Advocate.  The total amount assessed shall be the amount of the budget approved annually by
      the General Assembly for the operations of the Office of Small Business Advocate pursuant
      to this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7H. Small Business Advocate›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1041.4. Proceedings before department or courts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7H. Small Business Advocate › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1041.4. Proceedings before department or courts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1041.4. Proceedings before department or courts (2023)
content:
Nothing contained in this article shall in any way limit the right of any person to
   bring a proceeding before either the department or a court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 7H. Small Business Advocate›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1041.2. Standing to represent employers' interests
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 7H. Small Business Advocate › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1041.2. Standing to represent employers' interests
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1041.2. Standing to represent employers' interests (2023)
content:
In addition to his powers and duties under the act of December 21, 1988 (P.L. 1871,
   No. 181), known as the “Small Business Advocate Act,”1the small business advocate shall have standing to represent the interest of employers
   as a party in proceedings before the department or any court involving filings by
   rating organizations and insurers pursuant to Article VII.2

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1051. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1051. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1051. Short title (2023)
content:
This act shall be known, and may be cited, as the “Workers' Compensation Security
   Fund Act.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1052. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1052. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1052. Definitions (2023)
content: As hereafter used in this act, unless the context or subject matter otherwise require--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1054. Returns by stock companies and mutual carriers and reciprocal exchanges
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1054. Returns by stock companies and mutual carriers and reciprocal exchanges
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1054. Returns by stock companies and mutual carriers and reciprocal exchanges (2023)
content:
Every stock company, mutual carrier and reciprocal exchange shall, on or before the
   first day of September, one thousand nine hundred and thirty-eight, file with the
   Treasurer of the Commonwealth, and with the commissioner, identical returns under
   oath, on a form to be prescribed and furnished by the commissioner, stating the amount
   of net written premiums for the year's period ending June thirtieth, one thousand
   nine hundred and thirty-eight, on policies issued, renewed, or extended by such stock
   company, mutual carrier and reciprocal exchange to insure payment of compensation
   pursuant to the Workmen's Compensation Law.  For the purposes of this act, “net written premiums” shall mean gross written premiums,
   less return premiums on policies returned not taken and on policies cancelled.  Thereafter on or before the first day of September of each year, each such stock
   company, mutual carrier and reciprocal exchange shall file similar identical returns,
   stating the amount of such net written premiums for the year's period ending on the
   preceding June thirtieth on policies issued, renewed, or extended by such stock company,
   mutual carrier and reciprocal exchange.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1053. Fund for insuring payments by insolvent stock companies and mutual carriers and reciprocal exchanges and the insolvent State Workmen's Insurance Fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1053. Fund for insuring payments by insolvent stock companies and mutual carriers and reciprocal exchanges and the insolvent State Workmen's Insurance Fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1053. Fund for insuring payments by insolvent stock companies and mutual carriers and reciprocal exchanges and the insolvent State Workmen's Insurance Fund (2023)
content:
There is hereby created a fund, to be known as “The Workers' Compensation Security
   Fund,” for the purpose of assuring to persons entitled thereto the compensation provided
   by the Workmen's Compensation Law for employments insured in insolvent stock companies;
   insolvent mutual carriers;  insolvent reciprocal exchanges;  or the State Workmen's
   Insurance Fund.  Such fund shall be applicable to the payment of valid claims for compensation heretofore
   or hereafter made pursuant to the Workmen's Compensation Law and remaining unpaid,
   in whole or in part, by reason of the default, after the effective date of this act
   of an insolvent stock company;  insolvent mutual carrier or insolvent reciprocal exchange
   or the insolvent State Workmen's Insurance Fund.  Expenses of administration also shall be paid from the fund as herein provided.  Such fund shall consist of all contributions received and paid into the fund by
   stock companies, mutual carriers and reciprocal exchanges as herein defined, all property
   and securities acquired by and through the use of moneys belonging to the fund, and
   of interest earned upon moneys deposited or invested, as herein provided.  The fund shall be administered by the commissioner in accordance with the provisions
   of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1060. Custody and management of fund; company ceasing to do business
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1060. Custody and management of fund; company ceasing to do business
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1060. Custody and management of fund; company ceasing to do business (2023)
content:
(1) The fund created by this act shall be separate and apart from all other Commonwealth
      moneys.  The State Treasurer shall be the custodian of said fund, and all disbursements from
      said fund shall be made by the State Treasurer upon vouchers signed by the commissioner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1064. Expenses of administration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1064. Expenses of administration
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1064. Expenses of administration (2023)
content:
The expenses of administering the fund shall be paid out of such fund.  The commissioner shall serve as administrator of the fund without additional remuneration,
   but may be allowed and paid, from the fund, expenses incurred in the performance of
   his duties in connection with the fund.  The compensation of persons employed by the commissioner, for the purposes of this
   act, in connection with the fund shall be deemed administration expenses payable out
   of such fund, in the manner provided in section ten of this act.1The commissioner shall include in his regular report to the Governor a statement
   of the expenses of administering the fund during the period covered by such report.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1059. Rules and regulations; failure to make returns; revocation of authority
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1059. Rules and regulations; failure to make returns; revocation of authority
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1059. Rules and regulations; failure to make returns; revocation of authority (2023)
content:
(1) The Insurance Department shall adopt regulations as necessary to administer the
      fund, including regulations to establish contributions to be paid to the fund.   Contributions shall be established on an actuarial basis to provide an amount sufficient
      to pay outstanding and anticipated claims in a timely manner, to meet the costs of
      the Insurance Department to administer the fund and to maintain a minimum balance
      in the fund of $500,000,000.  Nothing in this section shall prevent the department from using money in the fund
      to pay liabilities and claims.  If, due to the payment of liabilities or claims, the balance of the fund is reduced
      below $500,000,000, the department shall require contributions to maintain the actuarial
      soundness of the fund and to restore, in a timely manner, the balance of the fund
      to a level at or above $500,000,000.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1063. Defense of pending claims
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1063. Defense of pending claims
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1063. Defense of pending claims (2023)
content:
The commissioner, or a representative committee of interested carriers which the commissioner
   may from time to time appoint, or both, may investigate and defend before the Workmen's
   Compensation Board or any court, any and all claims for compensation against an employer
   insured by an insolvent carrier, or against an insolvent carrier, and may prosecute
   any pending appeal from, or may appeal from, or make application for modification,
   recision or review of any agreement, award or decision against any such employer or
   carrier.  Until all such claims for compensation are closed and all awards are paid, the commissioner,
   as administrator of the funds, shall be a party in interest in respect to all such
   claims, agreements and awards.  For the purposes of this section, the commissioner shall have exclusive power to
   select and employ such clerks and assistants as may be deemed necessary, and to fix
   and determine their powers and duties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1061. Payment of claims against insolvent carriers; recovery against insolvent carriers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1061. Payment of claims against insolvent carriers; recovery against insolvent carriers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1061. Payment of claims against insolvent carriers; recovery against insolvent carriers (2023)
content:
(1) A valid claim for compensation or installments thereof, heretofore or hereafter
      made pursuant to the Workmen's Compensation Law, as defined herein, which has remained
      or shall remain due and unpaid for sixty days by reason of default, after the effective
      date of this act, by an insolvent carrier, shall be paid from the fund in the manner
      provided in this act.  Any person in interest may file with the commissioner an application for payment
      of compensation from the fund on a form to be prescribed and furnished by the commissioner.  A certified copy of the award must accompany the application.  The commissioner shall thereupon certify to the State Treasurer such award for payment
      according to the terms of the same, whereupon payment shall be made by the State Treasurer,
      on warrant of the Auditor General and on requisition of the commissioner.  Claimants receiving benefits from the fund by virtue of Longshore and Harbor Workers'
      Compensation Act (44 Stat. 1424,33 U.S.C. § 901 et seq.) awards shall be subject to the provisions of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1065.1. Transfer of assets and reserves and surplus liabilities to Workers' Compensation Security Fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1065.1. Transfer of assets and reserves and surplus liabilities to Workers' Compensation Security Fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1065.1. Transfer of assets and reserves and surplus liabilities to Workers' Compensation Security Fund (2023)
content:
All assets, moneys, securities, reserves, surplus liabilities and the like presently
   in either the Stock Workmen's Compensation Security Fund or the Mutual Carrier and
   Reciprocal Exchange Workmen's Compensation Security Fund shall forthwith be transferred
   to the single Workers' Compensation Security Fund created hereby.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1065. Contributions, provisions concerning
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1065. Contributions, provisions concerning
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1065. Contributions, provisions concerning (2023)
content:
Other than the obligation to contribute to the fund as provided in this act, no deposit,
   bond or other security shall be required of any carrier as a condition to authorization
   to transact the business of workmen's compensation insurance in this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article I. Interpretation and Definitions›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1202. Number and gender
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article I. Interpretation and Definitions › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1202. Number and gender
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1202. Number and gender (2023)
content:
Wherever in this act the singular is used, the plural shall be included;  and where
   the masculine gender is used, the feminine and neuter shall be included.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article I. Interpretation and Definitions›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1205. “Contractor” defined
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article I. Interpretation and Definitions › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1205. “Contractor” defined
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1205. “Contractor” defined (2023)
content:
The term “contractor,” as used in article two, section two hundred and three,1and article three, section three hundred and two (b),2shall not include a contractor engaged in an independent business, other than that
   of supplying laborers or assistants, in which he serves persons other than the employer
   in whose service the disability occurs, but shall include a subcontractor to whom
   a principal contractor has sublet any part of the work which such principal contractor
   has undertaken.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1066. Partial invalidity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 8. Workers' Compensation Security Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1066. Partial invalidity
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1066. Partial invalidity (2023)
content:
If any part of this act be adjudged unconstitutional, it shall not invalidate the
   remainder of the act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article I. Interpretation and Definitions›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1201. Short title; general application
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article I. Interpretation and Definitions › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1201. Short title; general application
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1201. Short title; general application (2023)
content:
This act shall be called and may be cited as The Pennsylvania Occupational Disease
   Act.  It shall apply to disabilities and deaths caused by occupational disease as defined
   in this act, resulting from employment within this Commonwealth, irrespective of the
   place where the contract of hiring was made, renewed, or extended, and shall not apply
   to any such disabilities and deaths resulting from employment outside of the Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article I. Interpretation and Definitions›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1206. Public authority, trade or business
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article I. Interpretation and Definitions › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1206. Public authority, trade or business
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1206. Public authority, trade or business (2023)
content:
The exercise and performance of the powers and duties of a local or other public authority
   shall, for the purposes of this act, be treated as the trade or business of the authority.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article I. Interpretation and Definitions›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1203. “Employer” defined
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article I. Interpretation and Definitions › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1203. “Employer” defined
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1203. “Employer” defined (2023)
content:
The term “employer,” as used in this act, is declared to be synonymous with master,
   and to include natural persons, partnerships, joint-stock companies, corporations
   for profit, corporations not for profit, municipal corporations, the Commonwealth,
   and all governmental agencies created by it.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article I. Interpretation and Definitions›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1204. “Employe” defined
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article I. Interpretation and Definitions › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1204. “Employe” defined
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1204. “Employe” defined (2023)
content:
The term “employe,” as used in this act, is declared to be synonymous with servant,
   and includes all natural persons who perform services, except agricultural services
   or domestic services performed in a private home, for another for a valuable consideration,
   exclusive of persons whose employment is casual in character and not in the regular
   course of the business of the employer and exclusive of persons to whom articles or
   materials are given out to be made up, cleaned, washed, altered, ornamented, finished,
   or repaired, or adapted for sale, in the worker's own home, or on other premises not
   under the control or management of the employer.  Every executive officer of a corporation elected or appointed in accordance with
   the charter and by-laws of the corporation, except elected officers of the Commonwealth
   or any of its political subdivisions, shall be an employe of the corporation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article I. Interpretation and Definitions›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1209. Disability or death resulting from military activities or enemy sabotage
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article I. Interpretation and Definitions › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1209. Disability or death resulting from military activities or enemy sabotage
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1209. Disability or death resulting from military activities or enemy sabotage (2023)
content:
No compensation shall be paid for any occupational disease if, during hostile attacks
   on the United States, disability or death of an employe results solely from military
   activities of the armed forces of the United States or from military activities or
   enemy sabotage of a foreign power.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article I. Interpretation and Definitions›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1208. Occupational diseases enumerated
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article I. Interpretation and Definitions › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1208. Occupational diseases enumerated
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1208. Occupational diseases enumerated (2023)
content: The term “occupational disease,” as used in this act, shall mean only the following diseases:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article II. Damages by Action at Law›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1302. Negligence of employe, liability for
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article II. Damages by Action at Law › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1302. Negligence of employe, liability for
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1302. Negligence of employe, liability for (2023)
content:
The employer shall be liable for the negligence of employes other than the plaintiff,
   while acting within the scope of their employment, including engineers, chauffeurs,
   miners, mine-foremen, fire-bosses, mine superintendents, plumbers, officers of vessels,
   and all other employes licensed by the Commonwealth or other governmental authority,
   if the employer be allowed by law the right of free selection of such employes from
   the class of persons thus licensed;  and such employes shall be the agents and representatives
   of their employers, and their employers shall be responsible for the acts and neglects
   of such employes, as in the case of other agents and employes of their employers;
   and, notwithstanding the employment of such employes, the property in and about which
   they are employed, and the use and operation thereof, shall at all times be under
   the supervision, management and control of their employers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article I. Interpretation and Definitions›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1207. “Department,” “board,” “referee” defined
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article I. Interpretation and Definitions › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1207. “Department,” “board,” “referee” defined
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1207. “Department,” “board,” “referee” defined (2023)
content:
The term “department,” when used in this act, shall mean the Department of Labor and
   Industry of this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article II. Damages by Action at Law›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1301. Negligence of fellow employe, no defense
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article II. Damages by Action at Law › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1301. Negligence of fellow employe, no defense
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1301. Negligence of fellow employe, no defense (2023)
content:
In any action brought to recover damages for disability or death of an employe caused
   by occupational disease arising out of and in the course of his employment, it shall
   not be a defense that the occupational disease was caused in whole or in part by the
   negligence of a fellow employe.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article II. Damages by Action at Law›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1304. Agreements outside act not valid; benefits from other sources
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article II. Damages by Action at Law › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1304. Agreements outside act not valid; benefits from other sources
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1304. Agreements outside act not valid; benefits from other sources (2023)
content:
No agreement, composition, or release of damages made before the date of any disability
   or death resulting from occupational disease, except the agreement defined in article
   three of this act,1shall be valid or shall bar a claim for damages for such disability or death;  and
   any such agreement other than that defined in article three herein, is declared to
   be against the public policy of this Commonwealth.  The receipt of benefits from any association, society, or fund shall not bar the
   recovery of damages by action at law, nor the recovery of compensation under article
   three hereof;  and any release executed in consideration of such benefits shall be
   void:  Provided, however, That if the employe receives unemployment compensation benefits,
   such amount or amounts so received shall be credited as against the amount of the
   award made under the provisions of the occupational disease act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article II. Damages by Action at Law›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1303. Hiring by employe, assistant, or contractor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article II. Damages by Action at Law › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1303. Hiring by employe, assistant, or contractor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1303. Hiring by employe, assistant, or contractor (2023)
content:
An employer who permits the entry upon premises occupied by him or under his control
   of a laborer or an assistant hired by an employe or contractor who has rejected article
   three of this act,1for the performance upon such premises of a part of the employer's regular business
   entrusted to such employe or contractor, shall be liable to such laborer or assistant
   in the same manner and to the same extent as to his own employe.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article II. Damages by Action at Law›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1305. Liability of fellow employe
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article II. Damages by Action at Law › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1305. Liability of fellow employe
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1305. Liability of fellow employe (2023)
content:
If disability or death is compensable under this act, a person shall not be liable
   to anyone at common law or otherwise on account of such disability or death for any
   act or omission occurring while such person was in the same employ as the person disabled
   or killed, except for intentional wrong.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article III. Elective Compensation›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1403. Acceptance; persons bound
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article III. Elective Compensation › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1403. Acceptance; persons bound
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1403. Acceptance; persons bound (2023)
content:
Such agreement shall constitute an acceptance of all the provisions of article three
   of this act,1and shall operate as a surrender by the parties thereto of their rights to any form
   or amount of compensation or damages for any disability or death resulting from occupational
   disease, or to any method of determination thereof, other than as provided in article
   three of this act.  Such agreement shall bind the employer and his personal representatives, and the
   employe, his or her wife, or husband, widow or widower, next of kin, and other dependents.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article III. Elective Compensation›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1404. Termination of agreement as to operation or non-operation of article three
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article III. Elective Compensation › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1404. Termination of agreement as to operation or non-operation of article three
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1404. Termination of agreement as to operation or non-operation of article three (2023)
content:
Any agreement between employer and employe for the operation or nonoperation of the
   provisions of article three of this act1may be terminated by the posting of notice by the employer or by either party upon
   thirty days' notice to the other in writing, if a copy of such notice, with proof
   of posting or proof of service, be filed in the department as provided in section
   three hundred and two of this article.2

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article III. Elective Compensation›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1402. Presumption of acceptance; rejection of act; Commonwealth or subdivisions; assistant hired on premises; intermediate employer or contractor; notice to employes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article III. Elective Compensation › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1402. Presumption of acceptance; rejection of act; Commonwealth or subdivisions; assistant hired on premises; intermediate employer or contractor; notice to employes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1402. Presumption of acceptance; rejection of act; Commonwealth or subdivisions; assistant hired on premises; intermediate employer or contractor; notice to employes (2023)
content:
(a) In every contract of hiring made after October first, one thousand nine hundred
      and thirty-nine, and in every contract of hiring renewed or extended by mutual consent,
      expressed or implied, after said date, it shall be conclusively presumed that the
      parties have accepted the provisions of article three of this act,1and have agreed to be bound thereby, unless the employer shall post at his plant,
      office or place of business a notice of his intention not to pay such compensation
      or unless there be, at the time of the making, renewal, or extension of such contract,
      an express statement in writing, from either party to the other, that the provisions
      of article three of this act are not intended to apply, and unless a true copy of
      such posted notice or such written statement, accompanied by proof of posting or proof
      of service thereof upon the other party, setting forth under oath or affirmation the
      time, place, and manner of such posting or service, be filed with the department within
      twenty days after such posting or service.  Every contract of hiring, oral, written, or implied from circumstances, now in operation,
      or made or implied on or before October first, one thousand nine hundred and thirty-nine,
      shall be conclusively presumed to continue subject to the provisions of article three
      hereof, unless the employer shall on or before said date either post at his plant,
      office or place of business a notice of his intention not to pay such compensation
      or unless either party shall, on or before said date, in writing, have notified the
      other party to such contract that the provisions of article three hereof are not intended
      to apply, and unless there shall be filed with the department a true copy of such
      notice, together with proof of posting or service, within the time and in the manner
      hereinabove prescribed:  Provided, however, That the provisions of this section shall
      not be so construed as to impair the obligation of any contract now in force.  Such posted notice shall constitute sufficient notice to all employes and to the
      parents and guardians of all minor employes, and a certified copy of proof of posting
      or proof of service shall be prima facie evidence of notice.  It shall not be lawful for any officer or agent of this Commonwealth, or for any
      county, city, borough, town, or township therein, or for any officer or agent thereof,
      or for any other governmental authority created by the laws of this Commonwealth,
      to give such notice of rejection of the provisions of this article to any employe
      of the Commonwealth or of such governmental agency.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article III. Elective Compensation›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1404.1. Instructions brochure; employe's rights
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article III. Elective Compensation › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1404.1. Instructions brochure; employe's rights
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1404.1. Instructions brochure; employe's rights (2023)
content:
The Secretary of Labor and Industry shall, within ninety (90) days after the effective
   date of this amendatory act, prepare a brochure of instructions, setting forth the
   rights of an employe in the event of disability or death caused by occupational disease
   and informing him of the time and manner in which claims should be filed.  A copy of such brochure shall be provided each insurance company authorized to write
   insurance policies covering occupational diseases under this act.  Such insurance companies shall prepare at their own expense copies of said brochure
   for distribution to such insured employers.  Each insurance company shall prepare the brochures immediately upon receipt of the
   sample brochure from the Secretary of Labor and Industry in such quantity as required
   by employers for distribution to each employe.  The employer shall distribute such brochures to each employe at the time of hiring
   and to each existing employe within thirty (30) days after the receipt of the brochure.
