title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2611. Payment of moneys from fund; annual actuarial study; distribution of surplus
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2611. Payment of moneys from fund; annual actuarial study; distribution of surplus (2023)
content: (a) The moneys in the fund are hereby made available and shall be paid:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2615. Inspection of premises; examination of records; rules and regulations for prevention of injuries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2615. Inspection of premises; examination of records; rules and regulations for prevention of injuries
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2615. Inspection of premises; examination of records; rules and regulations for prevention of injuries (2023)
content:
(a) The board shall be entitled to inspect the plant, workroom, shop, farm, mine,
      quarry, operation and all other property or premises of any subscriber and shall be
      entitled to examine from time to time the books, records and payrolls of any subscriber
      or intending subscriber for the purpose of determining the amount of the premium payable
      to such subscriber or intending subscriber.  The board shall have the power to appoint those inspectors and auditors as may be
      necessary to carry out the powers given in this section.  The board may, with the consent of the department and commissioner, cause this inspection
      and examination to be made by the inspectors of the department and the auditors of
      the Insurance Department.  These inspectors and auditors shall have free access to all such premises, books,
      records and payrolls during the regular working and office hours.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2617. Payment of premiums
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2617. Payment of premiums
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2617. Payment of premiums (2023)
content:
All premiums shall be payable to the State Treasurer who shall issue an appropriate
   receipt therefor, and such receipt, together with the certificate of the board specified
   in section 1516,1shall be the evidence that the applicant has become a subscriber to the fund and
   is insured therein.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2619. Offenses and penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2619. Offenses and penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2619. Offenses and penalties (2023)
content:
Any person who shall knowingly furnish or make any false certificate, application
   or statement required in this article shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.  Any subscriber who shall, after notice from the board, neglect or refuse to file
   the statement described in section 15181within ten (10) days after such notice shall be liable to pay to the fund a penalty
   of ten dollars ($10) for each day that such neglect or refusal shall continue, to
   be recovered at the suit of the fund.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2616. Application to become a subscriber
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2616. Application to become a subscriber
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2616. Application to become a subscriber (2023)
content:
(a) Any employer subject to Article III and who shall desire to become a subscriber
      to the fund for the purpose of insuring his liability to his employes;  and any employer
      who wants insurance under the Longshore and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act (44 Stat.
      1424,33 U.S.C. § 901 et seq.);  and any employer who wants insurance under the Federal Coal Mine Health and Safety
      Act of 1969 (Public Law 91-173,30 U.S.C. § 801 et seq.) and who shall desire to become a subscriber to the fund for the purpose of insuring
      his liability to his employes;  and any employer who shall desire to become a subscriber
      to the fund for the purpose of insuring therein his liability for all sums the employer
      shall become legally obligated to pay any employe of his as damages because of bodily
      injury by accident or disease, including death at any time resulting therefrom, sustained
      by such employe arising out of and in the course of his employment, shall make a written
      application for such insurance to the board.  In the application, the applicant shall state:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2618. Statement of subscriber upon termination of subscription
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2618. Statement of subscriber upon termination of subscription
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2618. Statement of subscriber upon termination of subscription (2023)
content:
Each subscriber to the fund shall, within one (1) month after his subscription has
   terminated, furnish a written statement to the board setting forth the maximum average
   and minimum number of employes insured in the fund that such subscriber had employed
   during the preceding year, and the actual amount of the money payroll of such employes
   for such year.  When the board has subdivided the employments in any group into classes, as provided
   in section 1510,1the subscriber shall state the number and actual amounts of the money payroll of
   such employes of each of such classes.  Within thirty (30) days, the board shall state the account of each subscriber for
   that year, based on the facts thus proven, and shall render a copy of this statement
   to the subscriber.  If the amount of the premium theretofore paid by a subscriber shall exceed the amount
   due according to such stated account, then the excess shall be forthwith refunded
   to the subscriber by payment out of the fund.  If the amount shown by the statement exceeds the amount of the premium theretofore
   paid by the subscriber, the excess shall be forthwith due and payable by the subscriber
   into the fund, and until paid shall be a lien, as State taxes are a lien, upon the
   real and personal property of the subscriber and, if unpaid, shall be collectible
   as State taxes are now collectible, with interest at the rate of twelve per centum
   per annum commencing thirty (30) days after service of the copy of the account, which
   service shall be by registered mail.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2620. Discharge from liability
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2620. Discharge from liability
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2620. Discharge from liability (2023)
content:
(a) Any subscriber to the fund who shall, within seven (7) days after knowledge or
      notice of an accident to an employe in the course of his employment as required by
      section 311,1have filed with the board a true statement of such knowledge or a true copy of the
      notice shall be discharged from all liability for the payment of compensation for
      the personal injury or death of such employe by such accident, and all such compensation
      due therefor under Article III shall be paid out of the fund.  The report of the accident required by the act of July 19, 1913 (P.L. 843, No. 408),2referred to as the Employee Injury Reporting Law, shall be sufficient compliance
      with this section if that report is made within seven (7) days of the injury and shall
      state that the employer making the report is a subscriber to the fund.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2623. Execution of agreements and promulgation of regulations; payment of benefits and damages
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2623. Execution of agreements and promulgation of regulations; payment of benefits and damages
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2623. Execution of agreements and promulgation of regulations; payment of benefits and damages (2023)
content:
(a) The board is hereby empowered to execute the agreements provided in this act and
      to promulgate such regulations as they may deem necessary for this purpose.  When any such agreement has been approved by the department, the same shall be properly
      filed and docketed, and the board shall from time to time until such agreement shall
      be modified or terminated as provided in this act pay the sums therein agreed upon.  All such payments shall be made by check of the State Treasurer issued upon requisition
      of the secretary.  Every such check shall be mailed to the person or persons entitled thereto under
      such agreement.  When any award is made by the Workers' Compensation Appeal Board or by a workers'
      compensation judge in any proceedings brought by an employe of a subscriber or the
      dependents of such employe against the fund, this award shall be filed and docketed,
      and the board shall from time to time until such award is modified, reversed or terminated
      pay the sums therein lawfully awarded against the fund.  All such payments shall be made by check of the State Treasurer issued upon requisition
      of the secretary, and every such check shall be mailed to the person or persons entitled
      thereto under the award.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2622. Investigation of accidents
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2622. Investigation of accidents
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2622. Investigation of accidents (2023)
content:
Upon receipt of a notice or statement of knowledge of an accident to an employe of
   a subscriber occurring in the course of his employment, the board shall, if it deems
   necessary, cause an investigation to be made by an inspector appointed by it or an
   inspector of the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2701. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2701. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2701. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this article shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2624. Payment of compensation for administration of the fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2624. Payment of compensation for administration of the fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2624. Payment of compensation for administration of the fund (2023)
content:
All salaries, wages, fees or other compensation of physicians, attorneys, investigators,
   assistants and other employes necessary for the proper administration of the fund
   and the proper conduct of the work of the board shall be paid out of the fund.  All payments to employes, dependents of deceased employes, physicians, attorneys,
   investigators, assistants and others entitled to be paid out of the fund shall be
   made by the State Treasurer upon requisition of the secretary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2625. Information not open to public inspection
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2625. Information not open to public inspection
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2625. Information not open to public inspection (2023)
content:
Information acquired by the fund, its officers and employes from employers, employes
   or insurance corporations or associations shall not be open to public inspection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2621. Subrogation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 11. State Workers' Insurance Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2621. Subrogation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2621. Subrogation (2023)
content:
In every case where a claim is made against the fund, the fund shall be entitled to
   every defense against such claim that would have been open to the employer and shall
   be subrogated to every right of the employer arising out of such accident against
   the employe, the dependents and against third persons.  The fund may, in the name of the State Workers' Insurance Fund, sue or be sued to
   enforce any right given against or to any subscriber or other person under this act
   or the Longshore and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act (44 Stat. 1424,33 U.S.C. § 901 et seq.) or the Federal Coal Mine Health and Safety Act of 1969 (Public Law 91-173,30 U.S.C. § 801 et seq.) and employers1who want insurance against liability for all sums or under circumstances where an
   employer becomes legally obligated to pay any employe for damages because of bodily
   injury by accident or disease, including death at any time resulting therefrom, sustained
   by such employe arising out of and in the course of his employment;  proceedings provided
   in Article IV may be instituted by or against the fund to enforce, before the Workers'
   Compensation Appeal Board or any workers' compensation judge thereof, the rights given
   to or against the fund by this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2703. Claims
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2703. Claims
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2703. Claims (2023)
content:
(a) Scope.--This section shall apply to claims for an injury or a death which occurs on or after
      the effective date of this article.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2705. Department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2705. Department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2705. Department (2023)
content:
(a) Insurance inquiry.--Within ten days of notice of a claim, the fund shall demand from the employer proof
      of applicable insurance coverage.  Within 14 days from the date of the fund's request, the employer must provide proof
      of insurance.  If the employer does not provide proof, there shall be rebuttable presumption of
      uninsurance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2706. Other remedies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2706. Other remedies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2706. Other remedies (2023)
content:
Nothing contained in this article shall serve to abrogate the provisions of section
   305(d)1allowing the claimant or dependents to bring a direct suit for damages at law as
   provided by Article II.  The fund shall be entitled to assert rights to subrogation under section 3192for recovery made from the employer or any other third party.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2704. Claim petition
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2704. Claim petition
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2704. Claim petition (2023)
content:
(a) Authorization.--If a claim for compensation is filed under this article and the claim is not voluntarily
      accepted as compensable, the employee may file a claim petition naming both the employer
      and the fund as defendants.  Failure of the uninsured employer to answer a claim petition shall not serve as
      an admission or otherwise bind the fund under section 416.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2709. Uninsured employer obligations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2709. Uninsured employer obligations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2709. Uninsured employer obligations (2023)
content:
Nothing in this article shall alter the uninsured employer's obligations under this
   act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2707. Assessments and transfers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2707. Assessments and transfers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2707. Assessments and transfers (2023)
content:
(a)(1) The department shall calculate the amount necessary to maintain the fund and
         shall assess insurers and self-insured employers as is necessary to provide an amount
         sufficient to pay outstanding and anticipated claims in the following year in a timely
         manner and to meet the costs of the department to administer the fund.  The fund shall be maintained in the same manner as the Workmen's Compensation Administration
         Fund under section 4461and the regulations thereunder.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund›PA ST 77 P.S. § 2708. Regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 12. Uninsured Employers Guaranty Fund › PA ST 77 P.S. § 2708. Regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 2708. Regulations (2023)
content:
The department may promulgate regulations for the administration and enforcement of
   this article.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation›Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases›Article IV. Procedure›PA ST 77 P.S. § 1513. Review and modification of agreements; powers of board or referee; supersedeas
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 77 P.S. Workers' Compensation › Chapter 9. Occupational Diseases › Article IV. Procedure › PA ST 77 P.S. § 1513. Review and modification of agreements; powers of board or referee; supersedeas
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 77 P.S. § 1513. Review and modification of agreements; powers of board or referee; supersedeas (2023)
content:
The board, or a referee designated by the board, may, at any time, review and modify
   or set aside an existing original or existing supplemental agreement, upon petition
   filed by either party with the board or in the course of the proceedings under any
   petition pending before such board or referee, if it be proved that such agreement
   was in any material respect incorrect.
